Sweep the arm across the body in a fly arc until it crosses center.
Return to start under control and complete all reps before switching sides.

name: Push-Up
description: A classic bodyweight compound push that trains the chest, shoulders, and triceps requiring no equipment.
instructions: Start in a high plank with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Keep the body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower the chest to just above the floor by bending the elbows.
Push explosively back to the start position and repeat.

name: Incline Push-Up
description: A bodyweight push-up with hands elevated to reduce load and target the lower chest.
instructions: Place hands on an elevated surface like a bench at shoulder-width.
Extend legs back into a plank position.
Lower chest toward the bench by bending elbows.
Push back up to straight arms and repeat.

name: Decline Push-Up
description: A bodyweight push-up with feet elevated on a bench to increase load and shift focus to the upper chest.
instructions: Place feet on a bench and hands on the floor at shoulder-width.
Maintain a straight body line from feet to head.
Lower chest to the floor by bending elbows.
Press back up to full arm extension and repeat.

name: Wide-Grip Push-Up
description: A bodyweight push-up with a wide hand placement to increase chest activation and stretch.
instructions: Start in a plank with hands placed well outside shoulder-width.
Keep the body in a rigid straight line.
Lower chest toward the floor while flaring elbows outward.
Push back up to the starting position and repeat.

name: Archer Push-Up
description: An advanced push-up variation where one arm extends laterally to load a single side of the chest.
instructions: Begin in a wide push-up stance with hands far apart.
Shift weight to one side as you bend that elbow, extending the other arm straight.
Lower toward the working-side hand until chest is near the floor.
Push back to the center and repeat on the other side.

name: Chest Dip
description: A compound bodyweight dip with forward lean to heavily recruit the lower chest and triceps.
instructions: Grip parallel dip bars and support your weight with straight arms.
Lean forward approximately 30 degrees to target the chest.
Lower the body until upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Press back up to full arm extension and repeat.

name: Weighted Chest Dip
description: A chest dip performed with added weight via a belt or vest to progressively overload the lower chest.
instructions: Attach weight via a dip belt and grip the parallel bars.
Lean slightly forward throughout the movement.
Lower under control until upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Press back to full extension and repeat.

name: Machine Chest Press
description: A compound chest press performed on a guided machine for stable loading and beginner-friendly setup.
instructions: Adjust seat height so handles align with mid-chest.
Grip handles with palms facing down or neutral.
Push handles forward until arms are fully extended.
Return under control to the start position and repeat.

name: Incline Machine Chest Press
description: A machine chest press on an incline angle targeting the upper chest with guided stability.
instructions: Adjust the seat so handles align with the upper chest.
Grip handles and keep back flat against the pad.
Push handles upward and forward until arms extend.
Lower slowly to the start and repeat.

name: Decline Machine Chest Press
description: A machine press on a decline angle to isolate and overload the lower chest with guided movement.
instructions: Sit in the decline machine and adjust seat to align handles with lower chest.
Grip handles and brace the back against the pad.
Press handles downward and forward to full extension.
Return slowly to start and repeat.

name: Pec Deck Fly
description: An isolation machine fly that adducts the chest through a fixed arc for peak mid-chest contraction.
instructions: Sit in the pec deck and adjust so arms are at chest height.
Place forearms against the pads and grip the handles.
Squeeze the chest to bring pads together in front of the body.
Slowly return to the start with a full stretch and repeat.

name: Smith Machine Bench Press
description: A compound bench press performed in a Smith machine offering a guided bar path for chest development.
instructions: Position a flat bench under the Smith machine bar and set the height.
Lie back and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Rotate the bar to unrack and lower it to mid-chest.
Press back up to full extension, rotate to re-rack when done.

name: Smith Machine Incline Bench Press
description: An incline chest press in a Smith machine targeting the upper chest with a guided movement path.
instructions: Set an incline bench under the Smith machine bar.
Lie back and grip the bar at upper chest level.
Rotate to unrack, then lower to the upper chest.
Press back to full extension and re-rack after set.

name: Cable Chest Press
description: A compound chest press with cables that provides constant tension through the full pressing range.
instructions: Set cables to chest height and grip both handles from behind.
Stand in a split stance and lean slightly forward.
Press both handles forward until arms are extended.
Return slowly to start and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Press
description: A unilateral dumbbell press that challenges the chest and core stability on one side at a time.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding one dumbbell at chest level.
Keep the non-working arm extended or resting on the thigh.
Press the dumbbell to full arm extension above the chest.
Lower under control and complete reps before switching sides.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
description: A unique chest and lat stretch exercise where a dumbbell is lowered behind the head in a sweeping arc.
instructions: Lie perpendicular on a bench with only shoulders supported, hips dropped.
Hold one dumbbell with both hands above the chest.
Lower the dumbbell behind the head in a wide arc until a stretch is felt.
Pull the dumbbell back over the chest and repeat.

name: Barbell Pullover
description: A pullover variation using a barbell for increased loading across the chest and lats.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench and hold the barbell with a close overhand grip above the chest.
Keep a slight bend in the elbows throughout.
Lower the bar in an arc behind the head until a stretch is felt.
Pull back over the chest and repeat.

name: Cable Pullover
description: A cable pullover providing constant tension through the arc to target the upper chest and serratus.
instructions: Set a cable to the highest position and attach a rope or bar.
Stand facing away and hold attachment with extended arms overhead.
Pull the cable downward in an arc keeping arms straight.
Return slowly above the head and repeat.

name: Ring Push-Up
description: A push-up performed on gymnastic rings that maximally engages chest stabilizers through an unstable surface.
instructions: Set rings just above the floor and grip with palms facing in.
Extend legs into a plank and keep the body rigid.
Lower the chest toward the rings keeping the palms neutral.
Push back up and turn the rings out slightly at the top, squeezing the chest.

name: Svend Press
description: An isolation press where weight plates are pinched together and pressed outward to maximally contract the inner chest.
instructions: Hold two weight plates pinched between your palms at chest level.
Press the plates outward in front of the body to full arm extension.
Squeeze the chest hard to maintain pinch throughout the movement.
Return the plates back to the chest and repeat.

name: Landmine Press
description: A compound press using a landmine-anchored barbell that provides a natural arc ideal for upper chest development.
instructions: Anchor a barbell in a landmine sleeve and stand at the end holding it with both hands.
Position the bar at chest level and stand in a split or parallel stance.
Press the bar forward and upward following the natural arc.
Return to chest level under control and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Landmine Press
description: A unilateral landmine press that builds upper chest strength and anti-rotation core stability.
instructions: Anchor a barbell in a landmine and hold the end with one hand at shoulder height.
Stand in a staggered stance with the opposite foot forward.
Press the bar upward and forward following the arc.
Return to shoulder height and repeat before switching sides.

name: Push-Up Plus
description: A push-up variation that adds a final protraction at the top to activate the serratus anterior and chest.
instructions: Begin in standard push-up position with arms extended.
Lower to the floor in a controlled push-up.
Press back up to full extension.
At the top, push the upper back toward the ceiling to fully protract the shoulder blades.

name: Cable Incline Fly
description: A cable fly performed on an incline bench with low pulleys to train the upper chest with constant tension.
instructions: Position an incline bench between two low cable pulleys.
Grab both cable handles and lie back on the bench.
With a slight elbow bend, arc the arms up and together above the upper chest.
Lower slowly back to full stretch and repeat.

name: Cable Decline Fly
description: A cable fly on a decline bench using high pulleys for constant tension on the lower chest.
instructions: Position a decline bench between two high cable pulleys.
Grab both handles and secure feet on the decline bench.
With a slight elbow bend, arc both arms down and together below the chest.
Return to full stretch overhead and repeat.

name: Floor Press
description: A pressing exercise performed lying on the floor that limits range of motion and reduces shoulder stress.
instructions: Lie on the floor under a barbell in a rack or with a spotter.
Set up as in a bench press and unrack the bar.
Lower until triceps touch the floor and pause briefly.
Press back to full arm extension and repeat.

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
description: A floor-based dumbbell press that limits bottom range for shoulder-friendly chest training.
instructions: Sit on the floor and tip the dumbbells back as you lie down.
Hold dumbbells at chest level with elbows resting on the floor.
Press both dumbbells up to full arm extension.
Lower until elbows touch the floor and repeat.

name: Incline Cable Chest Press
description: A compound incline press using low cables to deliver constant tension while targeting the upper chest.
instructions: Set cables low and position an incline bench between them.
Grab both handles and lie on the incline bench.
Press both handles up and together above the upper chest.
Lower slowly back to chest level and repeat.

name: Bodyweight Chest Fly
description: A bodyweight fly using sliders or plates on the floor to adduct the chest through a wide arc.
instructions: Place sliders or plates under both hands and get into a push-up position.
Slide both hands out wide while lowering the chest toward the floor.
Squeeze the chest to slide hands back together.
Return to plank position and repeat.

name: Resistance Band Chest Fly
description: A band-resisted fly that mimics cable or dumbbell fly mechanics without machines.
instructions: Anchor a resistance band behind you at chest height.
Hold one end in each hand with arms spread wide.
With a slight elbow bend, sweep both arms forward until hands meet.
Slowly return to the start under band tension and repeat.

name: Resistance Band Chest Press
description: A band-resisted horizontal press that trains chest strength anywhere without gym equipment.
instructions: Anchor a resistance band at chest height behind you.
Hold both ends at shoulder level with palms forward.
Press both hands forward until arms are fully extended.
Return slowly to chest level and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Fly
description: A unilateral dumbbell fly that works each side of the chest independently for improved symmetry.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench holding one dumbbell above the chest.
Keep the non-working hand on the hip or abdomen.
Lower the dumbbell out to the side in a wide arc.
Squeeze the chest to return to the top and repeat before switching sides.

name: Medicine Ball Push-Up
description: A push-up with hands on a medicine ball that requires stability and shifts emphasis across the chest.
instructions: Place both hands on a single medicine ball and extend into a plank.
Keep the core tight and body in a straight line.
Lower the chest toward the ball while stabilizing on the curved surface.
Press back up and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Cable Chest Press
description: A unilateral cable press that builds chest strength while demanding core anti-rotation stability.
instructions: Set cable to chest height and stand sideways to the machine.
Grip the handle in the far hand at chest level in a staggered stance.
Press the handle forward until the arm is fully extended.
Return to start under control and complete reps before switching sides.

name: Neutral Grip Dumbbell Press
description: A dumbbell press with palms facing each other that reduces shoulder stress while engaging the chest effectively.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench holding dumbbells above the chest with palms facing each other.
Keep elbows at roughly 45 degrees to the torso.
Lower dumbbells toward the sides of the chest.
Press back up to the start and repeat.

name: Dead Bug
description: A foundational deep-core drill that trains trunk control while the limbs move.
instructions: Lie on your back with your ribs down and low back controlled.
Set your arms and legs in the starting position.
Move the prescribed limb pattern slowly without shifting your torso.
Return under control and repeat.

name: Wall Press Dead Bug
description: A dead bug variation that adds an isometric press into the wall for more trunk tension.
instructions: Lie on your back close enough to press your hands into the wall.
Brace hard and keep your ribs down.
Move the opposite leg pattern while maintaining the wall press.
Return slowly without losing trunk pressure.

name: Band Pulldown Dead Bug
description: A dead bug with overhead band tension that increases anti-extension demand.
instructions: Anchor the band overhead and lie on your back holding it taut.
Pull the band down to set your lats and ribs.
Move through the dead bug pattern without losing position.
Return slowly and keep the band tension steady.

name: Stability Ball Dead Bug
description: A dead bug variation using a ball press to reinforce deep-core tension and cross-body control.
instructions: Lie on your back and press a ball between opposite hand and knee.
Brace and keep your low back controlled.
Extend the free arm and leg slowly away.
Return under control and switch sides.

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Dead Bug
description: A loaded dead bug that adds anti-rotation demand through a single-arm kettlebell hold.
instructions: Lie on your back holding one kettlebell locked out over your shoulder.
Brace and keep the loaded arm steady.
Move the opposite-side dead bug pattern slowly.
Return under control before switching sides.

name: Medicine Ball Dead Bug Pullover
description: A dead bug variation that adds an overhead pullover to challenge trunk position.
instructions: Lie on your back holding the ball above your chest with legs set for a dead bug.
Brace and slowly move the ball overhead as one leg extends.
Keep your ribs down and low back controlled.
Return to the start and alternate sides.

name: Tabletop March
description: A supine bracing drill that teaches deep-core control while alternating the legs.
instructions: Lie on your back with your hips and knees at ninety degrees.
Brace and keep your low back gently controlled.
Lower one foot toward the floor without shifting your trunk.
Bring it back up and alternate sides.

name: Supine Toe Tap
description: A toe-tap variation that trains trunk control while one leg lowers from tabletop.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees over your hips and shins parallel to the floor.
Brace and keep your ribs stacked.
Tap one foot to the floor under control.
Return to tabletop and alternate sides.

name: Bent-Knee Leg Lower
description: A bent-knee leg-lowering drill that builds lower-core control without a long lever.
instructions: Lie on your back with your hips and knees bent to ninety degrees.
Brace and flatten your trunk position gently.
Lower both legs as far as you can without arching.
Bring them back up under control.

name: Single-Leg Leg Lower
description: A single-leg lowering drill that trains deep-core control against a longer lever.
instructions: Lie on your back with both legs raised and your core braced.
Lower one straight leg slowly while the other stays still.
Stop before your trunk position changes.
Return and switch sides.

name: Dead Bug Leg Extension
description: A dead bug variation focused on bilateral lower-body reach while resisting lumbar extension.
instructions: Lie on your back with both hips and knees bent to tabletop.
Brace and keep your ribs down.
Extend both legs out together only as far as you can control.
Bring them back in slowly.

name: Hollow Body Hold
description: A classic anti-extension hold that teaches full-body trunk tension.
instructions: Lie on your back and tuck your ribs down.
Lift your shoulders and legs into a hollow position.
Keep the low back controlled against the floor.
Hold only as long as you can keep clean tension.

name: Tuck Hollow Hold
description: A shortened-lever hollow hold that makes the anti-extension pattern more accessible.
instructions: Lie on your back and pull your knees in toward a tucked hollow position.
Lift your shoulders slightly and keep your ribs down.
Brace hard without letting your low back arch.
Hold the position with smooth breathing.

name: Hollow Body Rock
description: A dynamic hollow variation that trains anti-extension while the body rocks as one unit.
instructions: Set up in a strong hollow body position.
Keep your body rigid from ribs to toes.
Rock forward and back without breaking shape.
Stop if your low back loses contact.

name: Hollow Flutter Kick
description: A hollow-body flutter kick that combines anti-extension with alternating leg action.
instructions: Set up in a hollow body position with your low back controlled.
Lift your shoulders and legs slightly off the floor.
Alternate small controlled kicks from the hips.
Keep the trunk steady through the set.

name: Hollow Scissor Kick
description: A hollow scissor-kick pattern that adds crossing leg motion to the anti-extension demand.
instructions: Set up in a hollow body position with your legs hovering.
Brace hard and keep your ribs down.
Cross the legs over and under in a controlled scissor pattern.
Maintain the same trunk position throughout.

name: Front Plank
description: A foundational anti-extension exercise that trains full-trunk bracing in a straight-body position.
instructions: Set up in a straight-body plank with your ribs stacked over your pelvis.
Brace hard and keep your hips level.
Hold or move through the pattern without losing tension.
Finish before your low back starts to sag.

name: RKC Plank
description: A high-tension plank variation that emphasizes maximal bracing and anti-extension.
instructions: Set up in a forearm plank with your elbows under your shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes, quads, and fists hard.
Pull your elbows and toes toward each other without moving.
Hold only while you can maintain maximal tension.

name: Long Lever Plank
description: A plank with the elbows farther forward that increases anti-extension demand.
instructions: Set up in a straight-body plank with your ribs stacked over your pelvis.
Brace hard and keep your hips level.
Hold or move through the pattern without losing tension.
Finish before your low back starts to sag.

name: Stability Ball Plank
description: A plank performed on a ball to add instability and deeper trunk control demand.
instructions: Set up in a straight-body plank with your ribs stacked over your pelvis.
Brace hard and keep your hips level.
Hold or move through the pattern without losing tension.
Finish before your low back starts to sag.

name: Plank Shoulder Tap
description: A plank variation that adds anti-rotation demand by alternating shoulder taps.
instructions: Set up in a strong high plank.
Brace and keep your hips level.
Lift one hand to tap the opposite shoulder.
Set it down and alternate sides without rocking.

name: Plank Dumbbell Drag
description: A high-plank drag that trains anti-rotation as the weight moves under the body.
instructions: Set up in a high plank with the weight just outside one hand.
Brace hard and keep your hips level.
Reach across to drag the weight under your body.
Set it down and alternate sides.

name: Slider Body Saw
description: A body-saw pattern on sliders that makes anti-extension work more demanding through motion.
instructions: Set up in a forearm plank with your feet on the sliders.
Brace hard and keep your hips level.
Glide your body backward and forward under control.
Stop before your low back starts to arch.

name: Suspension Trainer Body Saw
description: A suspended body saw that increases anti-extension demand through a hanging foot support.
instructions: Set up in a forearm plank with your feet in the straps.
Brace and keep your ribs down.
Saw your body backward and forward under control.
Keep the trunk rigid throughout.

name: Kneeling Ab Wheel Rollout
description: A kneeling rollout that trains deep anti-extension strength through a long reach.
instructions: Set up with your trunk braced and hips slightly tucked.
Roll or reach out slowly as far as you can control.
Keep your ribs down and avoid low-back arching.
Pull back to the start under full control.

name: Standing Ab Wheel Rollout
description: A standing ab-wheel rollout that creates a very high anti-extension demand.
instructions: Set up with your trunk braced and hips slightly tucked.
Roll or reach out slowly as far as you can control.
Keep your ribs down and avoid low-back arching.
Pull back to the start under full control.

name: Barbell Rollout
description: A rollout performed with a loaded barbell for anti-extension trunk strength.
instructions: Set up with your trunk braced and hips slightly tucked.
Roll or reach out slowly as far as you can control.
Keep your ribs down and avoid low-back arching.
Pull back to the start under full control.

name: Stability Ball Rollout
description: A ball rollout that provides a more accessible anti-extension option than a wheel rollout.
instructions: Set up with your trunk braced and hips slightly tucked.
Roll or reach out slowly as far as you can control.
Keep your ribs down and avoid low-back arching.
Pull back to the start under full control.

name: Slider Rollout
description: A rollout using sliders that challenges trunk control with a smooth low-friction reach.
instructions: Set up with your trunk braced and hips slightly tucked.
Roll or reach out slowly as far as you can control.
Keep your ribs down and avoid low-back arching.
Pull back to the start under full control.

name: Suspension Trainer Fallout
description: A suspended fallout that trains anti-extension while the hands move away from the body.
instructions: Stand facing the straps and hold the handles in front of your chest.
Brace and keep your ribs down.
Let your arms travel forward as your body leans out in one line.
Pull back to the start without arching.

name: Ring Fallout
description: A ring fallout that increases instability while training anti-extension through a forward lean.
instructions: Stand facing the rings and hold them close together.
Brace hard and lean out as your arms move forward.
Keep your body in one line without flaring your ribs.
Pull yourself back to the start under control.

name: Stability Ball Stir the Pot
description: A ball-plank variation that combines anti-extension with controlled small circles.
instructions: Set up in a forearm plank on the stability ball.
Brace and keep your hips level.
Draw small circles with your forearms on the ball.
Keep the trunk still as the arms move.

name: Walkout to Plank
description: A walkout to plank that trains trunk control while lengthening the body lever.
instructions: Stand tall and hinge to place your hands on the floor.
Walk your hands forward until you reach a strong plank.
Hold the trunk steady as you walk back in.
Stand up and repeat smoothly.

name: Dragon Flag
description: An advanced anti-extension movement that keeps the body rigid while lowering from the shoulders.
instructions: Lie on a bench and grip the support behind your head.
Lift your body into a straight rigid line from shoulders to feet.
Lower slowly without bending at the hips.
Raise back up under full control.

name: Turkish Get-Up
description: A full-body stability exercise that challenges anti-rotation and shoulder control through multiple positions.
instructions: Lie on your back with one kettlebell locked out over your shoulder.
Roll to your elbow and hand while keeping your eyes on the weight.
Bridge and thread the leg through into a half-kneeling position.
Stand up under control and reverse the steps to return.

name: Bird Dog
description: A classic quadruped stability drill that trains anti-rotation through opposite arm and leg reach.
instructions: Set up on hands and knees with your spine neutral.
Brace your trunk before moving.
Reach through the prescribed arm and leg pattern without twisting.
Return slowly and repeat on the next side.

name: Banded Bird Dog
description: A bird dog with band resistance that increases the challenge to trunk and hip control.
instructions: Set up on hands and knees with your spine neutral.
Brace your trunk before moving.
Reach through the prescribed arm and leg pattern without twisting.
Return slowly and repeat on the next side.

name: Quadruped Hover
description: A hovering quadruped hold that trains deep-core bracing with the knees just off the floor.
instructions: Set up on hands and knees with your toes tucked.
Brace hard and lift your knees just off the floor.
Keep your spine neutral and hips level.
Hold only while you can stay steady.

name: Half Turkish Get-Up
description: A partial get-up that builds anti-rotation and shoulder stability without standing all the way up.
instructions: Lie on your back with one arm locked out holding the weight.
Roll to your elbow and then your hand while keeping the load stable.
Bridge and sweep the leg through to half kneeling if prescribed.
Reverse the pattern slowly back to the floor.

name: Bear Plank
description: A bent-knee plank that challenges bracing and trunk position with the knees hovering.
instructions: Set up in a bear position with your knees hovering under your hips.
Brace hard and keep your back flat.
Hold the position without letting the hips drift.
Reset before your posture breaks.

name: Bear Plank Shoulder Tap
description: A bear-plank progression that adds alternating shoulder taps for anti-rotation work.
instructions: Set up in a bear plank with your knees hovering low.
Brace hard and keep your hips quiet.
Lift one hand to tap the opposite shoulder.
Alternate sides without rocking.

name: Bear Crawl
description: A crawling pattern that trains deep-core stability while the limbs move reciprocally.
instructions: Set up in a bear position with your knees hovering.
Brace and move opposite hand and foot forward together.
Keep your hips low and trunk steady as you crawl.
Continue with small controlled steps.

name: Reverse Bear Crawl
description: A backward bear crawl that changes the coordination and bracing demand of the crawl pattern.
instructions: Set up in a bear position with your knees hovering.
Brace and move opposite hand and foot backward together.
Keep your hips level and steps controlled.
Continue backward without twisting.

name: Lateral Bear Crawl
description: A side-to-side bear crawl that adds frontal-plane control to the crawling pattern.
instructions: Set up in a bear position with your knees hovering.
Brace and step hand and foot to the side in sequence.
Keep your hips low and trunk square.
Continue laterally under control.

name: Bear Plank Dumbbell Drag
description: A bear-plank drag that adds anti-rotation while the weight moves under the body.
instructions: Set up in a bear plank with the weight just outside one hand.
Brace hard and keep the knees hovering low.
Reach across to drag the weight under your body.
Alternate sides without rocking.

name: High Plank Bird Dog
description: A high-plank reach that combines anti-extension and anti-rotation in a long-lever position.
instructions: Set up in a strong high plank.
Brace your trunk and keep the hips level.
Reach one arm and the opposite leg away from the floor.
Return under control and alternate sides.

name: Side Plank
description: A foundational anti-lateral-flexion drill that builds deep side-core stability.
instructions: Set up on one forearm with your body in a straight line.
Brace and keep your hips lifted.
Hold the position without rotating forward or back.
Switch sides after the set.

name: Side Plank Reach-Through
description: A side plank variation that adds controlled torso rotation and return.
instructions: Set up in a side plank with your top arm reaching up.
Brace and keep your hips lifted.
Rotate and reach the top arm under your torso.
Return to the open position under control.

name: Side Plank Row
description: A side plank with a rowing pattern that increases anti-rotation and shoulder-control demand.
instructions: Set up in a side plank facing the cable or band.
Brace and keep your hips lifted.
Row the handle without rotating your torso.
Return slowly before the next rep.

name: Side Plank with Top-Leg Raise
description: A side plank progression that adds hip abduction while the trunk stays stable.
instructions: Set up in a strong side plank.
Brace and keep your hips stacked.
Raise the top leg without letting the torso move.
Lower it under control and continue.

name: Side Plank Hip Dip
description: A dynamic side-plank variation that trains side-core control through a small range.
instructions: Set up in a side plank with your body in a straight line.
Lower your hip slightly toward the floor.
Drive it back up without twisting.
Repeat with controlled reps.

name: Bench Copenhagen Plank
description: A shorter-lever Copenhagen variation that is more accessible than the full version.
instructions: Set your top knee on the bench and support yourself on your forearm.
Brace and lift your hips into line.
Hold the position without twisting.
Switch sides after the set.

name: Star Side Plank
description: A side plank progression that adds a lifted top arm and leg for greater stability demand.
instructions: Set up in a strong side plank.
Brace and lift the top arm and top leg.
Hold the star position without rotating.
Lower with control and switch sides.

name: Kettlebell Arm Bar
description: A loaded shoulder-stability drill that trains trunk control while the body rotates around a fixed arm.
instructions: Lie on your back with one kettlebell locked out over your shoulder.
Brace and roll onto your side without losing the vertical arm.
Keep the shoulder packed as you settle into the position.
Return carefully and switch sides.

name: Kettlebell Windmill
description: A standing stability exercise that trains anti-rotation and shoulder control through a hip hinge.
instructions: Stand with one kettlebell locked out overhead and your feet set wide.
Brace and hinge at the hips while keeping your eyes on the weight.
Lower your free hand down your leg without twisting the torso.
Drive back up under control.

name: Standing Pallof Press
description: A classic anti-rotation press that trains the trunk to resist cable or band pull.
instructions: Set the band or cable at chest height and take a stable stance.
Hold the handle at your chest and brace your trunk.
Press or hold without letting the torso rotate.
Return slowly and reset before the next rep.

name: Half-Kneeling Kettlebell Halo
description: A halo variation that trains trunk stability while the kettlebell moves around the head.
instructions: Set up in a half-kneeling stance with the kettlebell held at chest height.
Brace your trunk and keep your ribs stacked over your pelvis.
Circle the bell slowly around your head without leaning or twisting.
Reverse the direction and repeat.

name: Tall-Kneeling Kettlebell Halo
description: A tall-kneeling halo that emphasizes rib-pelvis control while the load circles the head.
instructions: Kneel tall with your glutes squeezed and the kettlebell in front of your chest.
Brace hard and keep your torso stacked.
Move the bell around your head in a slow controlled halo.
Switch directions without losing position.

name: Split-Stance Pallof Press
description: A split-stance Pallof press that adds lower-body stance control to anti-rotation work.
instructions: Set the band or cable at chest height and take a stable stance.
Hold the handle at your chest and brace your trunk.
Press or hold without letting the torso rotate.
Return slowly and reset before the next rep.

name: Stability Ball Pike
description: A ball-supported pike that challenges anti-extension and midline control as the hips lift.
instructions: Set up in a high plank with your shins or feet on the stability ball.
Brace hard and keep your shoulders strong.
Lift your hips into a pike by pulling the ball toward your hands.
Lower back to plank under control.

name: Standing Pallof Hold
description: A static Pallof hold that trains the trunk to resist rotation over time.
instructions: Set the handle at chest height and take a stable stance.
Press the handle straight out from your chest.
Hold without letting your torso rotate.
Bring it back in under control.

name: Suspension Trainer Pike
description: A suspended pike that increases anti-extension demand while the feet move in the straps.
instructions: Set up in a strong plank with your feet in the straps.
Brace hard and keep the shoulders stacked.
Lift your hips up into a pike without letting the low back sag.
Lower slowly back to plank.

name: Pallof Walkout
description: A Pallof progression that adds stepping away from the anchor while resisting rotation.
instructions: Hold the band at your chest and brace your trunk.
Press it out and take small steps away from the anchor.
Keep your torso square as tension increases.
Walk back in under control.

name: Waiter March
description: A single-arm overhead march that trains anti-lateral-flexion and trunk control while walking in place.
instructions: Stand tall with one weight locked out overhead.
Brace hard and keep your ribs stacked.
March in place without leaning or rotating.
Lower the load carefully and switch sides.

name: Pallof Press March
description: A Pallof variation that adds marching to challenge anti-rotation and balance together.
instructions: Press the band or cable out from your chest.
Brace hard and keep the torso square.
March one knee up at a time without rotating.
Return the handle to your chest under control.

name: Standing Single-Arm Cable Press
description: A unilateral cable press that trains the core to resist rotation while pressing.
instructions: Set your stance and brace your trunk before pressing.
Keep the ribs down and pelvis stacked.
Press the load smoothly without letting your torso rotate.
Return under control and repeat.

name: Bottoms-Up March
description: A bottoms-up carry in place that increases anti-rotation demand with a highly unstable load.
instructions: Rack a kettlebell bottoms-up and stand tall.
Brace hard and keep the bell vertical.
March in place slowly without letting your torso sway.
Set the bell down under control and switch sides.

name: Zercher March
description: A front-loaded march that challenges deep-core stiffness and anti-extension under load.
instructions: Hold the bar in the crooks of your elbows and stand tall.
Brace hard and keep your ribs stacked.
March one knee up at a time without leaning back.
Set the load down carefully when the set ends.

name: Sandbag Shoulder Carry
description: A unilateral shoulder-loaded carry that builds anti-lateral-flexion and anti-rotation strength while walking.
instructions: Load the sandbag onto one shoulder and stand tall.
Brace hard and keep your torso square.
Walk under control without leaning or rotating.
Switch shoulders after the set.

name: Half-Kneeling Landmine Press
description: A half-kneeling landmine press that trains trunk stiffness while the load moves on an arc.
instructions: Set your stance and brace your trunk before pressing.
Keep the ribs down and pelvis stacked.
Press the load smoothly without letting your torso rotate.
Return under control and repeat.

name: Offset Front Rack Carry
description: A mismatched front-rack carry that increases anti-rotation and anti-extension demand while walking.
instructions: Rack two uneven loads at the shoulders and stand tall.
Brace hard and keep your ribs stacked.
Walk under control without letting the torso twist.
Set the weights down carefully when the set ends.

name: Farmer Carry
description: A bilateral carry that builds full-body bracing and deep-core stiffness under load.
instructions: Pick the load up and stand tall with your ribs stacked.
Brace hard and keep your shoulders organized.
Walk under control without leaning or rotating.
Set the load down carefully when the set ends.

name: Offset Farmer Carry
description: A carry using mismatched loads that increases anti-lateral-flexion and anti-rotation demand.
instructions: Pick the load up and stand tall with your ribs stacked.
Brace hard and keep your shoulders organized.
Walk under control without leaning or rotating.
Set the load down carefully when the set ends.

name: Front Rack Carry
description: A single-arm front-rack carry that challenges bracing and rib-pelvis control while walking.
instructions: Pick the load up and stand tall with your ribs stacked.
Brace hard and keep your shoulders organized.
Walk under control without leaning or rotating.
Set the load down carefully when the set ends.

name: Double Front Rack Carry
description: A bilateral front-rack carry that trains deep-core stiffness against front-loaded weight.
instructions: Pick the load up and stand tall with your ribs stacked.
Brace hard and keep your shoulders organized.
Walk under control without leaning or rotating.
Set the load down carefully when the set ends.

name: Overhead Carry
description: A bilateral overhead carry that demands trunk control while the load stays overhead.
instructions: Pick the load up and stand tall with your ribs stacked.
Brace hard and keep your shoulders organized.
Walk under control without leaning or rotating.
Set the load down carefully when the set ends.

name: Bottoms-Up Carry
description: A bottoms-up kettlebell carry that adds grip and shoulder stability to the core challenge.
instructions: Pick the load up and stand tall with your ribs stacked.
Brace hard and keep your shoulders organized.
Walk under control without leaning or rotating.
Set the load down carefully when the set ends.

name: Sandbag Bear Hug Carry
description: A front-loaded sandbag carry that heavily challenges bracing and breathing under load.
instructions: Pick the load up and stand tall with your ribs stacked.
Brace hard and keep your shoulders organized.
Walk under control without leaning or rotating.
Set the load down carefully when the set ends.

name: Zercher Carry
description: A carry performed in the elbow crease that demands strong trunk stiffness under front load.
instructions: Pick the load up and stand tall with your ribs stacked.
Brace hard and keep your shoulders organized.
Walk under control without leaning or rotating.
Set the load down carefully when the set ends.

name: Sandbag Front Carry
description: A sandbag front carry that challenges posture and deep-core control with an unstable front load.
instructions: Pick the load up and stand tall with your ribs stacked.
Brace hard and keep your shoulders organized.
Walk under control without leaning or rotating.
Set the load down carefully when the set ends.

name: Suitcase Hold
description: A static one-arm hold that trains deep-core resistance to side bending.
instructions: Pick the load up and reach a strong stable position.
Brace your trunk and keep your posture stacked.
Hold without leaning, shrugging, or twisting.
Set the load down under control when the hold is over.

name: Front Rack Hold
description: A front-rack hold that trains bracing and rib positioning against front-loaded resistance.
instructions: Pick the load up and reach a strong stable position.
Brace your trunk and keep your posture stacked.
Hold without leaning, shrugging, or twisting.
Set the load down under control when the hold is over.

name: Overhead Hold
description: A static overhead hold that challenges trunk stiffness under an arms-up load.
instructions: Pick the load up and reach a strong stable position.
Brace your trunk and keep your posture stacked.
Hold without leaning, shrugging, or twisting.
Set the load down under control when the hold is over.

name: Bottoms-Up Hold
description: A static bottoms-up kettlebell hold that combines deep-core bracing with upper-limb stability.
instructions: Pick the load up and reach a strong stable position.
Brace your trunk and keep your posture stacked.
Hold without leaning, shrugging, or twisting.
Set the load down under control when the hold is over.

name: Trap Bar Hold
description: A heavy trap-bar hold that challenges full-body bracing without the walking element of a carry.
instructions: Pick the load up and reach a strong stable position.
Brace your trunk and keep your posture stacked.
Hold without leaning, shrugging, or twisting.
Set the load down under control when the hold is over.

name: Sandbag Bear Hug Hold
description: A front-loaded hold that trains breathing and deep-core stiffness against an unstable implement.
instructions: Pick the load up and reach a strong stable position.
Brace your trunk and keep your posture stacked.
Hold without leaning, shrugging, or twisting.
Set the load down under control when the hold is over.

name: Suitcase March
description: A one-arm marching drill that adds single-leg anti-lateral-flexion demand to the suitcase position.
instructions: Pick the load up on one side and stand tall.
Brace hard without leaning away from the weight.
March one knee up at a time under control.
Set the weight down carefully after the set.

name: Front Rack March
description: A front-rack marching drill that adds balance and trunk-control demand to the rack position.
instructions: Set one load in the front-rack position and stand tall.
Brace your trunk and keep your ribs stacked.
March one knee up at a time without twisting.
Set the load down under control after the set.

name: Overhead March
description: An overhead marching drill that combines single-leg control with arms-up trunk stability.
instructions: Press the load overhead and stand tall.
Brace hard and keep your ribs down.
March one knee up at a time without arching your back.
Lower the load under control when the set ends.

name: 90/90 Breathing
description: A foundational breathing drill that teaches rib and pelvis control for deep-core activation.
instructions: Lie on your back with your hips and knees bent to ninety degrees.
Settle your ribs down and relax your neck.
Inhale through your nose and exhale fully through your mouth.
Repeat with slow controlled breaths.

name: Wall 90/90 Breathing
description: A wall-supported breathing drill that adds hamstring tension to help position the pelvis.
instructions: Lie on your back with your feet flat on the wall and knees bent to ninety degrees.
Press lightly into the wall to feel your hamstrings.
Inhale through your nose and exhale fully while keeping your ribs down.
Repeat for smooth controlled breaths.

name: Crocodile Breathing
description: A prone breathing drill that teaches diaphragmatic expansion without compensating through the neck.
instructions: Lie face down with your forehead resting on your hands.
Relax your shoulders and jaw.
Breathe in through your nose and feel your torso expand into the floor.
Exhale slowly and repeat.

name: Supine Diaphragmatic Breathing
description: A simple supine breathing drill that builds awareness of diaphragmatic trunk control.
instructions: Set up in the prescribed position and relax your neck and shoulders.
Take a slow breath in through your nose.
Exhale fully while keeping your ribcage and pelvis controlled.
Repeat for smooth controlled breaths.

name: Bear Position Breathing
description: A breathing drill in the bear position that trains deep-core control under light load.
instructions: Set up in a bear position with your knees hovering slightly.
Brace gently and keep your back flat.
Take slow breaths without losing your trunk position.
Reset before your posture breaks down.

name: Floor Crunch
description: A basic floor crunch that trains spinal flexion through a short controlled range.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet set.
Brace lightly and keep the low back controlled.
Curl your ribs toward your pelvis.
Lower slowly without dropping out of tension.

name: Stability Ball Crunch
description: A ball-supported crunch that increases range by extending over the ball.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet set.
Brace lightly and keep the low back controlled.
Curl your ribs toward your pelvis.
Lower slowly without dropping out of tension.

name: Decline Bench Crunch
description: A decline crunch that makes bodyweight flexion more challenging with a steeper torso angle.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet set.
Brace lightly and keep the low back controlled.
Curl your ribs toward your pelvis.
Lower slowly without dropping out of tension.

name: Weighted Floor Crunch
description: A loaded floor crunch that adds resistance to the standard crunch pattern.
instructions: Lie on your back and hold the load against your chest.
Keep your feet planted and brace lightly.
Curl your ribs toward your pelvis under control.
Lower slowly without letting the weight pull you down.

name: Medicine Ball Crunch
description: A medicine-ball crunch that adds front-loaded resistance to upper-ab flexion.
instructions: Lie on your back and hold the load against your chest.
Keep your feet planted and brace lightly.
Curl your ribs toward your pelvis under control.
Lower slowly without letting the weight pull you down.

name: Kneeling Cable Crunch
description: A kneeling cable crunch that loads torso flexion with steady cable resistance.
instructions: Kneel facing the cable with the rope set high.
Brace and keep your hips mostly fixed.
Crunch your ribs down toward your pelvis.
Return slowly without letting the stack slam.

name: Ab Crunch Machine
description: A machine crunch that guides torso flexion through a fixed path.
instructions: Adjust the machine so your body lines up with the pads and pivot.
Brace your trunk and take the handles or pads securely.
Crunch through the torso until you reach the end range.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Toe Touch Crunch
description: A straight-leg crunch variation that reaches toward the feet to emphasize upper-ab flexion.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs up toward the ceiling.
Brace and keep the legs steady.
Crunch up and reach toward your toes.
Lower slowly without losing control.

name: Weighted Toe Touch Crunch
description: A loaded toe-touch crunch that adds resistance to the straight-leg upper-ab reach pattern.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs straight up and the weight over your chest.
Brace your trunk and keep the legs steady.
Crunch up and reach the load toward your toes.
Lower slowly without losing tension.

name: Hanging L-Sit
description: A hanging L-sit that trains the abs isometrically by holding the legs straight out in front.
instructions: Hang from the bar with your shoulders set and body steady.
Raise your straight legs until they are about parallel to the floor.
Hold the position with your ribs down and knees locked.
Lower under control when the hold is complete.

name: Sit-Up
description: A classic sit-up that uses a longer torso range than a standard crunch.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet set as needed.
Brace your midline and start by curling the torso up.
Sit up until you reach the top position.
Lower back down under control.

name: Butterfly Sit-Up
description: A sit-up done with the soles of the feet together for a common bodyweight core setup.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet set as needed.
Brace your midline and start by curling the torso up.
Sit up until you reach the top position.
Lower back down under control.

name: Anchored Sit-Up
description: A sit-up performed with the feet anchored to improve leverage and control.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet set as needed.
Brace your midline and start by curling the torso up.
Sit up until you reach the top position.
Lower back down under control.

name: Weighted Sit-Up
description: A loaded sit-up that adds external resistance to the full-range torso rise.
instructions: Lie on your back holding the load close to your torso.
Brace your midline and curl up into the sit-up.
Reach the top position without jerking the weight.
Lower back down under control.

name: Decline Sit-Up
description: A decline sit-up that increases difficulty by starting from a deeper torso angle.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet set as needed.
Brace your midline and start by curling the torso up.
Sit up until you reach the top position.
Lower back down under control.

name: AbMat Sit-Up
description: A sit-up using an AbMat to increase extension and range through the rep.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet set as needed.
Brace your midline and start by curling the torso up.
Sit up until you reach the top position.
Lower back down under control.

name: GHD Sit-Up
description: A GHD sit-up that greatly increases range and loading on the midline.
instructions: Set your feet and hips securely in the GHD.
Lower your torso under control into the stretched position.
Brace and sit all the way back up.
Repeat without overextending the low back.

name: Medicine Ball Sit-Up
description: A loaded sit-up using a medicine ball to add resistance through the full torso rise.
instructions: Lie on your back holding the medicine ball close to your chest.
Brace your midline and begin curling the torso up.
Sit up tall without throwing the load forward.
Lower back down slowly under control.

name: V-Up
description: A V-up that raises the torso and legs together for full anterior-core tension.
instructions: Lie flat with your arms and legs extended.
Brace your core and lift your torso and legs together.
Reach toward your feet at the top.
Lower both ends slowly to the start.

name: Weighted V-Up
description: A loaded V-up that adds external resistance to the combined torso-and-leg raise.
instructions: Lie flat holding the weight overhead or at your chest.
Brace and raise your torso and legs together.
Reach the load toward your feet at the top.
Lower slowly back to the floor.

name: Bench V-Up
description: A bench-supported V-up that lets the legs lower below the bench for extra range and tension.
instructions: Lie lengthwise on a bench with your body balanced and legs extended.
Brace your core and raise your torso and legs together.
Meet in the middle without swinging off the bench.
Lower both ends slowly back to the start.

name: Alternating V-Up
description: A V-up variation that alternates sides to combine anterior-core work with some rotational demand.
instructions: Lie flat with your arms and legs extended.
Raise one arm and the opposite leg toward each other.
Lower under control and switch sides.
Continue alternating without rushing.

name: Jackknife Sit-Up
description: A jackknife sit-up that blends a sit-up and leg raise into one coordinated rep.
instructions: Lie flat with your arms and legs extended.
Brace your core and lift your torso and legs together.
Reach toward your feet at the top.
Lower both ends slowly to the start.

name: Tuck-Up
description: A tuck-up that shortens the lever by bending the knees while the torso flexes up.
instructions: Lie back with your legs extended and hands set by your sides.
Brace and pull your knees in as your torso curls up.
Meet in the middle without swinging.
Extend back out under control.

name: Seated Knee Tuck
description: A seated tuck that trains the abs by bringing the knees toward the chest from a supported position.
instructions: Set up with your hands lightly supporting you and your legs extended.
Lean back slightly and brace your trunk.
Pull your knees in toward your chest.
Extend back out under control.

name: Decline Bench Knee Raise
description: A decline bench knee raise that increases lower-ab difficulty with a steeper body angle.
instructions: Set yourself securely on the decline bench and hold the top support.
Brace your trunk and bend your knees toward your chest.
Pause when your abs finish the rep without swinging.
Lower slowly until your legs extend again.

name: Slider Knee Tuck
description: A slider knee tuck that uses a plank position to load the abs while the knees pull under.
instructions: Set up in a plank with your feet on the sliders.
Brace hard and keep your shoulders stacked.
Slide your knees toward your chest.
Extend back out under control.

name: Stability Ball Knee Tuck
description: A stability-ball knee tuck that adds instability to the lower-ab tuck pattern.
instructions: Set up in a plank with your shins on the ball.
Brace and keep your shoulders stable.
Pull your knees in toward your chest.
Roll back out under control.

name: Suspension Trainer Knee Tuck
description: A suspended knee tuck that challenges the abs and shoulder stability at the same time.
instructions: Set up in a plank with your feet in the straps.
Brace your trunk and keep the shoulders stacked.
Pull your knees toward your chest.
Extend back out without letting your back sag.

name: Reverse Crunch
description: A reverse crunch that trains lower-ab pelvic curl without a long lever leg raise.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet off the floor.
Brace and curl your pelvis up toward your ribs.
Lift only as high as you can without swinging.
Lower slowly back to the start.

name: Decline Reverse Crunch
description: A decline reverse crunch that increases the challenge by changing the body angle.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet off the floor.
Brace and curl your pelvis up toward your ribs.
Lift only as high as you can without swinging.
Lower slowly back to the start.

name: Bench Reverse Crunch
description: A bench reverse crunch that gives the arms support while the pelvis curls up.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet off the floor.
Brace and curl your pelvis up toward your ribs.
Lift only as high as you can without swinging.
Lower slowly back to the start.

name: Garhammer Raise
description: A Garhammer raise that emphasizes the pelvic-curl portion of the lower-ab raise pattern.
instructions: Lie back with your hips and knees bent.
Brace and drive your knees upward by curling the pelvis.
Lift only as high as your abs can control.
Lower slowly to the starting position.

name: Lying Knee Raise
description: A lying knee raise that shortens the leg lever while training lower-ab control.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended.
Brace and bend your knees as you raise them toward your torso.
Stop when your abs finish the rep.
Lower slowly back to the floor.

name: Lying Leg Raise
description: A straight-leg raise that increases lower-ab demand with a long lever.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs straight and hands set for support.
Brace your trunk and keep the low back controlled.
Raise your legs until your hips or abs finish the rep.
Lower slowly without letting the legs drop.

name: Ankle-Weighted Leg Raise
description: A leg raise with ankle weights that adds resistance to the standard lower-ab pattern.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs straight and hands set for support.
Brace your trunk and keep the low back controlled.
Raise your legs until your hips or abs finish the rep.
Lower slowly without letting the legs drop.

name: Hip Raise
description: A hip raise that emphasizes the top-range pelvic curl after the legs come up.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs raised.
Brace and curl your hips up off the floor.
Lift only as high as you can stay controlled.
Lower slowly back to the start.

name: Leg Lower
description: A leg lower that trains lower-ab control by resisting the pull of the long lever downward.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs up and your low back controlled.
Brace hard before the lowering phase starts.
Lower your legs only as far as you can stay flat.
Bring them back up under control.

name: Alternating Leg Lower
description: An alternating leg-lower pattern that adds unilateral control to the lower-ab challenge.
instructions: Lie on your back with both legs raised and your trunk braced.
Lower one leg slowly while the other stays up.
Bring it back up under control.
Switch sides and continue alternating.

name: Flutter Kick
description: A flutter-kick drill that trains the lower abs by holding the legs off the floor while alternating.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended and your core braced.
Lift the legs slightly off the floor.
Alternate the legs in small controlled kicks.
Keep the low back steady through the set.

name: Scissor Kick
description: A scissor-kick drill that alternates the legs through a crossing pattern for lower-ab endurance.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs lifted slightly off the floor.
Brace your trunk and keep the low back controlled.
Alternate the legs by crossing them over and under each other.
Continue smoothly without letting the legs drop.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
description: A hanging knee raise that trains the lower abs while the hands support bodyweight.
instructions: Hang from the bar with your grip and shoulders set.
Brace your trunk to limit swinging.
Raise your knees or legs to the target height.
Lower slowly to a dead stop before the next rep.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
description: A straight-leg hanging raise that increases difficulty with a longer lever.
instructions: Hang from the bar with your grip and shoulders set.
Brace your trunk to limit swinging.
Raise your knees or legs to the target height.
Lower slowly to a dead stop before the next rep.

name: Toes-to-Bar
description: A hanging raise that takes the feet to the bar for a high-skill lower-ab movement.
instructions: Hang from the bar with your grip and shoulders set.
Brace hard and start the raise without swinging.
Lift your feet all the way to the bar.
Lower under control to a dead stop.

name: Captain's Chair Knee Raise
description: A supported knee raise that reduces grip demand while training the lower abs.
instructions: Set your forearms and back firmly into the support.
Brace and pull your knees toward your chest.
Stop when your abs finish the rep.
Lower slowly without swinging.

name: Captain's Chair Leg Raise
description: A straight-leg version of the captain's-chair raise for a harder lower-ab challenge.
instructions: Set yourself firmly into the support pads.
Brace and raise your straight legs upward.
Stop at the top without swinging.
Lower slowly back to the start.

name: Decline Bench Leg Raise
description: A decline bench leg raise that makes the straight-leg lower-ab pattern more challenging.
instructions: Set yourself securely on the decline bench and hold the top support.
Brace your trunk and raise your straight legs under control.
Stop when your abs finish the rep without swinging.
Lower slowly back to the start.

name: Hanging Oblique Knee Raise
description: A hanging raise that drives the knees up toward one side to target the obliques.
instructions: Hang from the bar with your body steady.
Raise your knees toward one side of your torso.
Squeeze through the obliques at the top.
Lower slowly and switch sides.

name: Bicycle Crunch
description: A cross-body crunch that combines flexion and rotation through alternating reps.
instructions: Lie on your back with your hands light at your head and legs lifted.
Crunch up and rotate one elbow toward the opposite knee.
Extend the other leg as you switch sides.
Keep alternating with control.

name: Heel Touch
description: A floor oblique exercise that reaches side to side through controlled torso flexion.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet planted.
Lift your shoulders slightly off the floor.
Reach one hand toward the same-side heel.
Switch sides and keep alternating smoothly.

name: Side Crunch
description: A side-lying crunch that shortens one side of the torso to target the obliques.
instructions: Set up in the starting position with your torso angled for the side you are training.
Brace lightly and keep your hips stable.
Crunch through the side of your torso.
Lower slowly back to the start.

name: Side Sit-Up
description: A side sit-up that moves through a larger oblique range than a side crunch.
instructions: Set up in the starting position with your torso angled for the side you are training.
Brace lightly and keep your hips stable.
Crunch through the side of your torso.
Lower slowly back to the start.

name: Side Jackknife
description: A side jackknife that brings the torso and legs together to train the obliques dynamically.
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs extended and top arm set for balance.
Brace and raise your legs as your torso bends toward them.
Meet in the middle without swinging.
Lower slowly before repeating.

name: Side V-Up
description: A side V-up that uses a longer lever than a side jackknife for a harder oblique challenge.
instructions: Lie on your side with your body long and stacked.
Raise your straight legs and torso together.
Reach toward your feet at the top.
Lower slowly under control.

name: Oblique V-Up
description: A rotational V-up that combines anterior-core lifting with an oblique reach.
instructions: Lie flat with your arms and legs extended.
Raise one hand toward the opposite foot.
Lower under control back to the floor.
Alternate sides without rushing.

name: Lying Windshield Wiper
description: A lying leg rotation drill that challenges the obliques while the legs stay elevated.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs raised and trunk braced.
Rotate your legs to one side under control.
Bring them back through center.
Repeat to the other side without letting your shoulders lift.

name: Bent-Knee Windshield Wiper
description: A bent-knee windshield wiper that shortens the lever for a more accessible rotational pattern.
instructions: Lie on your back with your hips and knees bent to ninety degrees.
Brace your trunk and rotate your knees to one side.
Bring them back through center under control.
Repeat to the other side.

name: Hanging Windshield Wiper
description: A hanging rotational leg raise that heavily challenges the obliques and grip.
instructions: Hang from the bar with your shoulders set and trunk braced.
Raise your legs and rotate them to one side.
Sweep back through center under control.
Repeat to the other side without using momentum.

name: Russian Twist
description: A seated rotational exercise that trains the obliques through repeated torso turns.
instructions: Sit tall with your feet set as needed and your torso leaned back slightly.
Brace your trunk and keep the chest up.
Rotate to one side under control.
Rotate to the other side and keep alternating.

name: Weighted Russian Twist
description: A loaded Russian twist that adds resistance to seated rotational work.
instructions: Set up tall with the weight or handle in front of your torso.
Brace your trunk and keep the hips mostly still.
Rotate through the ribs and torso under control.
Return slowly to center before repeating.

name: Cable Reverse Crunch
description: A cable reverse crunch that adds constant resistance to the pelvic-curl lower-ab pattern.
instructions: Attach the cable low and lie down with the strap secured to your ankles.
Brace your trunk and draw your knees in toward your chest.
Curl your pelvis up at the top without swinging.
Lower slowly until the cable stays under control.

name: Medicine Ball Oblique Slam
description: A diagonal medicine-ball slam that trains the obliques through explosive rotation and flexion.
instructions: Stand tall holding the ball near one shoulder.
Brace and rotate sharply as you drive the ball down across your body.
Catch or retrieve it while staying balanced.
Repeat for reps and then switch sides.

name: Seated Cable Twist
description: A seated cable twist that keeps the obliques loaded through both directions of rotation.
instructions: Set up tall with the weight or handle in front of your torso.
Brace your trunk and keep the hips mostly still.
Rotate through the ribs and torso under control.
Return slowly to center before repeating.

name: Cable Torso Rotation
description: A standing cable rotation that trains the obliques against steady horizontal resistance.
instructions: Set the implement at the working height and take a stable stance.
Brace your trunk and start with your hands at the loaded side.
Rotate and pull the handle across your body.
Return slowly without letting the hips spin out.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
description: An ab-wheel rollout that challenges the abs by resisting spinal extension through a long range.
instructions: Kneel with the wheel under your shoulders and brace your trunk hard.
Roll forward while keeping your hips and ribs controlled.
Go only as far as you can avoid low-back sagging.
Pull back to the start under control.

name: Standing Band Rotation
description: A band rotation that gives a simple elastic-resistance option for oblique work.
instructions: Set the implement at the working height and take a stable stance.
Brace your trunk and start with your hands at the loaded side.
Rotate and pull the handle across your body.
Return slowly without letting the hips spin out.

name: Landmine Rotation
description: A landmine rotation that uses the bar path to load the obliques through standing turns.
instructions: Hold the end of the bar with both hands and stand tall.
Brace your trunk and guide the bar to one side.
Rotate through the torso under control.
Bring the bar back and continue to the other side.

name: Landmine 180
description: A sweeping landmine rotation that moves through a larger side-to-side range than a standard landmine twist.
instructions: Hold the end of the bar in front of your chest.
Rotate and guide it down toward one hip.
Drive it back through the middle to the other side.
Keep the movement smooth and controlled.

name: Standing Cable Wood Chop
description: A high-to-low cable chop that trains the obliques through a diagonal pulling path.
instructions: Set the implement at the working height and take a stable stance.
Brace your trunk and start with your hands at the loaded side.
Rotate and pull the handle across your body.
Return slowly without letting the hips spin out.

name: Standing Cable Lift
description: A low-to-high cable lift that trains the obliques through an upward diagonal path.
instructions: Set the implement at the working height and take a stable stance.
Brace your trunk and start with your hands at the loaded side.
Rotate and pull the handle across your body.
Return slowly without letting the hips spin out.

name: Half-Kneeling Cable Chop
description: A half-kneeling chop that makes diagonal cable rotation stricter through the trunk.
instructions: Set the implement at the working height and take a stable stance.
Brace your trunk and start with your hands at the loaded side.
Rotate and pull the handle across your body.
Return slowly without letting the hips spin out.

name: Half-Kneeling Cable Lift
description: A half-kneeling cable lift that trains upward diagonal rotation with less lower-body help.
instructions: Set the implement at the working height and take a stable stance.
Brace your trunk and start with your hands at the loaded side.
Rotate and pull the handle across your body.
Return slowly without letting the hips spin out.

name: Standing Band Wood Chop
description: A high-to-low band chop that gives an elastic-resistance option for diagonal oblique work.
instructions: Set the implement at the working height and take a stable stance.
Brace your trunk and start with your hands at the loaded side.
Rotate and pull the handle across your body.
Return slowly without letting the hips spin out.

name: Standing Band Lift
description: A low-to-high band lift that trains the obliques through an upward diagonal pattern.
instructions: Set the implement at the working height and take a stable stance.
Brace your trunk and start with your hands at the loaded side.
Rotate and pull the handle across your body.
Return slowly without letting the hips spin out.

name: Kneeling Cable Oblique Crunch
description: A cable crunch with a side-bending path to emphasize one oblique chain at a time.
instructions: Kneel beside the high cable with the handle set for one side.
Brace and keep your hips quiet.
Crunch down through the side of your torso.
Return slowly before repeating on the other side.

name: Standing Cable Oblique Crunch
description: A standing cable side crunch that loads oblique flexion from a tall stance.
instructions: Set up in the starting position with your torso angled for the side you are training.
Brace lightly and keep your hips stable.
Crunch through the side of your torso.
Lower slowly back to the start.

name: Dumbbell Side Bend
description: A one-arm side bend that loads lateral trunk flexion with a dumbbell.
instructions: Stand tall with the load at your side.
Brace your trunk and keep your shoulders square.
Bend through your side only as far as you can control.
Return to upright without leaning back.

name: Kettlebell Side Bend
description: A kettlebell side bend that changes the feel of the loaded lateral-flexion pattern.
instructions: Stand tall with the load at your side.
Brace your trunk and keep your shoulders square.
Bend through your side only as far as you can control.
Return to upright without leaning back.

name: Cable Side Bend
description: A cable side bend that keeps the obliques loaded throughout the lateral-flexion range.
instructions: Stand tall with the load at your side.
Brace your trunk and keep your shoulders square.
Bend through your side only as far as you can control.
Return to upright without leaning back.

name: Standing Oblique Crunch
description: A standing oblique crunch that drives the elbow and knee together on one side.
instructions: Stand tall with one hand by your head and the other arm free for balance.
Brace and lift the same-side knee.
Crunch the elbow toward the knee through your side.
Lower slowly before repeating.

name: Cross-Body Mountain Climber
description: A plank-based knee-drive drill that adds a rotational oblique element to the mountain climber pattern.
instructions: Start in a strong plank with your hands under your shoulders.
Brace your trunk and keep your hips level.
Drive one knee across toward the opposite side.
Switch sides smoothly without bouncing.

name: Suspension Trainer Oblique Crunch
description: A suspended oblique crunch that combines instability with cross-body knee drives.
instructions: Set up in a plank with your feet in the straps.
Brace hard and keep your shoulders stacked.
Drive your knees toward one side of your torso.
Extend back out and alternate sides.

name: Stability Ball Oblique Crunch
description: A ball-supported oblique crunch that lets the torso move through extra side-flexion range.
instructions: Set up in the starting position with your torso angled for the side you are training.
Brace lightly and keep your hips stable.
Crunch through the side of your torso.
Lower slowly back to the start.

name: Decline Oblique Crunch
description: A decline oblique crunch that makes side-flexion more demanding by changing the torso angle.
instructions: Set up in the starting position with your torso angled for the side you are training.
Brace lightly and keep your hips stable.
Crunch through the side of your torso.
Lower slowly back to the start.

name: Rotary Torso Machine
description: A rotary-torso machine exercise that trains controlled trunk rotation on a fixed path.
instructions: Adjust the machine so your body lines up with the pads and pivot.
Brace your trunk and take the handles or pads securely.
Crunch through the torso until you reach the end range.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Oblique Crunch Machine
description: A machine side crunch that guides oblique flexion through a fixed resistance path.
instructions: Adjust the machine so your body lines up with the pads and pivot.
Brace your trunk and take the handles or pads securely.
Crunch through the torso until you reach the end range.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Roman Chair Side Bend
description: A supported side bend on a Roman chair that trains the obliques through a larger range.
instructions: Set yourself on the side-bend bench with the support at your hips.
Brace your trunk and keep your spine long.
Bend through the side under control.
Return to the top without jerking.

name: Side Plank Knee Tuck
description: A side plank variation that adds dynamic oblique flexion with a knee tuck.
instructions: Set up in a side plank with the top arm and leg free to move.
Brace your trunk and keep the support shoulder stacked.
Draw the top knee toward your torso or elbow.
Extend back out under control.

name: Hanging Hip Raise
description: A hanging raise that emphasizes curling the pelvis upward at the top of the rep.
instructions: Hang from the bar with your body steady and grip secure.
Raise your knees or legs until your hips can curl upward.
Drive the pelvis up at the top of the rep.
Lower slowly back to a dead stop.

name: Captain's Chair Hip Raise
description: A supported hip raise that emphasizes the pelvic-curl finish from the chair position.
instructions: Set your forearms and back into the support pads.
Raise your knees and curl your pelvis upward at the top.
Squeeze the lower abs without swinging.
Lower slowly to the start.

name: In-and-Out
description: A seated core movement that alternates between a tucked and extended body position.
instructions: Sit with your hands lightly supporting you and your legs extended.
Lean back slightly and brace your trunk.
Pull your knees in toward your chest.
Extend back out without losing posture.

name: Cross-Body Sit-Up
description: A sit-up variation that reaches across the body to add an oblique component.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet set.
Sit up while reaching one hand across toward the opposite side.
Lower back down under control.
Alternate the reaching side on the next rep.

name: Rotational Sit-Up
description: A sit-up with deliberate trunk rotation to train flexion and obliques together.
instructions: Lie on your back with the load or hands centered over your torso.
Sit up and rotate toward one side at the top.
Lower back down under control.
Alternate the rotational direction each rep.

name: Vertical Leg Crunch
description: A crunch performed with the legs held vertical to challenge trunk control and upper-ab flexion.
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs straight up.
Brace and keep the legs as still as possible.
Crunch your shoulders up toward the ceiling.
Lower slowly without dropping your ribs.

name: Weighted Hanging Knee Raise
description: A hanging knee raise with added load that increases resistance without moving to straight legs.
instructions: Secure the load between your feet or ankles and hang from the bar.
Brace hard and limit body swing.
Raise your knees toward your chest under control.
Lower slowly to a dead stop before repeating.

name: Barbell Overhead Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Hold a barbell at upper-chest level with your hands just outside shoulder width.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the bar overhead until your arms extend comfortably.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Seated Barbell Overhead Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Sit upright on a bench and hold a barbell at shoulder height.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the bar overhead until your arms extend comfortably.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell at each shoulder.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the dumbbells overhead until your arms extend comfortably.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Sit upright on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the dumbbells overhead until your arms extend comfortably.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Shoulder Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Stand tall with one dumbbell racked at one shoulder.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the dumbbell overhead without leaning to one side.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Sit upright holding one dumbbell at shoulder level.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the dumbbell overhead while staying square on the bench.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Arnold Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Stand tall with the dumbbells in front of your shoulders and palms facing you.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Rotate your palms outward and press the dumbbells overhead.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Seated Arnold Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Sit upright with the dumbbells in front of your shoulders and palms facing you.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Rotate your palms outward and press the dumbbells overhead.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Barbell Push Press
description: An explosive pressing movement that uses leg drive to move the weight overhead.
instructions: Hold a barbell at shoulder level with your feet under your hips.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Dip slightly, then drive through your legs and press the bar overhead.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Dumbbell Push Press
description: An explosive pressing movement that uses leg drive to move the weight overhead.
instructions: Stand tall with dumbbells at shoulder height.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Dip slightly, then drive up and press the dumbbells overhead.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Push Press
