description: An explosive pressing movement that uses leg drive to move the weight overhead.
instructions: Hold one dumbbell at shoulder height with your free arm out for balance.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Dip slightly, then drive up and punch the dumbbell overhead.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Kettlebell Overhead Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Stand tall with kettlebells racked at your shoulders.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the kettlebells overhead until your arms extend comfortably.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Overhead Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Rack one kettlebell at one shoulder and stand tall.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the kettlebell overhead without twisting your torso.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Seated Kettlebell Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Sit upright with kettlebells at shoulder height.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the kettlebells overhead until your arms extend comfortably.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Bottoms-Up Kettlebell Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Hold one kettlebell upside down at shoulder height with the handle vertical.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the kettlebell overhead while keeping it balanced.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Half-Kneeling Single-Arm Kettlebell Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Set up in a half-kneeling stance with one kettlebell racked at your shoulder.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the kettlebell overhead while staying tall through your hips.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Tall-Kneeling Landmine Press
description: An angled pressing movement that trains the delts with a shoulder-friendly path.
instructions: Kneel tall with both knees down and hold the landmine bar at chest height.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Drive the bar up and slightly forward until your arms extend.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Seated Machine Shoulder Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles start around shoulder height.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the machine handles overhead until your arms extend comfortably.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Machine Shoulder Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Sit tall and grip one machine handle at shoulder height.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the handle overhead without letting your torso shift.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Smith Machine Shoulder Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Sit under a Smith machine bar with the bar at shoulder level.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the bar overhead until your arms extend comfortably.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Cable Shoulder Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Stand between cable handles with your hands at shoulder height.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the handles overhead until your arms extend comfortably.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Cable Shoulder Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Stand tall holding one cable handle at shoulder height.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the handle overhead while resisting rotation through your torso.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Half-Kneeling Single-Arm Cable Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Set up in a half-kneeling stance with one cable handle at shoulder height.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the handle overhead without shifting your hips.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Resistance Band Overhead Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Stand on a resistance band and bring the handles to shoulder level.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the handles overhead until your arms extend comfortably.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Resistance Band Overhead Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Stand on one side of a band and hold the handle at one shoulder.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the handle overhead while keeping your torso tall and steady.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Z Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs straight and a barbell at shoulder level.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the bar overhead without leaning back.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Dumbbell Z Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs straight and dumbbells at shoulder height.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the dumbbells overhead without leaning back.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Viking Press
description: A controlled overhead press that builds the delts through a strong vertical path.
instructions: Stand inside a Viking press machine and hold the handles at shoulder height.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Press the handles overhead until your arms extend comfortably.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Handstand Push-Up
description: A bodyweight pressing movement that heavily challenges the delts and upper-body control.
instructions: Kick into a handstand against a wall with your hands set just outside shoulder width.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Lower your head toward the floor, then press back to full support.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Pike Push-Up
description: A bodyweight pressing movement that heavily challenges the delts and upper-body control.
instructions: Start in a pike position with your hips high and hands under your shoulders.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Lower your head between your hands, then press back up.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Half-Kneeling Single-Arm Landmine Press
description: An angled single-arm press that trains the front and side delts through a shoulder-friendly path.
instructions: Set up in a half-kneeling stance with one hand on the end of the landmine bar.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Drive the bar up and slightly forward with the working arm.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Machine Lateral Raise
description: A unilateral machine raise that isolates the side delt with a fixed resistance path.
instructions: Set the machine so one arm lines up comfortably with the pad or handle.

Raise the working arm out to the side until shoulder height.
Lower with control and repeat before switching sides.

name: Lying Cable Lateral Raise
description: A cable lateral raise performed lying on a bench for smooth tension through the side delts.
instructions: Lie sideways on a bench holding a low cable handle in the top hand.
Keep a soft bend in your elbow and your torso steady.
Raise the handle out to the side until your arm reaches shoulder height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Cuban Press
description: A rotating shoulder movement that trains the delts through external rotation and pressing.
instructions: Hold a light barbell at thigh level with a shoulder-width grip.
Brace your core and keep your torso stacked.
Row it high, rotate your forearms up, and press overhead.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Resistance Band Scaption

instructions: Stand on a band with the handles at your sides.

Raise your arms about 30 degrees forward from your sides until shoulder height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

instructions: Stand tall holding dumbbells at your sides.

Raise the dumbbells out to your sides until about shoulder height.

Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Incline Dumbbell Lateral Raise

Raise the dumbbell away from the floor until your arm is in line with your shoulder.

name: Cable Lateral Raise

name: Single-Arm Cable Lateral Raise

Raise the handle out to the side until your arm reaches shoulder height.

name: Behind-the-Back Cable Lateral Raise

instructions: Stand just in front of a low pulley so the cable starts behind your body.

Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Lean-Away Cable Lateral Raise

name: Seated Cable Lateral Raise

instructions: Sit between low pulleys or hold a cable handle while seated upright.

name: Machine Lateral Raise

instructions: Adjust the machine so your elbows or forearms line up with the pads.

name: Resistance Band Lateral Raise

instructions: Stand on a band with the handles at your sides.

Raise your arms out to the sides until shoulder height.

name: Single-Arm Resistance Band Lateral Raise

Raise your arm out to the side until shoulder height.

name: Dumbbell Y Raise

instructions: Stand tall with light dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Keep a soft bend in your elbows and a steady torso.
Raise your arms on a diagonal until they form a Y shape.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Cable Y Raise
description: A diagonal raise that trains the upper shoulders through a Y-shaped path.
instructions: Stand between low pulleys with the handles near your thighs.
Keep a soft bend in your elbows and a steady torso.
Raise your arms up and out on a diagonal into a Y shape.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Incline Dumbbell Y Raise
description: A diagonal raise that trains the upper shoulders through a Y-shaped path.
instructions: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with light dumbbells hanging below you.
Keep a soft bend in your elbows and a steady torso.
Raise your arms overhead on a diagonal into a Y shape.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Dumbbell Front Raise
description: An isolation raise that emphasizes the front delts.
instructions: Stand tall with dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Keep a soft bend in your elbows and a steady torso.
Raise the dumbbells forward until about shoulder height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Front Raise
description: A unilateral front raise that isolates one front delt at a time with a simple dumbbell setup.
instructions: Stand tall holding one dumbbell in front of your thigh.
Keep a soft bend in your elbow and your torso steady.
Raise the dumbbell forward until your arm reaches shoulder height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat before switching sides.

name: Machine Front Raise
description: A machine-based front raise that isolates the front delts with a guided path.
instructions: Adjust the machine so the lever starts near the front of your thighs or shoulders.
Sit tall and keep your torso still against the pad.
Raise the handles or lever arms forward until shoulder height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Barbell Front Raise
description: An isolation raise that emphasizes the front delts.
instructions: Stand tall holding a barbell in front of your thighs with a shoulder-width grip.
Keep a soft bend in your elbows and a steady torso.
Raise the bar forward until it reaches shoulder height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: EZ-Bar Front Raise
description: An isolation raise that emphasizes the front delts.
instructions: Stand tall holding an EZ-bar in front of your thighs.
Keep a soft bend in your elbows and a steady torso.
Raise the bar forward until about shoulder height.

name: Single-Arm Cable Front Raise
description: An isolation raise that emphasizes the front delts.
instructions: Stand facing away from a low pulley with one handle in one hand.

Lower with control to the start and repeat.

Keep a soft bend in your elbows and a steady torso.
Raise the end of the bar forward and upward until shoulder height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Resistance Band Front Raise
description: An isolation raise that emphasizes the front delts.
instructions: Stand on a resistance band with the handles in front of your thighs.
Keep a soft bend in your elbows and a steady torso.
Raise your arms forward until shoulder height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Dumbbell Scaption
description: A shoulder raise performed in the scapular plane for smooth front-and-side delt work.
instructions: Stand tall with light dumbbells at your sides.
Keep a soft bend in your elbows and a steady torso.
Raise your arms about 30 degrees forward from your sides until shoulder height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Cable Scaption Raise
description: A shoulder raise performed in the scapular plane for smooth front-and-side delt work.
instructions: Stand between low pulleys or use one cable setup for the movement path.
Keep a soft bend in your elbows and a steady torso.
Raise your arms in the scapular plane until shoulder height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: EZ-Bar Upright Row
description: A vertical pulling pattern that loads the side delts and upper shoulders.
instructions: Stand tall holding an EZ-bar in front of your thighs.
Keep your torso steady and lead with your elbows.
Pull the bar upward until your upper arms are near shoulder height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Cable Upright Row
description: A vertical pulling pattern that loads the side delts and upper shoulders.
instructions: Hold a straight-bar handle on a low cable in front of your thighs.
Keep your torso steady and lead with your elbows.
Pull the handle upward until your upper arms near shoulder height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Rope Upright Row
description: A vertical pulling pattern that loads the side delts and upper shoulders.
instructions: Hold a rope attachment from a low pulley with your hands close together.
Keep your torso steady and lead with your elbows.
Pull the rope upward and let your elbows flare out.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Cable Upright Row
description: A vertical pulling pattern that loads the side delts and upper shoulders.
instructions: Stand beside a low pulley holding one handle in one hand.
Keep your torso steady and lead with your elbows.
Pull the handle upward until your elbow reaches about shoulder height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Kettlebell Upright Row
description: A vertical pulling pattern that loads the side delts and upper shoulders.
instructions: Stand tall holding one or two kettlebells in front of your thighs.
Keep your torso steady and lead with your elbows.
Pull the weight upward until it reaches upper-chest height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Smith Machine Upright Row
description: A vertical pulling pattern that loads the side delts and upper shoulders.
instructions: Stand tall holding a Smith machine bar in front of your thighs.
Keep your torso steady and lead with your elbows.
Pull the bar upward until your upper arms approach shoulder height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Resistance Band Upright Row
description: A vertical pulling pattern that loads the side delts and upper shoulders.
instructions: Stand on a resistance band and hold the handles in front of your thighs.
Keep your torso steady and lead with your elbows.
Pull upward until your hands reach upper-chest height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Landmine Upright Row
description: A vertical pulling pattern that loads the side delts and upper shoulders.
instructions: Stand over the end of a landmine bar and hold it with both hands.
Keep your torso steady and lead with your elbows.
Pull the bar upward close to your body until it reaches upper-chest height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Cable Face Pull
description: A pull-to-face movement that builds the rear delts and upper shoulders.
instructions: Set a cable around face height and hold one handle in one hand.
Set your shoulders down and keep your torso still.
Pull the handle toward your face with your elbow high and out.
Return with control and repeat.

name: Resistance Band Face Pull
description: A pull-to-face movement that builds the rear delts and upper shoulders.
instructions: Anchor a band at face height and grip it with both hands.
Set your shoulders down and keep your torso still.
Pull the band toward your face while spreading your hands apart.
Return with control and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Cable Scaption Raise
description: A unilateral cable raise in the scapular plane that trains the front and side delts with constant tension.
instructions: Stand beside a low pulley holding one handle in the outside hand.
Keep a soft bend in your elbow and your torso steady.
Raise your arm on a slight diagonal in the scapular plane until shoulder height.
Lower with control to the start and repeat before switching sides.

name: Reverse Pec Deck
description: A rear-delt isolation movement that opens the arms against resistance.
instructions: Sit facing the reverse pec deck pads with your chest supported.
Set your shoulders down and keep your torso still.
Sweep the handles or arms back until your upper arms line up with your shoulders.
Return with control and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Reverse Pec Deck
description: A rear-delt isolation movement that opens the arms against resistance.
instructions: Sit on the reverse pec deck and hold one handle with one arm.
Set your shoulders down and keep your torso still.
Sweep the arm back until it lines up with your shoulder.
Return with control and repeat.

name: Cable Reverse Fly
description: A rear-delt isolation movement that opens the arms against resistance.
instructions: Stand between shoulder-height cables with the handles crossed in front of you.
Set your shoulders down and keep your torso still.
Open your arms out and back until they line up with your shoulders.
Return with control and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Cable Reverse Fly
description: A rear-delt isolation movement that opens the arms against resistance.
instructions: Stand beside a cable stack holding one handle across your body.
Set your shoulders down and keep your torso still.
Sweep your arm out and back until it lines up with your shoulder.
Return with control and repeat.

name: Bent-Over Dumbbell Reverse Fly
description: A rear-delt isolation movement that opens the arms against resistance.
instructions: Hinge at the hips with dumbbells hanging below your shoulders.
Set your shoulders down and keep your torso still.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder level.
Return with control and repeat.

name: Seated Bent-Over Dumbbell Reverse Fly
description: A rear-delt isolation movement that opens the arms against resistance.
instructions: Sit on a bench, hinge forward, and let dumbbells hang below your shoulders.
Set your shoulders down and keep your torso still.
Raise your arms out to the sides until shoulder level.
Return with control and repeat.

name: Incline Bench Rear Delt Fly
description: A rear-delt isolation movement that opens the arms against resistance.
instructions: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with dumbbells hanging beneath you.
Set your shoulders down and keep your torso still.
Raise your arms out to the sides until shoulder level.
Return with control and repeat.

name: Chest-Supported Cable Rear Delt Fly
description: A rear-delt isolation movement that opens the arms against resistance.
instructions: Set an incline bench between low cables and lie chest-down on it.
Set your shoulders down and keep your torso still.
Sweep your arms out and back until they line up with your shoulders.
Return with control and repeat.

name: Resistance Band Reverse Fly
description: A rear-delt isolation movement that opens the arms against resistance.
instructions: Hold a resistance band in front of your chest with straight but soft elbows.
Set your shoulders down and keep your torso still.
Pull the band apart until your arms spread wide.
Return with control and repeat.

name: TRX Reverse Fly
description: A rear-delt isolation movement that opens the arms against resistance.
instructions: Lean back holding the TRX handles with your body straight.
Set your shoulders down and keep your torso still.
Open your arms out to the sides and pull yourself upward.
Return with control and repeat.

name: Bent-Over Cable Reverse Fly
description: A bent-over cable reverse fly that keeps steady tension on the rear delts.
instructions: Set the cables low, hinge forward, and hold the handles with your arms slightly crossed.
Set your shoulders down and keep your torso still.
Open your arms out and back until they line up with your shoulders.
Return with control and repeat.

name: Rear Delt Row
description: A high-elbow row that emphasizes the rear delts over the lats.
instructions: Hinge at the hips with dumbbells hanging below your shoulders.
Keep your torso steady and lead with your elbows.
Row the weights up with your elbows flared out to the sides.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Chest-Supported Rear Delt Row
description: A high-elbow row that emphasizes the rear delts over the lats.
instructions: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with dumbbells hanging beneath you.
Keep your torso steady and lead with your elbows.
Row the weights by driving your elbows out wide.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Rear Delt Cable Row
description: A high-elbow row that emphasizes the rear delts over the lats.
instructions: Stand beside a cable stack and hold one handle across your body.
Keep your torso steady and lead with your elbows.
Row the handle back with your elbow high and out.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Rope Rear Delt Row
description: A high-elbow row that emphasizes the rear delts over the lats.
instructions: Attach a rope to a low or mid cable and hold it with both hands.
Keep your torso steady and lead with your elbows.
Row the rope toward your upper chest with elbows flared out.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: High Cable Rear Delt Row
description: A high-elbow row that emphasizes the rear delts over the lats.
instructions: Set the cables around upper-chest to shoulder height and grab the handles.
Keep your torso steady and lead with your elbows.
Row with your elbows high and wide until your hands near your upper chest.
Lower with control to the start and repeat.

name: Prone T Raise
description: A rear-delt isolation movement that opens the arms against resistance.
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench with light dumbbells hanging below you.
Set your shoulders down and keep your torso still.
Raise your arms straight out to the sides into a T shape.
Return with control and repeat.

name: Band Pull-Apart
description: A rear-delt isolation movement that opens the arms against resistance.
instructions: Hold a band straight out in front of your chest with both hands.
Set your shoulders down and keep your torso still.
Pull the band apart until your arms spread wide.
Return with control and repeat.

name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
description: A barbell hip hinge that loads the hamstrings and glutes through a long eccentric.
instructions: Stand tall with the bar in front of your thighs.
Push your hips back and lower the bar close to your legs.
Keep your spine neutral and feel the stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
description: A dumbbell hinge that trains the hamstrings and glutes with independent loading.
instructions: Hold the dumbbells at your sides and brace your trunk.
Hinge at the hips and lower the weights along your legs.
Pause when your hamstrings are fully loaded without rounding.
Stand tall by squeezing your glutes.

name: Kettlebell Romanian Deadlift
description: A kettlebell hinge that builds the posterior chain with a compact front-loaded setup.
instructions: Hold the kettlebell in front of your thighs.
Send your hips back and lower the bell close to your body.
Keep your chest proud and knees softly bent.
Drive through your heels and extend your hips to stand.

name: Smith Machine Romanian Deadlift
description: A fixed-path Romanian deadlift that emphasizes controlled hamstring and glute loading.
instructions: Unrack the bar and stand with it against your thighs.
Hinge back slowly while guiding the bar down your legs.
Stop when your hamstrings are stretched and your back stays flat.
Press your feet down and extend your hips to rise.

name: Cable Romanian Deadlift
description: A cable hinge that keeps steady tension on the hamstrings and glutes.
instructions: Hold the cable handle and step back until the stack is loaded.
Hinge your hips back while keeping the handle close to your legs.
Maintain a long spine and slight knee bend at the bottom.
Drive your hips forward to finish the rep.

name: Landmine Romanian Deadlift
description: A landmine hinge that combines hip loading with a guided arc path.
instructions: Hold the end of the barbell close to your hips.
Push your hips back and let the bar travel down in its arc.
Keep your torso rigid and shins nearly vertical.
Stand up by squeezing your glutes and extending your hips.

name: Trap Bar Romanian Deadlift
description: A trap bar Romanian deadlift that loads the posterior chain with a neutral grip.
instructions: Stand inside the trap bar and grip the handles.
Hinge your hips back while lowering the bar under control.
Keep the handles close and your spine neutral.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.

name: Resistance Band Romanian Deadlift
description: A banded hinge that trains the glutes and hamstrings with rising tension.
instructions: Stand on the band and hold the ends at your sides.
Hinge back and lower your hands toward mid-shin.
Keep tension in the band and your back flat.
Stand up hard by driving your hips through.

name: Barbell Stiff-Leg Deadlift
description: A longer-range deadlift variation that heavily challenges the hamstrings and glutes.
instructions: Stand with the bar over your midfoot and your legs nearly straight.
Hinge down to lower the bar while keeping it close.
Feel the stretch through the backs of your legs without rounding.
Extend your hips to bring the bar back to standing.

name: Dumbbell Stiff-Leg Deadlift
description: A dumbbell stiff-leg pull that emphasizes hamstring length under load.
instructions: Hold the dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Lower them with a deep hip hinge and minimal knee bend.
Keep the weights close and your torso braced.
Stand tall by contracting your glutes.

name: Smith Machine Stiff-Leg Deadlift
description: A fixed-path stiff-leg deadlift that isolates the posterior chain with stability.
instructions: Unrack the bar and stand tall with soft knees.
Hinge down while the bar tracks close to your legs.
Stop before your lower back loses position.
Drive your hips through to finish the rep.

name: Conventional Deadlift
description: A classic pull from the floor that builds the hamstrings, glutes, and entire posterior chain.
instructions: Set the bar over your midfoot and brace hard before lifting.
Push the floor away and keep the bar close as it rises.
Stand tall with your hips and knees fully extended.
Lower the bar back to the floor with control.

name: Kettlebell Deadlift
description: A simple hinge from the floor that teaches glute and hamstring strength with a compact load.
instructions: Place the kettlebell between your feet and hinge to grip it.
Brace your trunk and drive the floor away.
Stand tall while keeping the bell close to your body.
Lower it back between your feet with control.

name: Dumbbell Deadlift
description: A dumbbell pull from the floor that builds the posterior chain with independent handles.
instructions: Set the dumbbells beside your feet and hinge down to grab them.
Brace and stand up by driving through your heels.
Keep the weights close to your legs as you rise.
Return them to the floor under control.

name: Landmine Deadlift
description: A landmine deadlift that blends a squat-hinge pattern with strong glute loading.
instructions: Straddle the end of the barbell and grip the sleeve or handle.
Brace your torso and push the floor away to stand.
Keep the load close and your chest lifted.
Lower the bar back down in its arc with control.

name: Frog Pump
description: A glute-dominant bridge variation that uses a frog-leg position to emphasize hip extension.
instructions: Lie on your back with the soles of your feet together and knees open.
Brace your core and let your knees stay relaxed outward.
Drive your hips up by squeezing your glutes hard at the top.
Lower under control and repeat without losing the foot position.

name: Barbell Good Morning
description: A loaded hinge that trains the hamstrings and glutes through torso control.
instructions: Set the bar across your upper back and brace your trunk.
Hinge your hips back until your torso leans forward.
Keep a soft knee bend and a flat back throughout.
Drive your hips forward to return upright.

name: Safety Bar Good Morning
description: A safety bar good morning that shifts the load comfortably while training the posterior chain.
instructions: Rest the safety bar on your shoulders and grip the handles.
Hinge forward by pushing your hips back.
Keep your torso braced and your neck neutral.
Extend your hips to stand tall again.

name: Seated Good Morning
description: A seated hinge that reduces knee contribution and focuses on hamstrings, glutes, and low back control.
instructions: Sit on a bench with the bar secured across your upper back.
Brace and hinge your torso forward from the hips.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch without rounding.
Reverse the motion and sit tall again.

name: Smith Machine Good Morning
description: A guided good morning that helps control the hip hinge under load.
instructions: Position the bar on your upper back and unrack it.
Hinge your hips back while the bar tracks straight.
Lower until your hamstrings are loaded and your back stays flat.
Drive your hips forward to return upright.

name: Resistance Band Good Morning
description: A banded hinge that builds glute and hamstring strength with accommodating resistance.
instructions: Stand on the band and loop it over your upper back or shoulders.
Brace and hinge forward from your hips.
Keep the band taut and your knees softly bent.
Stand up by squeezing your glutes.

name: Bodyweight Good Morning
description: A simple bodyweight hinge that teaches posterior-chain mechanics and control.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and hands across your chest.
Push your hips back and lean forward under control.
Keep your spine neutral and knees slightly bent.
Drive your hips forward to stand back up.

name: Dumbbell Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
description: A unilateral hinge that challenges balance while loading one hamstring and glute at a time.
instructions: Hold the dumbbell and balance on one leg.
Hinge your hips back as the free leg reaches behind you.
Lower until your hips stay square and your back remains flat.
Drive through the standing foot to return upright.

name: Kettlebell Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
description: A kettlebell single-leg hinge that builds posterior-chain strength and stability.
instructions: Hold the kettlebell and plant one foot firmly on the floor.
Hinge forward while extending the free leg behind you.
Keep the bell close to your stance leg and your hips level.
Stand tall by squeezing the glute on the working side.

name: Barbell Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
description: A barbell single-leg hinge that demands high balance and posterior-chain control.
instructions: Set the bar in your hands and shift onto one leg.
Hinge down while the free leg extends behind you.
Keep the bar close and your torso rigid throughout.
Drive through the stance foot to stand back up.

name: Cable Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
description: A cable-based single-leg hinge that keeps constant tension through the working leg.
instructions: Hold the cable handle and stand on one leg.
Hinge back against the pull of the cable.
Lower until your hamstring is loaded and your hips stay square.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.

name: Landmine Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
description: A landmine single-leg hinge that provides a guided arc for unilateral posterior-chain work.
instructions: Hold the end of the barbell and stand on one leg.
Hinge forward as the free leg reaches back for balance.
Keep the load close and your trunk braced.
Return upright by driving through your planted foot.

name: Smith Machine Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
description: A guided unilateral hinge that lets you focus on one glute and hamstring at a time.
instructions: Stand on one leg with the Smith bar in your hands.
Hinge your hips back while keeping the bar path close.
Lower until you feel the working hamstring stretch.
Stand back up by squeezing the glute on the stance side.

name: Bodyweight Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
description: A balance-focused single-leg hinge that teaches posterior-chain control without external load.
instructions: Balance on one leg with a soft bend in the knee.
Hinge forward as your free leg extends behind you.
Keep your hips level and your spine long.
Stand back up by driving through the working foot.

name: Dumbbell B-Stance Romanian Deadlift
description: A staggered Romanian deadlift that biases one hamstring and glute while keeping balance simple.
instructions: Hold the dumbbells and place one foot slightly behind the other.
Keep most of your weight on the front leg as you hinge back.
Lower the weights close to the lead leg without twisting.
Drive through the front heel to stand up.

name: Barbell B-Stance Romanian Deadlift
description: A barbell staggered Romanian deadlift that emphasizes one side of the posterior chain.
instructions: Set the bar in your hands with one foot slightly behind for support.
Hinge back while keeping most pressure in the front foot.
Lower until the front hamstring is stretched and your back stays flat.
Stand tall by driving your lead hip forward.

name: Kettlebell B-Stance Romanian Deadlift
description: A kettlebell staggered hinge that targets one glute and hamstring with a stable setup.
instructions: Hold the kettlebell and step one foot slightly back.
Hinge from the hips while loading the front leg.
Keep your chest open and the kettlebell close to the lead thigh.
Stand up by squeezing the glute of the front side.

name: Cable B-Stance Romanian Deadlift
description: A cable staggered hinge that keeps steady tension on the lead-side hamstring and glute.
instructions: Grab the cable handle and set one foot slightly behind the other.
Hinge back while keeping most of your weight on the front leg.
Let the cable pull you into the stretch without rounding.
Drive through the lead foot to stand tall.

name: Barbell Frog Pump
description: A loaded frog pump that targets the glutes and hamstrings with a short powerful bridge pattern.
instructions: Lie back with the barbell settled across your hips and your feet pressed together.
Let your knees open out and brace your trunk before each rep.
Drive your hips upward by squeezing your glutes hard.
Lower slowly while keeping the frog-leg position fixed.

name: Hamstring Walkout
description: A bridge-based hamstring exercise that lengthens the lever as you walk the heels away from the hips.
instructions: Start in a glute bridge with your hips lifted and feet flat.
Take small heel steps forward while keeping your hips off the floor.
Walk out until your hamstrings are fully challenged without losing position.
Walk your heels back in and lower only after you regain the bridge.

name: Single-Leg Good Morning
description: A unilateral good morning that strengthens the hamstrings and glutes while improving balance.
instructions: Balance on one leg with your hands across your chest.
Hinge forward from the hips as the free leg reaches back.
Keep your spine long and hips square to the floor.
Return upright by squeezing the glute on the standing side.

name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Romanian Deadlift
description: A supported unilateral hinge that lets the front hamstring and glute take most of the load.
instructions: Hold the dumbbells and place your rear foot on a bench behind you.
Keep most of your weight over the front leg and hinge back.
Lower until the front hamstring is fully loaded.
Drive through the front foot to stand back up.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
description: A heavy hip extension exercise that strongly targets the glutes and hamstrings.
instructions: Rest your upper back on a bench and roll the bar over your hips.
Plant your feet and brace your core before lifting.
Drive through your heels to raise your hips until locked out.
Lower your hips under control to the start.

name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
description: A hip thrust variation that uses dumbbells for direct glute and hamstring loading.
instructions: Set your upper back on a bench and place the dumbbell over your hips.
Brace your trunk and keep your feet flat on the floor.
Drive your hips up until your torso is level with your thighs.
Lower back down with control.

name: Smith Machine Hip Thrust
description: A guided hip thrust that makes glute-focused loading stable and repeatable.
instructions: Set a bench behind you and position the Smith bar over your hips.
Plant your feet and brace before starting the rep.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips to full extension.
Lower the bar back down with control.

name: Machine Hip Thrust
description: A machine hip thrust that trains glutes and hamstrings with a fixed setup.
instructions: Sit into the machine and secure your body against the pad.
Place your feet firmly and brace your midsection.
Drive the pad upward by extending your hips.
Lower the weight slowly to the start.

name: Resistance Band Hip Thrust
description: A banded hip thrust that increases tension as the hips lock out.
instructions: Set your upper back on a bench and place the band over your hips.
Plant your feet and create tension in the band.
Drive your hips upward until fully extended.
Lower back down while keeping the band under tension.

name: Landmine Hip Thrust
description: A landmine hip thrust that provides a stable loading angle for hip extension.
instructions: Rest your upper back on a bench and position the bar end over your hips.
Set your feet and brace before each rep.
Drive through your heels to extend your hips strongly.
Lower back to the bottom with control.

name: Cable Hip Thrust
description: A cable-loaded hip thrust that keeps tension on the glutes and hamstrings through the full rep.
instructions: Set a bench in front of the low cable and attach the belt or handle.
Position your upper back on the bench and brace your core.
Drive your hips upward against the cable resistance.
Lower slowly until your hips are back at the start.

name: Bodyweight Hip Thrust
description: A bodyweight hip thrust that builds glute and hamstring strength with minimal setup.
instructions: Place your upper back on a bench with your feet flat on the floor.
Brace your trunk and keep your chin tucked slightly.
Drive your hips upward until your body forms a straight line.
Lower back down with control.

name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
description: A unilateral hip thrust that isolates one glute and hamstring at a time.
instructions: Set your upper back on a bench and lift one foot off the floor.
Brace and press through the planted heel.
Drive your hips up while keeping your pelvis level.
Lower under control and repeat on the same side.

name: B-Stance Hip Thrust
description: A staggered hip thrust that biases one glute while keeping extra balance support.
instructions: Set up for a hip thrust and place one foot slightly forward.
Keep most of your pressure through the lead heel.
Drive your hips up while the rear leg gives light assistance.
Lower with control and finish all reps on one side.

name: Glute Bridge
description: A floor-based bridge that targets the glutes and hamstrings with a short range.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat.
Brace your core and press your lower back lightly into the floor.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips.
Lower back down under control.

name: Barbell Glute Bridge
description: A loaded floor bridge that builds glute and hamstring strength without a bench.
instructions: Lie on the floor with the barbell settled across your hips.
Bend your knees and brace your trunk before lifting.
Drive through your heels to raise your hips to full extension.
Lower the bar back to the floor with control.

name: Dumbbell Glute Bridge
description: A dumbbell floor bridge that directly trains the glutes and hamstrings.
instructions: Lie on your back and place the dumbbell over your hips.
Set your feet and brace before the rep starts.
Lift your hips by pressing through your heels.
Lower back to the floor slowly.

name: Smith Machine Glute Bridge
description: A guided glute bridge that lets you load hip extension safely from the floor.
instructions: Lie under the Smith bar with it positioned over your hips.
Plant your feet and brace your midsection.
Drive your hips up until fully extended.
Lower the bar under control to the start.

name: Resistance Band Glute Bridge
description: A banded floor bridge that keeps the glutes working hard through lockout.
instructions: Lie on your back with the band secured for hip resistance.
Place your feet flat and brace your core.
Drive your hips up against the band tension.
Lower slowly while keeping tension on the band.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
description: A unilateral bridge that trains one glute and hamstring at a time from the floor.
instructions: Lie on your back with one foot planted and the other leg lifted.
Brace and press through the planted heel.
Raise your hips while keeping your pelvis level.
Lower back down with control on the same side.

name: Feet-Elevated Glute Bridge
description: A bridge with the feet raised to increase posterior-chain range and demand.
instructions: Lie on your back with your heels elevated on a bench or box.
Brace your trunk and keep your toes pulled up.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips off the floor.
Lower under control until your hips touch down.

name: Stability Ball Glute Bridge
description: A bridge on a ball that combines hip extension with extra stability demand.
instructions: Lie on your back with your heels resting on the ball.
Brace your core and keep the ball steady.
Drive your hips upward until your body forms a straight line.
Lower slowly without letting the ball drift.

name: Marching Glute Bridge
description: A bridge variation that adds alternating leg lifts for unilateral glute control.
instructions: Lift into a glute bridge with both feet planted.
Keep your hips high and your ribs down.
Slowly lift one knee toward your chest without dropping your pelvis.
Alternate sides while maintaining the bridge position.

name: Long-Lever Glute Bridge
description: A long-lever bridge that increases hamstring demand while still training hip extension.
instructions: Lie on your back with your feet set farther away than a normal bridge.
Brace your trunk and dig your heels into the floor.
Lift your hips while keeping your legs long.
Lower under control without losing tension.

name: Lying Leg Curl
description: A machine hamstring curl performed face down with controlled knee flexion.
instructions: Adjust the pad so it rests just above your heels.
Brace your body into the bench before starting.
Curl the pad toward your glutes under control.
Lower the weight back to the start slowly.

name: Seated Leg Curl
description: A seated machine curl that trains the hamstrings through a long stretch position.
instructions: Set the machine so your knees line up with the pivot.
Lock your thighs in place under the support pad.
Curl your heels down and back as far as comfortable.
Return the weight slowly to full extension.

name: Standing Leg Curl
description: A standing machine curl that isolates one hamstring through a supported single-leg action.
instructions: Set the roller pad behind your lower leg and hold the handles.
Keep your thigh still as you bend your knee.
Curl your heel up toward your glute.
Lower the pad back down with control.

name: Single-Leg Lying Leg Curl
description: A one-leg prone machine curl that highlights side-to-side hamstring strength.
instructions: Set one ankle under the pad and keep your hips down.
Brace into the bench before starting the rep.
Curl your heel toward your glute without twisting.
Lower slowly until your knee is nearly straight.

name: Single-Leg Seated Leg Curl
description: A unilateral seated machine curl that isolates one hamstring at a time.
instructions: Set one leg on the pad and align your knee with the machine pivot.
Lock your torso and thigh in place.
Curl the working heel down under control.
Return to the start without letting the weight drop.

name: Single-Leg Hamstring Walkout
description: A unilateral walkout that challenges one hamstring and glute at a time from a bridge position.
instructions: Lift into a bridge with one heel planted and the other leg off the floor.
Take small steps out with the working heel while keeping your pelvis level.
Stop when you can still control the bridge without cramping or twisting.
Walk the heel back in and repeat on the same side.

name: Prone Cable Leg Curl
description: A cable hamstring curl performed face down for smooth tension through the range.
instructions: Attach the ankle strap and lie face down in front of the low pulley.
Keep your hips down and leg straight at the start.
Curl your heel toward your glute against the cable.
Lower back to full extension with control.

name: Standing Cable Leg Curl
description: A standing cable curl that isolates the hamstrings one leg at a time.
instructions: Attach the ankle strap to one leg and face the machine.
Brace your torso and keep your thigh still.
Curl your heel upward under steady tension.
Lower the leg back down slowly.

name: Seated Cable Leg Curl
description: A seated cable curl that trains knee flexion with continuous resistance.
instructions: Sit facing away from the low cable with the strap on one ankle.
Sit tall and keep your thigh steady on the bench.
Curl your heel back under control.
Extend your leg slowly to the start.

name: Lying Resistance Band Leg Curl
description: A band hamstring curl performed lying down with simple anchored resistance.
instructions: Lie face down with the band attached around your ankles or heels.
Start with your legs straight and hips pressed into the floor.
Curl your heels toward your glutes against the band.
Lower slowly until your legs are straight again.

name: Seated Resistance Band Leg Curl
description: A seated band curl that lets you train hamstrings with portable resistance.
instructions: Sit tall with the band anchored in front of you around both ankles.
Keep your thighs still and your trunk braced.
Curl your heels back under tension.
Return your legs forward with control.

name: Standing Resistance Band Leg Curl
description: A standing band curl that isolates the hamstrings with light, accessible resistance.
instructions: Anchor the band low and loop it around one ankle.
Stand tall and hold onto support for balance.
Curl your heel up toward your glute.
Lower the leg slowly until straight.

name: Dumbbell Leg Curl
description: A lying hamstring curl that uses a dumbbell held between the feet.
instructions: Lie face down and secure a dumbbell carefully between your feet.
Keep your thighs pressed into the bench or floor.
Curl the dumbbell toward your glutes under control.
Lower slowly without dropping the weight.

name: Stability Ball Leg Curl
description: A ball-based leg curl that combines hamstring flexion with hip stability.
instructions: Lie on your back with your heels on the ball and hips lifted.
Keep your glutes tight and your body in a straight line.
Curl the ball toward you by bending your knees.
Roll the ball back out under control.

name: Single-Leg Stability Ball Leg Curl
description: A unilateral ball curl that strongly challenges one hamstring at a time.
instructions: Lift your hips with one heel on the ball and the other leg off the floor.
Keep your pelvis level as you start the curl.
Pull the ball toward you with the working leg.
Extend the leg back out slowly.

name: Slider Leg Curl
description: A floor hamstring curl that uses sliders for smooth bilateral knee flexion.
instructions: Lie on your back with your heels on sliders and hips lifted.
Brace your trunk and keep your hips off the floor.
Slide your heels toward your glutes.
Extend your legs back out with control.

name: Single-Leg Slider Leg Curl
description: A unilateral sliding curl that builds hamstring strength and pelvic control.
instructions: Place one heel on a slider and lift your hips into a bridge.
Keep the free leg off the floor and your hips level.
Slide the working heel toward your glute.
Extend the leg back out slowly.

name: Towel Leg Curl
description: A hamstring curl on a slick surface using towels as simple sliders.
instructions: Lie on your back with your heels on towels on a smooth floor.
Lift your hips and brace your trunk.
Pull your heels toward your body by bending your knees.
Slide them back out under control.

name: Single-Leg Towel Leg Curl
description: A one-leg towel curl that challenges hamstrings and glute stability together.
instructions: Set one heel on a towel and raise your hips off the floor.
Keep your free leg lifted and pelvis level.
Slide the working heel in toward your glute.
Extend the leg back out slowly.

name: Suspension Trainer Leg Curl
description: A suspended hamstring curl that combines knee flexion with core and hip control.
instructions: Place both heels in the suspension trainer and lie on your back.
Lift your hips and keep your body straight.
Curl your heels toward your glutes.
Extend your legs back out with control.

name: Single-Leg Suspension Trainer Leg Curl
description: A unilateral suspended curl that heavily taxes one hamstring at a time.
instructions: Put one heel in the strap and lift your hips off the floor.
Keep your free leg lifted and your torso braced.
Curl your heel toward your body under control.
Extend the working leg back out slowly.

name: Stability Ball Hamstring Walkout
description: A ball-based walkout that combines hip extension with a long-lever hamstring challenge.
instructions: Place your heels on the ball and lift your hips into a bridge.
Slowly roll the ball farther away by extending your knees.
Keep your hips high and trunk braced as the lever lengthens.
Pull the ball back in and maintain control through the full return.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
description: A demanding bodyweight hamstring curl that emphasizes eccentric strength.
instructions: Kneel with your ankles secured under a sturdy pad, low bar, or partner.
Brace your glutes and lower yourself forward slowly.
Catch yourself lightly with your hands if needed.
Pull back up using your hamstrings as much as possible.

name: Donkey Kick
description: A bodyweight hip-extension exercise that isolates the glutes while teaching pelvic control.
instructions: Start on all fours with your hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Brace your trunk and keep your spine still throughout the rep.
Drive one heel upward by extending the hip without swinging the torso.
Lower the knee back down under control and repeat on the same side.

name: Resistance Band Donkey Kick
description: A band-resisted donkey kick that adds continuous tension to glute-focused hip extension.
instructions: Loop the band securely and set up on all fours with tension on one foot.
Brace your midsection and keep your hips square to the floor.
Kick the working heel back and up by extending the hip.
Return slowly until the knee is under your hip again.

name: Razor Curl
description: A glute-ham developer movement that blends hip flexion and hamstring curl strength.
instructions: Set yourself on the GHD with your body supported and feet secured.
Lower into the stretched position while keeping tension in your hamstrings.
Curl yourself back up by bending the knees and extending the hips.
Finish in control and reset for the next rep.

name: 45-Degree Back Extension
description: A hip-dominant back extension that strengthens the glutes and hamstrings.
instructions: Set your hips on the pad with your feet secured behind you.
Hinge down under control while keeping your spine neutral.
Drive your hips into the pad to raise your torso.
Stop when your body forms a straight line.

name: Single-Leg 45-Degree Back Extension
description: A unilateral back extension that challenges one glute and hamstring more directly.
instructions: Set up on the 45-degree bench with one foot firmly secured.
Lower your torso under control while staying square.
Drive through the working hip to raise your body.
Return slowly and keep the nonworking side quiet.

name: Bench Reverse Hyperextension
description: A flat-bench reverse hyper that trains the glutes and hamstrings through hip extension.
instructions: Lie face down on a flat bench with your hips near the edge.
Hold the bench and brace your trunk to stay stable.
Lift your legs by extending your hips until they line up with your body.
Lower your legs back down under control.

name: Glute-Ham Developer Hip Extension
description: A hip-extension-focused GHD exercise that targets the glutes and hamstrings with torso support.
instructions: Set your hips on the GHD pad with your feet secured.
Hinge forward while keeping your spine neutral.
Extend your hips to raise your torso back in line.
Pause briefly at the top and lower again.

name: Stability Ball Back Extension
description: A ball-supported hip extension that trains the posterior chain with extra stability demand.
instructions: Lie face down over the ball with your feet anchored wide.
Brace your trunk and start from a slight forward bend.
Extend your hips to raise your torso in line with your legs.
Lower slowly back over the ball.

name: Machine Back Extension
description: A machine hip extension that strengthens the glutes and hamstrings with guided resistance.
instructions: Adjust the machine so the pad lines up with your hips.
Brace your trunk and start from the bent position.
Extend your hips to move the lever through the working range.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Resistance Band Pull-Through
description: A banded hip hinge that emphasizes glute extension with accommodating resistance.
instructions: Anchor the band low behind you and step forward into tension.
Hinge your hips back with the band passing between your legs.
Drive your hips through to stand tall.
Return to the hinge position under control.

name: Single-Leg Reverse Hyperextension
description: A unilateral reverse hyper that trains one glute and hamstring at a time from a supported position.
instructions: Set up on the reverse hyper with one leg hanging free and the other quiet.
Brace your torso into the pad before starting the rep.
Raise the working leg by extending the hip without twisting.
Lower under control and finish all reps on one side before switching.

name: Pull-Up
description: A bodyweight vertical pull using a pronated grip to develop lat width and upper back thickness.
instructions: Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with palms facing away.
Hang at full arm extension with shoulders packed.
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving elbows down and back.
Lower under control until arms are fully extended.

name: Chin-Up
description: A bodyweight vertical pull with a supinated grip that increases bicep involvement while targeting the lats.
instructions: Grip the bar shoulder-width apart with palms facing toward you.
Hang with arms fully extended and core braced.
Pull your chin above the bar by driving elbows down toward your hips.
Lower slowly back to the dead hang position.

name: Wide-Grip Pull-Up
description: A pull-up variation with a grip wider than shoulder-width to maximize lat stretch and width.
instructions: Grip the bar significantly wider than shoulder-width with palms facing away.
Initiate the pull by depressing the shoulder blades.
Pull until your upper chest reaches the bar, focusing on squeezing the lats.
Lower in a controlled manner to a full dead hang.

name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
description: A pull-up performed with a neutral (palms-facing) grip for a shoulder-friendly lat-focused movement.
instructions: Grip a neutral-grip attachment or handles with palms facing each other.
Hang at full arm extension with shoulder blades slightly retracted.
Pull your chest up toward the handles by driving elbows toward your hips.
Lower under full control back to the start.

name: Weighted Pull-Up
description: A pronated pull-up with added external load via a belt or vest to increase resistance for strength development.
instructions: Attach a weight plate to a dip belt and secure it around your waist.
Grip a pull-up bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with a pronated grip.
Pull explosively, driving elbows down until your chest reaches the bar.
Lower slowly under control to a full dead hang.

name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
description: A pull-up using a resistance band looped around the bar to reduce bodyweight load for beginners or high-rep sets.
instructions: Loop a resistance band over the pull-up bar and place your knees or feet inside it.
Grip the bar with a pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Pull your chest toward the bar with the band providing assistance.
Lower slowly and repeat.

name: Machine-Assisted Pull-Up
description: A pull-up performed on an assisted pull-up machine that counterbalances a portion of your bodyweight.
instructions: Set the counterweight to the desired assistance level.
Kneel or stand on the platform and grip the bar with a pronated grip.
Pull your chin above the bar, keeping elbows driving downward.
Lower with control until arms are fully extended.

name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
description: A cable machine pulldown using a wide pronated grip to target lat width from a seated position.
instructions: Sit at a lat pulldown machine and grip the bar wide with palms facing away.
Secure your thighs under the pad and lean back slightly.
Pull the bar to your upper chest by driving your elbows toward the floor.
Return the bar under control to full arm extension.

name: Neutral-Grip Lat Pulldown
description: A lat pulldown using a narrow neutral-grip attachment to allow a full range of motion with reduced wrist strain.
instructions: Attach a V-bar or parallel grip handle to the top pulley of a cable machine.
Sit down, secure thighs under the pad, and grip the V-bar with palms facing each other.
Pull the attachment to your chest, driving elbows straight down.
Slowly extend arms back to the starting position.

name: Reverse-Grip Lat Pulldown
description: A lat pulldown performed with a supinated grip to emphasize the lower lats and increase bicep engagement.
instructions: Grip the pulldown bar shoulder-width with palms facing toward you.
Sit tall with thighs secured and a slight lean back.
Pull the bar toward your upper chest by pulling elbows down and back.
Extend arms to full stretch before the next rep.

name: Single-Arm Cable Pulldown
description: A unilateral lat pulldown using a single cable handle to address side-to-side imbalances.
instructions: Attach a single handle to the top pulley and sit facing the machine.
Grip the handle with one hand and sit with your torso slightly inclined away.
Pull the handle down toward your hip by driving your elbow down and back.
Return to full extension with control and repeat before switching arms.

name: Straight-Arm Cable Pulldown
description: A cable isolation movement keeping the arms straight to isolate the lats through a large arc of motion.
instructions: Set a cable machine to the highest pulley and attach a straight bar.
Stand facing the machine and grip the bar with arms extended overhead.
Keeping arms straight, pull the bar down to your thighs using only your lats.
Slowly return to the overhead position with full lat stretch.

name: Single-Arm Straight-Arm Pulldown
description: A unilateral version of the straight-arm pulldown for unmatched lat isolation and stretch.
instructions: Set the cable pulley to head height and attach a single handle.
Grip the handle with one hand, arm extended toward the pulley.
Keeping the arm straight, sweep it down toward your hip in a wide arc.
Return slowly with control and repeat before switching sides.

name: Kneeling Cable Pulldown
description: A lat pulldown performed in a kneeling position to eliminate leg drive and force pure lat engagement.
instructions: Set a cable to the highest pulley and attach a rope.
Kneel directly beneath the cable with your back upright.
Grip the rope and pull both ends toward either side of your neck.
Return slowly to full arm extension overhead.

name: Behind-the-Neck Pulldown
description: A lat pulldown where the bar is pulled to behind the neck for a different lat angle, suitable for flexible lifters.
instructions: Sit at a pulldown station with a wide grip on the bar.
Lean your head and upper body slightly forward.
Pull the bar down behind your head to the base of your skull.
Return the bar with control to full arm extension.

name: Incline Bench Lat Pulldown
description: A pulldown performed lying prone on an incline bench to restrict trunk movement and isolate the lats.
instructions: Position an incline bench facing a cable tower and set the pulley to the top.
Lie prone (face down) on the incline bench and grip the bar overhead.
Pull the bar toward your chest while keeping your torso flat on the bench.
Slowly return to full arm extension.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
description: A classic lat and chest stretch exercise performed lying perpendicular on a bench with a single dumbbell.
instructions: Lie perpendicular on a flat bench with your upper back supported and hips dropped.
Hold a single dumbbell with both hands above your chest, arms slightly bent.
Lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head until you feel a deep lat stretch.
Pull it back over your chest using your lats.

name: Kneeling Cable Pullover
description: A kneeling cable pullover variation that provides constant tension on the lats through the full range of motion.
instructions: Set the cable to the highest pulley and attach a rope.
Kneel facing the machine at arm's length from the stack.
With a slight forward lean, pull the rope from overhead down to your thighs with straight arms.
Return with control to the fully stretched overhead position.

name: Gymnastic Ring Pull-Up
description: A pull-up performed on gymnastics rings, requiring greater stabilization and allowing wrist rotation for joint health.
instructions: Set gymnastics rings at the appropriate height and grip one with each hand.
Hang with arms fully extended, allowing rings to naturally rotate.
Pull your chest to ring height by driving elbows down and back.
Lower with control to a full hang.

name: Ring Muscle-Up
description: An advanced gymnastics movement transitioning from a pull-up to a ring dip in one fluid motion.
instructions: Hang from gymnastics rings with a false grip.
Generate a slight swing and aggressively pull the rings to your hips.
Transition by rotating your wrists over the rings and pressing to full elbow extension.
Lower back with control through the pull-up phase.

name: Bar Muscle-Up
description: An advanced calisthenic movement where the athlete transitions from below to above a pull-up bar in one motion.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with a pronated grip, slightly wider than shoulders.
Generate a kip or explosive pull to get your hips above bar level.
Press yourself up and over the bar to a support position.
Control the descent back to the dead hang.

name: Archer Pull-Up
description: A pull-up variation where one arm pulls while the other extends, creating a unilateral-like loading effect.
instructions: Grip a wide bar, wider than your normal pull-up position.
Pull your body toward one hand while the opposite arm extends nearly straight.
Rise until the active elbow passes the bar and your shoulder reaches hand height.
Lower and alternate sides each rep.

name: Assisted One-Arm Pull-Up
description: A progression toward the full one-arm pull-up using a band or towel for minimal assistance on one side.
instructions: Loop a light band over the bar and grip it with your assisting hand.
Place your working hand directly on the bar in a pronated grip.
Pull yourself up using primarily the working arm while the band provides minimal assistance.
Lower with control and repeat before switching sides.

name: Typewriter Pull-Up
description: A pull-up variation where you traverse side to side at the top for extended time under tension on each lat.
instructions: Grip the bar wide with a pronated grip and pull yourself to bar level.
Shift your body horizontally toward one hand while extending the other arm.
Traverse back across toward the other hand, maintaining chin above bar.
Lower from the last position and repeat.

name: Commando Pull-Up
description: A pull-up variation where the body is positioned perpendicular to the bar with a staggered grip, targeting each lat differently.
instructions: Stand perpendicular to the bar and place hands in a staggered grip with palms facing each other.
Pull your body up, directing one side of the neck toward the bar.
Lower and pull up toward the opposite side of the neck.
Alternate sides each rep.

name: Rope Lat Pulldown
description: A lat pulldown using a rope attachment to allow natural wrist rotation and a slightly different line of pull.
instructions: Attach a rope to the top pulley and sit at the pulldown station.
Grip both ends of the rope with palms facing in and arms extended overhead.
Pull the rope down and slightly apart toward your upper chest.
Slowly return to the full overhead stretch.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Pullover
description: A unilateral dumbbell pullover performed lying on a bench to isolate each lat independently.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in one hand above your chest, arm slightly bent.
Lower the dumbbell in an arc toward the floor behind your head.
Feel a full stretch in the lat, then pull the weight back to the starting position.
Complete reps before switching sides.

name: Standing Single-Arm Cable Pullover
description: A standing unilateral cable pullover that demands significant core stability while isolating one lat.
instructions: Set a cable pulley to head height and attach a single handle.
Stand side-on to the machine and grip the handle with the far hand.
With a straight arm, sweep it downward in a wide arc to your hip.
Return slowly to the stretched position and repeat before switching sides.

name: Underhand Seated Cable Row
description: A seated cable row with a supinated grip that shifts more tension to the lower lats.
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and sit on the bench facing the machine.
Grip the bar with palms facing up and arms fully extended.
Row the bar to your lower abdomen while pulling elbows tight to your sides.
Return the bar with a controlled stretch.

name: High Cable Lat Pull
description: A standing cable exercise pulling a high pulley to the thigh, isolating the lat in a functional position.
instructions: Set the cable pulley to its highest position and attach a single handle.
Stand facing the machine and grip the handle with one arm extended upward.
Pull the handle down toward your thigh by depressing and adducting the shoulder.
Return to the overhead position and repeat before switching sides.

name: Single-Arm Overhead Cable Lat Stretch Pull
description: A single-arm overhead pull specifically designed to maximally stretch and contract the lat through its full range.
instructions: Sit sideways at a cable machine with a high pulley and single handle.
Reach across your body overhead to grip the handle.
Pull the handle down toward your outside hip in a sweeping arc.
Slowly return to the fully stretched overhead position.

name: Hammer Strength Pulldown
description: A machine pulldown using a Hammer Strength plate-loaded unit for a fixed arc of motion with heavy loading.
instructions: Load the Hammer Strength pulldown with appropriate plates and adjust the seat.
Grip the handles and sit with chest against the pad.
Pull the handles down toward your armpits by driving elbows toward your hips.
Return with control to full arm extension.

name: Unilateral Hammer Strength Pulldown
description: A unilateral version of the Hammer Strength pulldown for isolated lat work with a plate-loaded machine.
instructions: Load only one side of the Hammer Strength pulldown machine.
Sit and grip one handle, bracing the opposite side for stability.
Pull the loaded handle down toward your armpit.
Return with control and complete all reps before switching.

name: Selectorized Lat Pulldown Machine
description: A cable-stack machine pulldown designed specifically for lat development with a fixed seat and thigh pad.
instructions: Adjust the thigh pad and select the weight on the stack.
Grip the bar and sit with thighs secured.
Pull the bar to your upper chest while leaning back slightly.
Return bar to full arm extension before next rep.

name: Landmine Lat Pulldown
description: A landmine-based pulling exercise that mimics a lat pulldown with a natural arcing resistance path.
instructions: Load a barbell in a landmine attachment and kneel facing the loaded end.
Grip the end of the barbell with both hands and extend arms overhead.
Pull the bar down toward your chest in an arc.
Return with control to the overhead position.

name: Supine Barbell Lat Pull
description: A floor-based pulling exercise lying supine where a low cable or band is pulled toward the waist to train the lats horizontally.
instructions: Anchor a resistance band overhead at low height and lie on your back facing the anchor.
Grip the band with both hands with arms extended overhead.
Pull the band toward your hips, keeping arms straight and pressing your back flat.
Return slowly to the overhead stretch.

name: Suspension Trainer Lat Pulldown
description: A TRX or suspension trainer version of the pulldown performed from a standing or inclined position.
instructions: Anchor a suspension trainer overhead and grip handles with arms extended upward.
Lean back so your body forms an angle with the floor.
Pull your body upward by driving elbows down to your sides.
Extend arms back to the start under control.

name: Feet-Elevated Suspension Trainer Row
description: A suspension trainer row with the feet elevated on a bench to increase the bodyweight load on the back.
instructions: Set a suspension trainer low and place your feet on a bench.
Grip the handles with palms facing each other and hang with arms extended.
Pull your chest toward the handles by driving elbows down.
Lower under control to the starting position.

name: Close-Grip Lat Pulldown
description: A lat pulldown with a very close pronated grip that targets the lower lats and allows a deep stretch.
instructions: Attach a short straight bar to the top pulley and grip it with hands 6–8 inches apart.
Sit with thighs secured and arms fully extended overhead.
Pull the bar to your upper chest while keeping elbows pointed down.
Return slowly to full arm extension.

name: Resistance Band Lat Pulldown
description: A lat pulldown using a resistance band anchored overhead, suitable for home training.
instructions: Anchor a resistance band at the highest possible point.
Kneel below it and grip the band with both hands overhead.
Pull the band down to your chest by driving elbows toward the floor.
Slowly release to full arm extension.

name: Banded Pull-Up (Overhand)
description: An overhand pull-up with a looped resistance band providing assistance at the bottom of the range where strength is lowest.
instructions: Loop a resistance band over a pull-up bar and step both feet in.
Grip bar with a pronated grip slightly wider than shoulders.
Pull up until chin is over the bar, using the band's assistance.
Lower slowly to a full hang.

name: D-Handle Lat Pulldown
description: A lat pulldown using a single D-ring handle on a cable for a unique angle and greater range of motion per side.
instructions: Attach a D-handle to the top cable pulley.
Sit and hold the handle with one hand, arm extended overhead.
Pull the handle to the side of your chest by driving the elbow down.
Return to full extension and complete reps before switching arms.

name: Lean-Away Single-Arm Cable Pulldown
description: A single-arm cable pulldown performed while leaning laterally away to pre-stretch the working lat maximally.
instructions: Sit at a cable machine with a high pulley and grip a single handle with one hand.
Lean your torso laterally away from the cable, pre-stretching the working lat.
Pull the handle down to your hip while holding the lateral lean.
Return to the stretched position and repeat before switching sides.

name: Scapular Pull-Up
description: A lat activation drill from a dead hang where only the shoulder blades depress without bending the elbows.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with arms fully extended.
Without bending your elbows, depress your shoulder blades downward.
Rise slightly as the scapulas retract and depress.
Hold briefly then return to passive hang and repeat.

name: Chest-to-Bar Pull-Up
description: A pull-up where the goal is to pull high enough that the chest, not just the chin, makes contact with the bar.
instructions: Grip a pull-up bar with a pronated grip, slightly wider than shoulders.
From a dead hang, initiate a powerful pull by depressing the shoulder blades.
Continue pulling aggressively until your chest makes contact with the bar.
Lower with control to a full dead hang.

name: Kipping Pull-Up
description: A dynamic pull-up using hip and body momentum to increase rep speed and volume in a functional fitness context.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar and generate a forward-backward swing with the hips.
As hips swing forward, aggressively pull the bar to your chest.
At the top, push away from the bar to begin the backswing for the next rep.
Maintain rhythm and keep tension through the lat.

name: Butterfly Pull-Up
description: An advanced kipping technique using a circular motion to achieve extremely high-speed pull-up repetitions.
instructions: Hang from a bar and initiate a circular motion with the hips, going backward.
As you pass through the bottom, explosively pull toward the bar in a circular path.
Pass through the top and continue the circular movement into the next rep.
Maintain a tight, rhythmic cycle without stopping.

name: Pull-Up Isometric Hold
description: An isometric hold at the top of a pull-up position to build lat and arm endurance at peak contraction.
instructions: Pull yourself to the top of a pull-up or use a box to start there.
Hold with chin above the bar, elbows bent and lats fully contracted.
Keep shoulders away from ears and core braced throughout the hold.
Hold for the desired duration then lower slowly.

name: Eccentric Pull-Up
description: A pull-up focusing exclusively on the slow eccentric (lowering) phase to build lat strength for beginners.
instructions: Use a box or jump to start with chin over the bar.
Grip the bar with a pronated grip and begin lowering your body slowly.
Take 3–5 seconds to lower yourself to a full dead hang.
Step back onto the box and repeat.

name: Cable Lat Prayer
description: A kneeling cable exercise pulling a rope attachment downward in a prayer-like arc to engage the lats and serratus.
instructions: Set a cable pulley to the highest position and attach a rope.
Kneel facing the machine and grip the rope with palms together overhead.
Pull the rope downward in an arc to your thighs while hinging slightly at the hips.
Return to the overhead position with control.

name: EZ-Bar Pullover
description: A pullover using an EZ-bar for a more comfortable wrist position while targeting the lats.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ-bar with a narrow pronated grip above your chest.
Lower the bar in an arc behind your head toward the floor.
Feel a full stretch in the lats and long head of the triceps.
Pull back to the starting position using your lats.

name: Incline Dumbbell Pullover
description: A dumbbell pullover performed on an incline bench to adjust the stretch angle and lat involvement.
instructions: Set an incline bench to a low angle and lie back on it with a dumbbell held overhead.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head in an arc.
Hold the stretch at the bottom, feeling the lats fully engaged.
Pull back to the start using the lats.

name: Pike Pull-Up
description: A pull-up with legs held parallel to the floor in an L-sit position to maximize core and lat engagement.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar and raise your legs until they're parallel to the floor.
Hold the L-sit position and maintain it throughout all reps.
Pull your chest to the bar while keeping legs horizontal.
Lower with control without dropping the legs.

name: Prone Hip Extension Cable Pull (Lat Emphasis)
description: A floor-based cable drill lying prone and pulling a high cable to the hips to isolate the lat in extension.
instructions: Lie face down in front of a cable machine set to a high pulley.
Extend arms overhead and grip a straight bar attachment.
Pull the bar along the floor toward your hips keeping arms straight.
Return slowly to the overhead stretched position.

name: High Cable Row to Hips
description: A standing cable row from a high pulley aimed at the hips to train the lat in its primary function of shoulder extension.
instructions: Set the cable pulley to chest height or above and attach a straight bar.
Stand facing the machine and grip the bar with arms extended forward.
Pull the bar toward your hips by driving elbows back and down.
Return to the start with full arm extension.

name: Kneeling Cable Pull to Waist
description: A half-kneeling cable pull targeting the lat while requiring hip and core stability.
instructions: Set a cable to the highest position and kneel on one knee facing the machine.
Grip the handle with the arm on the same side as the forward knee.
Pull the handle down to your hip while maintaining an upright torso.
Return to full extension and repeat before switching sides.

name: Cable Lat Pull-Around
description: A standing cable exercise where the arm sweeps in a large downward arc to recruit the lat through both adduction and extension.
instructions: Set a cable to the highest position and grip a single handle.
