Stand perpendicular to the cable with working arm extended toward the pulley.
Sweep the arm downward and back in a wide arc to your hip.
Return in the same arc to the starting position.

name: Decline Bench Pullover
description: A pullover variation on a decline bench that alters the stretch mechanics and lat recruitment angle.
instructions: Secure your feet on a decline bench and lie back with a dumbbell held overhead.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head in a controlled arc.
Stop when you feel a maximal lat stretch.
Pull back using the lats to the starting position.

name: Machine Pullover
description: A dedicated pullover machine that isolates the lats through a fixed rotary arc with constant cam-adjusted resistance.
instructions: Adjust the seat height so the shoulder joint aligns with the machine's pivot point.
Place your elbows on the pads and grip the handles with arms raised overhead.
Drive the pads down through a full arc until your elbows reach hip level.
Return with control to the overhead start position.

name: Hip-Hinge Pulldown
description: A cable pulldown performed in a hip-hinged bent-over position to train the lat in shoulder extension, not just adduction.
instructions: Set the cable to the highest pulley and attach a bar.
Hip-hinge to 45 degrees and grip the bar with a pronated grip.
Pull the bar down to your thighs by extending through the shoulder.
Return with a full lat stretch overhead.

name: Wide-Grip Ring Row
description: A ring row with a wider grip that emphasizes lat width over mid-back thickness.
instructions: Set rings to waist height and grip them wide with palms facing down.
Hang below the rings with body straight from heels to shoulders.
Pull your chest up to ring height with a wide-elbow flare.
Lower under control and repeat.

name: Close-Grip Neutral Chin-Up
description: A close-grip neutral pull-up targeting the lower lats and biceps with minimal shoulder strain.
instructions: Grip a close-set neutral handle attachment with palms facing each other.
Hang at full extension with a hollow body position.
Pull your chin above the handles by driving elbows to your hips.
Lower slowly with control.

name: Smith Machine Seated Pull-Up
description: A seated pull-up regression using a fixed Smith machine bar, pulling the chest up to the bar from the floor.
instructions: Set a Smith machine bar at overhead height and sit on the floor beneath it.
Grip the bar with a supinated grip and lie back partially.
Pull your chest up toward the bar by engaging the lats.
Lower to arm extension and repeat.

name: Foot-Anchored Cable Pulldown
description: A cable pulldown performed while anchoring your feet to a stable object, allowing maximum loading without a pulldown station.
instructions: Sit on the floor below a cable pulley and anchor your feet under a stable surface.
Grip the bar overhead and maintain a tall upright posture.
Pull the bar to your chest by driving elbows downward.
Return to full arm extension with control.

name: Cable Lat Contraction Hold
description: An isometric cable drill at the peak-contracted position of a pulldown to build mind-muscle connection in the lats.
instructions: Attach a handle to a high cable and pull it down to your hip.
Hold this peak contracted position with the lat fully shortened.
Focus on squeezing the lat for the full hold duration.
Release slowly and repeat on each side.

name: Explosive Pull-Up
description: A pull-up performed explosively to develop rate of force development through the pulling muscles.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with a pronated grip.
Explode upward as fast as possible, aiming to get your chest to the bar.
Release or hold briefly at the top, allowing hands to briefly leave the bar if able.
Land safely and lower with control to the dead hang.

name: Banded Lat Stretch and Pull
description: A mobility-focused drill using a resistance band to stretch and activate the lat through its full overhead range.
instructions: Anchor a resistance band at shoulder height on a rack or door.
Grip the band with one hand and step back to feel tension.
Reach overhead and lean away from the anchor to stretch the lat.
Pull the band down toward your hip, contracting the lat fully.

name: Lat-Focused Dumbbell Row
description: A dumbbell row variation with elbows flared out to shift focus from the rhomboids toward the lat.
instructions: Place one knee and hand on a bench and hold a dumbbell in the other hand.
Let the dumbbell hang with the arm extended and elbow slightly flared out.
Row the dumbbell toward your lower ribs with the elbow sweeping outward.
Lower with control and repeat before switching sides.

name: Feet-Elevated Inverted Row
description: An inverted row with feet elevated to increase bodyweight load and target the upper and outer lats.
instructions: Set a barbell in a rack at hip height and place your feet on a bench.
Grip the bar and hang below it with your body in a straight line.
Pull your chest to the bar with elbows driving toward the hips.
Lower slowly back to full arm extension.

name: Incline-Seat Cable Pulldown
description: A cable pulldown performed with the seat reclined slightly backward to emphasize the stretch at the top of the movement.
instructions: Set a cable to the top pulley and position an adjustable bench at a slight recline beneath it.
Grip the pulldown bar and sit back on the reclined bench.
Pull the bar to your chest, maximizing the stretch-to-contraction range.
Return to full arm extension.

name: Kneeling Single-Arm Lat Press-Down
description: A kneeling single-arm cable press-down where the lat drives the arm from overhead to the side of the hip.
instructions: Set a high cable and kneel perpendicular to it.
Grip the handle with the near hand, arm extended overhead.
Keeping the arm straight, press it down toward your hip by contracting the lat.
Return to the stretched overhead position and repeat.

name: Wide-Grip Pulldown to Chest
description: The most common wide-grip lat pulldown variation, bringing the bar to the upper chest with elbows driving toward the floor.
instructions: Grip a lat pulldown bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Sit with thighs secured under the pad and lean back to 10 degrees.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, squeezing the lats at the bottom.
Return to full arm extension with controlled tempo.

name: Alternating Cable Pulldown
description: A two-cable pulldown alternating arms to provide a unilateral stimulus while training bilaterally.
instructions: Attach two handles to two separate high cable pulleys.
Sit between or in front of the two pulleys, gripping one handle in each hand.
Pull one handle down to your shoulder while the other extends overhead.
Alternate in a controlled rhythm.

name: Wide Supinated-Grip Pulldown
description: A wide-grip pulldown with palms supinated to engage the lower lats and increase bicep stretch.
instructions: Grip a straight pulldown bar wide with palms facing toward you.
Sit with thighs secured and arms extended overhead.
Pull the bar to the upper chest with a slight torso lean back.
Slowly return to full extension.

name: Feet-Assisted Chin-Up
description: A modified chin-up with feet elevated on a surface to reduce load for beginners working toward full chin-ups.
instructions: Place a bench under a pull-up bar and rest your feet on it.
Grip the bar with a supinated close grip and hold your body diagonally.
Pull your chin above the bar by driving elbows toward your hips.
Lower back to full extension.

name: Underhand Barbell Row
description: A bentover barbell row with a supinated grip to shift emphasis from the traps to the lower lats.
instructions: Grip a barbell with a supinated (underhand) grip at shoulder width.
Hip-hinge to approximately 45 degrees.
Row the bar toward your lower abdomen, driving elbows tight to your sides.
Return to full arm extension and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Cable Row to Hip
description: A single-arm cable row aimed at the hip rather than the chest, focusing on lat extension over rhomboid retraction.
instructions: Set a cable pulley to mid height and attach a single handle.
Stand facing the machine and grip the handle with one hand.
Row the handle toward your hip, keeping the elbow close to the body.
Return with a full stretch and repeat before switching sides.

name: Seated Close-Grip Pulldown Machine
description: A machine-based close-grip pulldown that targets the lower lats with a fixed movement arc.
instructions: Select weight and adjust the thigh pads on the pulldown machine.
Use a close grip attachment and extend arms overhead.
Pull the attachment to your upper chest by driving elbows toward hips.
Extend arms back to full stretch.

name: Split-Stance Cable Pulldown
description: A standing cable pulldown in a split stance to add core and anti-rotation demands to the lat pulldown pattern.
instructions: Set a cable to the highest pulley and grip a straight bar.
Stand in a split stance (one foot forward) below the cable.
Pull the bar to your chest while maintaining a stable split stance.
Return to overhead and repeat.

name: Decline-Bench Cable Pulldown
description: A pulldown performed while lying on a decline bench to limit momentum and force pure lat engagement.
instructions: Position a decline bench under a cable station set to the top pulley.
Secure feet and lie back on the decline with arms extended toward the cable.
Pull the bar to your chest, focusing entirely on lat engagement.
Return to the overhead stretched position.

name: Hanging Lat Shrug
description: A drill from a dead hang where the shoulder blades depress alternately to activate lats independently.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar in a dead hang.
Depress one shoulder blade downward without bending that elbow.
Hold briefly and feel the lat contract on that side.
Alternate sides in a controlled rhythm.

name: Knee-Tuck Pull-Up
description: A pull-up variation where the knees are tucked to the chest at the top to increase core and lat demand.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with a pronated grip.
Pull yourself up while simultaneously tucking your knees to your chest.
Hold briefly at the top with chin over bar and knees tucked.
Lower legs and body simultaneously back to the dead hang.

name: Dumbbell Lat Swing
description: A controlled dumbbell swinging motion from overhead to the hip to build lat strength in shoulder extension.
instructions: Stand tall and hold a light dumbbell in one hand with arm extended overhead.
Keeping the arm nearly straight, sweep the dumbbell down toward your hip.
Reverse the motion back to overhead stretch with lat control.
Repeat before switching sides.

name: Single-Arm Suspension Trainer Row
description: A unilateral suspension trainer pull that challenges each side of the back with anti-rotation control.
instructions: Set a suspension trainer above head height and grip one handle with one hand.
Hang below the anchor with arm extended and feet on the floor as needed.
Pull your shoulder to the handle height using only the working arm.
Lower with control and complete reps before switching sides.

name: Functional Trainer Pulldown
description: A lat pulldown performed on a functional trainer using both cables simultaneously for symmetrical lat development.
instructions: Set both cables on a functional trainer to the highest position.
Kneel in the center and grip a handle in each hand.
Pull both handles simultaneously to shoulder level by driving elbows down.
Return slowly to the fully stretched overhead position.

name: Weighted Chin-Up
description: A supinated-grip chin-up with added weight for progressive overload on the lats and biceps.
instructions: Attach a dip belt with a weight plate and put it on.
Grip a pull-up bar shoulder-width with palms facing you.
Pull your chin above the bar from a dead hang.
Lower with control to full arm extension.

name: Floor Pike Lat Pullover
description: An ab-wheel or barbell rollout focusing on the lat's role in pulling the torso back to the pike position.
instructions: Kneel on the floor and hold an ab wheel with both hands.
Roll forward slowly until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Using the lats, pull the wheel back toward your knees.
Stop in the starting position and repeat.

name: Overhead Slam (Lat Focus)
description: A medicine ball overhead slam that uses explosive lat contraction for shoulder extension power training.
instructions: Hold a slam ball overhead with arms fully extended.
Engage the lats and explosively drive the ball downward to the floor.
Follow through the arc to full lat contraction at the hips.
Pick up the ball, reset, and repeat.

name: Cable Behind-the-Back Lat Pull
description: A cable pull from a low pulley behind the body to target the lat in shoulder hyperextension.
instructions: Set a low cable pulley and stand with your back to the machine.
Reach behind and grip the handle, arm extended behind your body.
Pull the handle forward and up toward your hip in a sweeping arc.
Return with control and repeat before switching sides.

name: Wide-Elbow Barbell Row
description: A bent-over barbell row with elbows flared wide and the bar pulled to the upper chest to target the upper back and rear delts.
instructions: Grip a barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width with a pronated grip.
Hip-hinge to 45 degrees with a flat back.
Row the bar to your upper chest with elbows flaring out to the sides.
Lower under control back to arm extension.

name: Cable Lat Pull with External Rotation
description: A cable pulldown combined with a shoulder external rotation to co-activate the lat and rotator cuff.
instructions: Attach a rope to the high cable and grip each end.
Pull the rope down toward your chest and simultaneously spread the ends outward.
At the bottom, externally rotate your shoulders so hands face upward.
Return with control to the overhead position.

name: Inverted Row
description: A bodyweight row using a pronated grip to increase lat involvement compared to a supinated row.
instructions: Set a barbell at hip height in a rack and lie beneath it.
Grip the bar pronated at shoulder width and hang with body straight.
Pull your chest to the bar with elbows sweeping outward.
Lower to full arm extension and repeat.

name: Single-Arm Cable Lat Stretch
description: A passive to active stretch using a cable for improving lat range of motion and activation.
instructions: Set a cable to the highest position and grip the handle with one hand.
Step away from the machine so the cable is taut with arm raised overhead.
Lean into the stretch, allowing the lat to lengthen fully.
Actively contract the lat to return the arm to your side.

name: Dual Cable Straight-Arm Pulldown
description: A straight-arm pulldown using both cables of a functional trainer simultaneously for balanced lat work.
instructions: Set both pulleys to the highest position and grip a handle in each hand.
Stand with slight forward lean and arms extended overhead.
Keep arms straight and pull both handles down to your thighs using the lats.
Return slowly to the overhead stretch.

name: Isometric Barbell Lat Hold
description: An isometric barbell hold in the contracted position of a row to build lat strength at peak contraction.
instructions: Grip a barbell in a bentover row position, bar pulled to your abdomen.
Hold this contracted position isometrically with lats fully engaged.
Keep breathing and brace the core for the full hold.
Lower the bar and reset before the next hold.

name: Wall-Assisted Active Lat Stretch
description: A wall-based active stretch that opens the lat and builds shoulder flexion mobility.
instructions: Stand beside a wall and extend one arm to press the hand flat against it.
Rotate your body away from the wall to stretch the lat.
Hold and breathe into the stretch.
Actively attempt to pull the arm away from the wall to engage the lat.

name: Crossover Cable Lat Pull
description: A cable pull where one arm reaches across the body overhead and pulls to the opposite hip, creating a diagonal lat activation.
instructions: Set a cable to the highest pulley and stand perpendicular to it.
Reach the far arm across your body to grip the handle overhead.
Pull in a diagonal arc from overhead-opposite to hip-same side.
Return slowly and repeat before switching.

name: Prone Lat Activation
description: A floor drill lying prone using a light cable or band to isolate lat activation before heavier pulling.
instructions: Lie prone on the floor with one arm extended overhead holding a band anchored ahead.
Keeping the arm straight, pull it down to your side using the lat.
Squeeze the lat hard in the contracted position.
Return with control and repeat before switching sides.

name: Rotating Pull-Up
description: A pull-up where the body rotates toward one side at the top to increase unilateral lat engagement.
instructions: Grip a pull-up bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Pull upward and rotate your torso so one shoulder leads to the bar.
Lower and rotate to the other side on the next rep.
Alternate rotations each rep.

name: Prone Banded Lat Pulldown
description: A band-resisted pulldown performed face-down on a bench to eliminate momentum and isolate the lats.
instructions: Anchor a band overhead and lie prone on a bench positioned below it.
Reach overhead and grip the band with both hands.
Pull the band toward your chest by driving elbows toward your hips.
Return to the overhead position and repeat.

name: Wide Neutral-Grip Pulldown
description: A lat pulldown using a bar with neutral-grip handles, reducing wrist and elbow stress while targeting the lats.
instructions: Attach a neutral-grip bar to the top cable pulley.
Sit at the station with thighs secured and arms fully extended.
Pull the bar toward your upper chest with palms facing each other.
Slowly return to the fully extended position.

name: Cable Lat Fly
description: A cable fly in the sagittal plane with straight arms pulling from overhead to the sides, mimicking a bodybuilding lat spread.
instructions: Set both pulleys overhead on a functional trainer.
Grip a handle in each hand with arms extended overhead.
Sweep both arms downward and outward in a wide arc to your sides.
Return slowly to the overhead stretch.

name: Lat-Focused Machine Row
description: A machine row with elbows tucked close and pulling angle aimed lower to shift stress from rhomboids to lats.
instructions: Adjust the machine for a lower pull angle and use a close neutral grip.
Sit upright and let arms extend fully toward the machine.
Row handles toward your lower ribs with elbows hugging your sides.
Return with full arm extension.

name: Supine Floor Cable Pulldown
description: A floor-based supine cable pulldown for complete elimination of momentum and strict lat training.
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor directly under a cable machine high pulley.
Reach overhead and grip the bar with a pronated grip.
Pull the bar to your chest by driving elbows to the floor.
Return slowly to the overhead position.

name: Barbell-Assisted Behind-Neck Pull-Up
description: A guided behind-the-neck pull-up using a Smith machine bar to safely target the upper lats at a different angle.
instructions: Set a Smith machine bar at a height above your head.
Grip the bar wide and hang beneath it with feet on the floor for support.
Pull your neck toward the bar, leading with the back of the head.
Lower under control and repeat.

name: Half-Kneeling Lat Pulldown
description: A lat pulldown from a half-kneeling position to develop single-leg stability and unilateral lat engagement.
instructions: Kneel on one knee facing a high cable pulley with the opposite foot forward.
Grip a handle with the same-side hand as the kneeling knee.
Pull the handle to your shoulder by driving the elbow down.
Return to full arm extension and complete reps before switching sides.

name: Rope Climb
description: A traditional vertical rope climb that maximally loads the lats in a compound pulling movement.
instructions: Grip the rope above your head with both hands.
Pull down with one hand while reaching up with the other.
Use the lat on each side alternately to drive yourself up.
Descend with control using a foot-wrap technique.

name: Battle Rope Lat Pull
description: A battle rope variation pulling the rope downward from overhead to train explosive lat endurance.
instructions: Anchor battle ropes above head height and grip both ends.
Stand with a slight forward lean and arms extended overhead.
Rapidly pull both ropes downward to hip level using the lats.
Return to overhead and repeat in rapid succession.

name: One-Arm Row with Lat Bias
description: A dumbbell row performed with the elbow path directed toward the hip to maximize lat activation over traps.
instructions: Place one hand and knee on a flat bench for support.
Hold a dumbbell in the opposite hand and allow it to hang below the shoulder.
Row the dumbbell toward your hip, keeping the elbow close to the torso.
Lower back to full extension and repeat before switching sides.

name: Table-Supported Lat Row
description: A bodyweight row using a sturdy table for resistance, pulling the chest toward the underside of the table.
instructions: Lie under a sturdy table and grip the edge with both hands.
Keep your body straight from heels to shoulders.
Pull your chest up to the table by driving elbows toward your hips.
Lower slowly to full arm extension.

name: Stiff-Arm Dumbbell Row
description: A dumbbell row with a straight arm, emphasizing the lat as a shoulder extensor rather than a scapula retractor.
instructions: Stand with a slight forward lean and hold a dumbbell in one hand, arm extended.
Keep the arm straight and row the dumbbell toward your hip by contracting the lat.
At the top, feel the full lat contraction with the arm beside your body.
Lower to the stretched position and repeat before switching sides.

name: Single-Arm Behind-Neck Pulldown
description: A unilateral cable pulldown where the handle is pulled to the back of the head for a unique lat angle.
instructions: Sit at a cable machine with a high single-handle attachment.
Grip with one hand and reach across the body slightly overhead.
Pull the handle to behind your ear while turning your head slightly away.
Return to the overhead stretch and repeat before switching sides.

name: Lying Face-Up Lat Pulldown
description: A lat pulldown performed lying supine on a bench to completely remove trunk stabilization and isolate lat mechanics.
instructions: Position a bench lengthwise under a cable machine high pulley.
Lie face-up on the bench and grip the pulldown bar overhead.
Pull the bar to your chest, keeping your back flat on the bench.
Return to full arm extension with controlled tempo.

name: Close-Grip Supinated Pull-Up
description: A close-grip chin-up with hands just inches apart to deeply work the lower lat through a full range of motion.
instructions: Grip a pull-up bar with hands 6 inches apart and palms facing you.
Hang at full arm extension with shoulders depressed.
Pull your chin over the bar by driving elbows down and together.
Lower to full arm extension.

name: Barbell Dead Hang
description: A passive hang from a barbell to develop grip endurance and decompress the spine under load.
instructions: Set a barbell in a power rack at a height that allows a full hang.
Grip the bar with a pronated grip and lift your feet off the floor.
Allow your body to hang completely, relaxing through the spine.
Hold for the desired time then step down.

name: Back Squat
description: A classic barbell squat that heavily loads the quads through a full standing squat pattern.
instructions: Set the bar across your upper back and brace your trunk.
Sit down into the squat while keeping your chest up.
Drive your knees forward and keep your feet planted.
Stand back up until your hips and knees lock out.

name: Box Squat
description: A back squat performed to a box, teaching depth control and building explosive hip drive out of the hole.
instructions: Set a box or bench at or just below parallel depth behind you.
Sit back onto the box under control, keeping your shins vertical.
Pause briefly without relaxing your trunk.
Drive up explosively through your whole foot.

name: Pause Back Squat
description: A back squat with a deliberate pause in the bottom position to build positional strength and control.
instructions: Squat to full depth and hold a strict 2-3 second pause.
Stay braced and keep the bar over mid-foot during the pause.
Drive up without bouncing or relaxing at the bottom.
Use less weight than your regular squat.

name: Overhead Squat
description: A full squat performed while holding the bar locked out overhead, demanding exceptional mobility and trunk stability.
instructions: Hold the bar overhead with a wide snatch grip and locked elbows.
Squat down while keeping the bar stacked over your mid-foot.
Push up against the bar the entire time.
Stand tall without letting the bar drift forward.

name: Barbell Thruster
description: A front squat flowing directly into an overhead press, taxing the legs, shoulders, and conditioning in one movement.
instructions: Front squat to full depth with the bar in the rack position.
Drive up hard and use the momentum to press the bar overhead.
Lock out overhead, then lower back to the rack position.
Keep your heels down and trunk braced throughout.

name: Clean and Jerk
description: The Olympic lift: clean the bar to the shoulders, then jerk it overhead. Demands power, mobility, and practiced technique.
instructions: Clean the bar explosively from the floor to the front rack.
Stand tall, reset your breath, and dip with a vertical torso.
Drive the bar overhead and lock out in a split or power stance.
Learn this lift with a coach before loading it heavy.

name: Front Squat
description: A front-loaded squat that emphasizes knee flexion and quad demand.
instructions: Rack the bar on the front of your shoulders with elbows high.
Lower into a deep squat with an upright torso.
Keep your whole foot down and knees tracking forward.
Drive up smoothly to return to standing.

name: Goblet Squat
description: A simple front-loaded squat that keeps the torso upright and the quads working hard.
instructions: Hold one dumbbell close to your chest.
Squat down between your hips with your chest tall.
Let your knees travel naturally as you stay balanced.
Push through your feet to stand back up.

name: Zercher Squat
description: A squat performed with the bar held in the elbows for a demanding front-loaded quad pattern.
instructions: Cradle the bar in the crooks of your elbows and brace hard.
Lower into the squat while keeping the torso upright.
Stay balanced over midfoot as your knees bend deeply.
Stand up strongly and re-brace at the top.

name: Hatfield Squat
description: A safety bar squat performed with hand support that allows stable deep quad-focused loading.
instructions: Set the safety bar across your shoulders and lightly hold the rack or rails.
Lower into a deep squat while staying upright and balanced.
Keep your feet planted as your knees travel forward freely.
Drive up hard through the floor while using the hands only for support.

name: Safety Bar Squat
description: A squat variation using a safety bar that lets many lifters stay more upright and quad-focused.
instructions: Set the safety bar securely across your shoulders.
Brace and squat down with your chest tall.
Keep your feet rooted as your knees and hips bend together.
Drive upward until you are fully standing again.

name: Smith Machine Squat
description: A guided bar squat that provides extra stability while still training the quads hard.
instructions: Stand under the Smith bar with it resting across your upper back.
Unlock the bar and lower into a controlled squat.
Keep pressure through your feet as your knees bend.
Push back up and re-rack the bar at the top.

name: Landmine Squat
description: A front-loaded squat using a landmine that naturally encourages an upright torso.
instructions: Hold the end of the barbell at chest height with both hands.
Sit down into the squat while keeping your torso tall.
Keep the bar close to your body and your heels down.
Drive through the floor to stand up.

name: Machine Hack Squat
description: A supported machine squat that allows heavy quad loading with a fixed path.
instructions: Set your shoulders under the pads and place your feet on the platform.
Unlock the machine and lower until your knees are deeply bent.
Keep your hips against the pad as you descend.
Press the platform away to stand back up.

name: Barbell Hack Squat
description: A barbell squat from behind the legs that shifts tension strongly into the quads.
instructions: Stand with the barbell behind your legs and grip it firmly.
Squat down while keeping your chest lifted and balance centered.
Drive through your feet to lift the bar as you stand.
Lower the bar back under control for the next rep.

name: Pendulum Squat
description: A machine squat with a swinging arm that creates a very strong quad-biased resistance curve.
instructions: Set your back and shoulders firmly against the machine pads.
Lower into the squat with control as the arm swings down.
Keep your feet planted and knees tracking smoothly.
Drive the platform up until you return to the start.

name: Belt Squat
description: A squat loaded at the hips that trains the quads hard with less spinal loading.
instructions: Attach the belt securely and step onto the platform.
Brace and squat down while staying tall through the torso.
Let your knees bend freely as you keep pressure through your feet.
Stand back up and control the load at the top.

name: Cable Belt Squat
description: A belt squat done on a cable stack that provides smooth constant tension to the quads.
instructions: Clip a dip belt to a low cable and stand on stable blocks or a platform.
Step back to create tension and brace your torso.
Squat down under control while keeping your chest tall.
Stand up smoothly against the cable resistance.

name: Lever Squat
description: A plate-loaded squat machine that combines stability with heavy quad-focused loading.
instructions: Set your shoulders under the machine pads and feet on the platform.
Lower into the squat with control and full range.
Keep even pressure through both feet as you descend.
Drive back up until the machine returns to the start.

name: Single-Leg Belt Squat
description: A one-leg belt squat that challenges the quads with high stability and reduced spinal loading.
instructions: Attach the belt and stand tall on one working leg with the other leg unloaded.
Lower into a controlled single-leg squat while keeping the torso steady.
Let the working knee bend deeply without losing foot pressure.
Stand back up through the same leg and reset before the next rep.

name: Double Kettlebell Front Squat
description: A front squat with two kettlebells that challenges the quads and trunk together.
instructions: Rack two kettlebells on the front of your shoulders.
Lower into a squat with your elbows kept high.
Keep your trunk braced and feet flat through the rep.
Drive up to standing and reset your breath.

name: Dumbbell Front Squat
description: A front-loaded squat with dumbbells that keeps the movement upright and quad-dominant.
instructions: Hold two dumbbells at shoulder level in a front-rack position.
Squat down while keeping your chest lifted.
Let your knees bend deeply as you stay balanced over midfoot.
Stand up strongly and keep the dumbbells stable.

name: Sandbag Front Squat
description: A front squat using a sandbag that adds an unstable front-loaded challenge to the quads.
instructions: Hug the sandbag high against your chest.
Lower into a squat while keeping the bag secure.
Stay tall through the torso and keep your feet flat.
Drive up to standing without letting the bag slip.

name: Sissy Squat
description: A knee-dominant bodyweight squat that isolates the quads through a long range of knee flexion.
instructions: Stand tall and lightly hold support if needed.
Let your knees travel forward as your torso leans back.
Lower until your quads are fully loaded without losing control.
Push through the balls and midfoot to return upright.

name: Spanish Squat
description: A supported squat using a strap or band behind the knees to heavily target the quads.
instructions: Set a strong band or strap behind both knees and step back into it.
Sit straight down while staying upright through the torso.
Keep tension on the band as your knees bend forward.
Stand back up while maintaining control of the setup.

name: Split Squat
description: A stationary staggered-stance squat that loads the front leg quads heavily.
instructions: Take a long split stance with your front foot planted firmly.
Lower your back knee toward the floor under control.
Keep most of your weight over the front leg as you descend.
Drive through the front foot to rise back up.

name: Dumbbell Split Squat
description: A split squat loaded at the sides to build quad strength one leg at a time.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and step into a split stance.
Drop your back knee straight down with control.
Stay tall and load the front leg through the full range.
Push through the front foot to return to the top.

name: Barbell Split Squat
description: A barbell split squat that allows heavier unilateral quad loading.
instructions: Place the bar across your upper back and step into a split stance.
Lower down until the front knee is deeply bent.
Keep your torso steady and your front heel planted.
Stand back up by driving through the front leg.

name: Goblet Split Squat
description: A front-loaded split squat that helps keep posture upright and the quads engaged.
instructions: Hold one weight close to your chest and set your split stance.
Lower under control until your back knee nears the floor.
Keep your torso upright and your front foot fully grounded.
Drive up through the front leg to stand tall again.

name: Front Rack Split Squat
description: A split squat with the load racked in front to increase trunk demand and quad bias.
instructions: Rack the weight at the front of your shoulders and take a split stance.
Lower straight down while keeping the elbows lifted.
Stay centered over the front leg throughout the rep.
Press through the front foot to come back up.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
description: A rear-foot-supported split squat that strongly challenges the front leg quads.
instructions: Place your back foot on a bench and set your front foot far enough forward.
Lower into the split squat with control.
Keep the front foot flat and the torso slightly forward but stable.
Drive through the front leg to return to the start.

name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
description: A loaded Bulgarian split squat that builds strong quads with a simple setup.
instructions: Hold dumbbells at your sides and elevate your back foot on a bench.
Lower until the front leg reaches a deep bend.
Keep tension on the front quad and stay balanced.
Drive back up through the front foot.

name: Barbell Bulgarian Split Squat
description: A barbell Bulgarian split squat for heavier unilateral quad work.
instructions: Set a bar on your upper back and elevate your rear foot on a bench.
Lower into the rep with full control.
Keep your front knee moving freely while your foot stays planted.
Stand up by pushing hard through the front leg.

name: Smith Machine Bulgarian Split Squat
description: A guided Bulgarian split squat that adds stability and consistent loading.
instructions: Set the bar on your upper back and place your rear foot on a bench.
Unlock the Smith bar and lower into the split squat.
Keep your torso controlled and front foot rooted.
Push back up and re-rack once the set is done.

name: Landmine Split Squat
description: A split squat using a landmine to create a stable front-loaded quad pattern.
instructions: Hold the end of the landmine bar at chest level and step into a split stance.
Lower straight down under control.
Keep the weight close as the front knee bends deeply.
Drive up through the front foot to finish the rep.

name: Front-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
description: A split squat with the front foot raised to increase knee travel and quad range.
instructions: Place your front foot on a small platform and step into your split stance.
Lower until your front knee bends through a long range.
Keep the front foot stable and the torso controlled.
Stand back up by pushing through the elevated front foot.

name: Dumbbell Front-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
description: A loaded front-foot-elevated split squat that emphasizes deep quad loading.
instructions: Hold dumbbells at your sides and elevate the front foot slightly.
Lower into the split squat with a long controlled range.
Let the front knee travel forward while staying balanced.
Drive back up through the front leg.

name: Cable Split Squat
description: A split squat against cable resistance that keeps constant tension on the quads.
instructions: Set the cable low and hold the handle at your chest or sides.
Step into a split stance and create steady tension.
Lower under control while keeping the front foot rooted.
Drive back up against the cable resistance.

name: Suspension Trainer Split Squat
description: A supported split squat that helps beginners train quad-dominant single-leg strength.
instructions: Hold the suspension trainer handles and step into a split stance.
Lower your body straight down while using the straps only for balance.
Keep the front leg doing most of the work.
Drive through the front foot to rise back up.

name: Safety Bar Split Squat
description: A split squat using a safety bar to allow heavy loading with stable upper-body position.
instructions: Set the safety bar across your shoulders and take a split stance.
Lower down until the front leg reaches a deep bend.
Keep your trunk braced and centered over the front foot.
Stand up strongly through the front leg.

name: Forward Lunge
description: A basic stepping lunge that trains quad strength and control one side at a time.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet under your hips.
Step forward and lower until both knees are bent.
Keep your front foot planted and your torso steady.
Push back to the start and repeat on the same or opposite side.

name: Dumbbell Forward Lunge
description: A forward lunge loaded at the sides for straightforward quad-focused unilateral work.
instructions: Hold dumbbells at your sides and stand tall.
Step forward into a controlled lunge.
Lower until the front knee is deeply bent and stable.
Push back to standing through the front foot.

name: Barbell Forward Lunge
description: A barbell forward lunge that allows heavier loading through the quad-dominant front leg.
instructions: Set the bar on your upper back and brace your torso.
Step forward and lower with control.
Keep your balance centered over the front foot.
Drive back to the starting stance.

name: Reverse Lunge
description: A lunge stepping backward that trains the front leg quads with controlled balance demands.
instructions: Stand tall and step one leg back behind you.
Lower until the front knee bends deeply under control.
Keep your torso upright and your front foot fully planted.
Drive through the front foot to return to standing.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
description: A reverse lunge with dumbbells that is easy to load and simple to perform.
instructions: Hold dumbbells at your sides and brace lightly.
Step one leg back into a long lunge.
Lower under control while the front leg stays stable.
Push through the front foot to stand back up.

name: Barbell Reverse Lunge
description: A reverse lunge with a barbell that supports heavier unilateral quad loading.
instructions: Place the bar across your upper back and stand tall.
Step back and lower into the lunge slowly.
Keep your front foot flat and knee tracking naturally.
Drive upward and bring the rear foot back in.

name: Front Rack Reverse Lunge
description: A reverse lunge with the weight racked in front to increase trunk stiffness and quad demand.
instructions: Rack the weight on the front of your shoulders.
Step one leg back into a controlled lunge.
Stay tall through the torso as the front knee bends.
Push through the front foot to return to the start.

name: Landmine Reverse Lunge
description: A reverse lunge using a landmine for a stable front-loaded resistance path.
instructions: Hold the end of the landmine bar at chest level.
Step back into the lunge while keeping the load close.
Lower under control until both knees are bent.
Drive through the front foot to stand tall again.

name: Smith Machine Reverse Lunge
description: A guided reverse lunge that adds balance support and steady loading.
instructions: Set the Smith bar on your upper back and stand under it securely.
Step one leg back and lower into the lunge.
Keep the front foot grounded and the torso under control.
Push through the front leg to return to the start.

name: Walking Lunge
description: A continuous lunge pattern that trains the quads while moving forward with each step.
instructions: Stand tall and step forward into your first lunge.
Lower under control and drive through the front foot.
Bring the rear leg through into the next step.
Continue alternating sides with smooth forward movement.

name: Dumbbell Walking Lunge
description: A loaded walking lunge that combines quad strength with coordination and control.
instructions: Hold dumbbells at your sides and stand tall.
Step forward into a controlled lunge and lower deeply.
Drive through the front foot and bring the rear leg through.
Keep moving forward with alternating steps.

name: Barbell Walking Lunge
description: A barbell walking lunge that allows heavy quad-focused loading over repeated steps.
instructions: Set the bar on your upper back and brace firmly.
Take a long step forward and lower into the lunge.
Push through the front foot and continue into the next step.
Maintain balance and posture as you walk forward.

name: Front Rack Walking Lunge
description: A walking lunge with the load in front that keeps the torso upright and quads engaged.
instructions: Rack the load at the front of your shoulders and brace hard.
Step forward into a deep lunge.
Drive up through the front foot and continue walking.
Keep your elbows lifted and torso stacked throughout.

name: Deficit Reverse Lunge
description: A reverse lunge from a small platform that increases knee range and front-leg quad demand.
instructions: Stand on a small platform with both feet balanced at the start.
Step one leg back off the platform and lower into a reverse lunge.
Keep the front foot flat as the front knee bends through a long range.
Drive through the front foot to return to the platform.

name: Slider Reverse Lunge
description: A reverse lunge with the rear foot on a slider for smooth constant tension on the front leg.
instructions: Stand with one foot on a slider and one foot planted.
Slide the rear foot back as you lower into the lunge.
Keep most of your weight on the front leg.
Pull the rear foot back in as you stand up.

name: Step-Up
description: A classic unilateral leg exercise that targets the quads by stepping onto a raised surface.
instructions: Place one foot firmly on a box or step.
Lean slightly over the working leg and drive upward.
Bring the trailing foot onto the platform if desired.
Step back down under control and repeat.

name: Dumbbell Step-Up
description: A loaded step-up that makes the front leg quads work hard through the ascent.
instructions: Hold dumbbells at your sides and place one foot on the box.
Drive through the working leg to rise up.
Keep the planted foot doing most of the work.
Lower back down slowly before the next rep.

name: Barbell Step-Up
description: A barbell step-up for heavier unilateral quad training on a box or bench.
instructions: Set the bar on your upper back and place one foot on the box.
Press through the working foot to stand on the platform.
Avoid pushing hard off the trailing foot.
Step down under control and repeat.

name: Goblet Step-Up
description: A front-loaded step-up that helps maintain upright posture while training the quads.
instructions: Hold one weight close to your chest and plant one foot on the step.
Drive up through the working leg until you are tall on the box.
Keep the load close and your torso steady.
Lower with control to the floor.

name: Front Rack Step-Up
description: A step-up with the load racked in front to add trunk demand and quad emphasis.
instructions: Rack the weight on the front of your shoulders and place one foot on the box.
Drive through that leg to stand up.
Keep your torso stacked and elbows lifted.
Step back down slowly to reset.

name: Kettlebell Step-Up
description: A step-up using kettlebells that challenges single-leg control and quad strength.
instructions: Hold kettlebells securely and plant one foot on the step.
Push through the working leg to rise onto the box.
Balance at the top without rushing the movement.
Lower yourself back down in control.

name: High Box Step-Up
description: A step-up onto a taller box that increases knee flexion and quad demand.
instructions: Use a box height that creates a deep bend in the working knee.
Plant one foot fully on the box and brace.
Drive upward without jumping off the floor.
Lower back down slowly and repeat on the same side.

name: Step-Up to Knee Drive
description: A step-up that finishes with the free knee driving up for extra balance and control demand.
instructions: Place one foot on the box and brace lightly.
Drive up through the working leg and lift the free knee at the top.
Balance briefly without collapsing on the standing leg.
Lower back down with control to reset.

name: Smith Machine Step-Up
description: A guided step-up that adds stability while allowing steady loading.
instructions: Set the Smith bar across your upper back and place one foot on the box.
Drive through the working leg to stand up.
Keep the guided bar path smooth and controlled.
Step back down carefully before the next rep.

name: Cable Step-Up
description: A step-up against cable resistance that keeps tension on the quads throughout the movement.
instructions: Attach the cable and place one foot on the step while holding the handle securely.
Drive up through the working leg against the cable pull.
Stay balanced and keep the torso under control.
Lower back down slowly without losing tension.

name: Landmine Step-Up
description: A front-loaded step-up using a landmine for a stable and easy-to-control resistance path.
instructions: Hold the end of the landmine bar at chest level and place one foot on the box.
Press through the working foot to rise up.
Keep the load close to your body throughout the rep.
Step back down under control and repeat.

name: Step-Down
description: A controlled lowering drill from a box that strengthens the quads through eccentric knee control.
instructions: Stand on a box with one foot near the edge.
Slowly bend the stance knee and lower the free heel toward the floor.
Keep the working knee tracking smoothly as you descend.
Stand back tall on the box to complete the rep.

name: Weighted Step-Down
description: A loaded step-down that challenges the quads through a longer controlled lowering phase.
instructions: Hold light dumbbells and stand on a box with one foot near the edge.
Lower yourself slowly by bending the stance knee.
Tap the free heel lightly if mobility allows.
Drive back up through the working leg to return to the top.

name: Forward Step-Down
description: A forward-facing step-down that builds strong quad control during descent.
instructions: Stand on a box facing forward with one foot at the edge.
Lower the free foot toward the floor in front of you.
Control the movement through the working knee and hip.
Stand back up on the box to finish the rep.

name: Peterson Step-Down
description: A quad-focused step-down done from a small platform with strong knee travel over the toes.
instructions: Stand on a small step with the free heel hanging off the edge.
Drive the working knee forward as you lower the free heel toward the floor.
Keep the working foot flat and the movement smooth.
Stand back up through the same leg without bouncing.

name: Poliquin Step-Up
description: A high-knee-over-toe step-up variation designed to target the quads through a long range.
instructions: Stand close to a low step and place one foot on it.
Let the front knee travel forward as you step up smoothly.
Keep the trailing foot light so the front leg does the work.
Lower slowly and repeat on the same side.

name: Pistol Squat
description: A full-range single-leg squat that places a very high demand on the working leg quads.
instructions: Stand on one leg with the other leg held in front.
Sit down under control while keeping the working foot planted.
Lower as far as you can without losing balance.
Drive back up through the working leg to stand tall.

name: Assisted Pistol Squat
description: A supported pistol squat that helps lifters learn single-leg quad strength and balance.
instructions: Hold a stable support lightly and stand on one leg.
Lower into the pistol squat under control.
Use only enough assistance to stay balanced.
Press through the working foot to stand back up.

name: Pistol Squat to Box
description: A single-leg squat to a box that reduces range while preserving the quad-focused pattern.
instructions: Stand on one leg in front of a box or bench.
Lower yourself until you lightly touch the box.
Keep the working foot flat and the nonworking leg off the floor.
Stand back up through the same leg.

name: Skater Squat
description: A rear-reaching single-leg squat that trains the quads with a compact bodyweight setup.
instructions: Stand on one leg and bend the other leg behind you.
Lower down while reaching the rear knee toward the floor.
Keep your balance centered over the working foot.
Drive through the working leg to return upright.

name: Assisted Skater Squat
description: A supported skater squat that makes single-leg quad training more accessible.
instructions: Hold a support lightly and stand on one leg.
Lower into the skater squat with the rear leg reaching behind.
Use just enough assistance to stay controlled.
Push through the working foot to stand up again.

name: Shrimp Squat
description: A challenging single-leg squat with the rear foot held behind the body.
instructions: Stand on one leg and hold the other foot behind you if able.
Lower slowly while keeping your chest lifted.
Balance over the working foot as your knee bends deeply.
Drive up through the stance leg to return to standing.

name: Assisted Shrimp Squat
description: A supported shrimp squat that lets you practice deep single-leg quad loading safely.
instructions: Lightly hold a support and stand on one leg.
Lower into the shrimp squat with control.
Use the support only to help balance and stay upright.
Press through the working foot to rise back up.

name: Single-Leg Hack Squat
description: A one-leg hack squat machine variation that isolates the working quad with a fixed path.
instructions: Set one foot on the platform and keep the other leg out of the working path.
Unlock the machine and lower under control through the working leg.
Keep the foot flat and the hips against the pad as the knee bends.
Press the platform away through the same leg to return to the top.

name: Suspension Trainer Pistol Squat
description: A pistol squat using straps for balance assistance and cleaner reps.
instructions: Hold the suspension trainer handles and stand on one leg.
Lower into the pistol squat while keeping tension in the straps.
Use the straps only to assist balance and range.
Drive through the working foot to return upright.

name: Counterbalance Pistol Squat
description: A pistol squat holding a light weight forward to improve balance and keep the torso upright.
instructions: Hold a light plate straight out in front and stand on one leg.
Lower into the pistol squat while reaching the load slightly forward.
Stay balanced over the working foot throughout the rep.
Drive back up to standing with control.

name: Seated Leg Extension
description: A machine isolation exercise that directly trains knee extension and the quads.
instructions: Adjust the seat so your knees line up with the machine pivot.
Place your shins behind the pad and brace the handles.
Extend your knees until your legs are nearly straight.
Lower the weight slowly back to the start.

name: Single-Leg Leg Extension
description: A one-leg machine extension that isolates the quads side to side.
instructions: Set the machine so the working knee aligns with the pivot.
Place one shin behind the pad and keep the other leg relaxed.
Extend the working knee smoothly to the top.
Lower with control and repeat before switching sides.

name: Standing Cable Leg Extension
description: A standing cable variation that trains the quads through active knee extension.
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable and face away from the stack.
Start with the working knee slightly bent.
Extend the knee forward until the leg is nearly straight.
Return under control without letting the cable snap back.

name: Cable Leg Extension
description: A cable-based leg extension that provides smooth constant tension to the quads.
instructions: Sit on a bench with an ankle strap attached to a low cable.
Start with your knee bent and the cable under tension.
Extend the knee until your lower leg is straightened out.
Lower slowly back to the starting bend.

name: Resistance Band Leg Extension
description: A light-resistance knee extension using a band to isolate the quads.
instructions: Anchor a band behind you and loop it around your ankle.
Sit or brace yourself with the working knee bent.
Extend the knee smoothly against the band tension.
Return slowly to the bent starting position.

name: Ankle Weight Leg Extension
description: A simple leg extension using ankle weights for low-load quad isolation work.
instructions: Sit tall with an ankle weight secured on the working leg.
Start with your knee bent and foot relaxed.
Straighten the knee until the leg is extended.
Lower back down slowly and repeat.

name: Terminal Knee Extension
description: A short-range knee extension drill that targets the quads near lockout.
instructions: Loop a band behind your knee and step back to create tension.
Start with the working knee slightly bent.
Straighten the knee fully by tightening the quad.
Bend back to the start under control and repeat.

name: Cable Terminal Knee Extension
description: A cable version of terminal knee extension that provides steady resistance near lockout.
instructions: Set a low cable behind the working knee and step forward into tension.
Begin with a small bend in the knee.
Extend the knee fully by contracting the quad.
Return to the start slowly without losing balance.

name: Machine Sissy Squat
description: A machine-based sissy squat that provides support while heavily targeting the quads.
instructions: Set your feet and lower legs into the machine pads securely.
Lean back from the knees as you lower under control.
Keep your hips extended and let the quads take the load.
Return upright smoothly without bouncing out of the bottom.

name: Reverse Nordic Curl
description: A kneeling quad exercise where the body leans back while the hips stay extended.
instructions: Kneel tall with your hips extended and glutes lightly squeezed.
Lean your body back from the knees in one straight line.
Go only as far as you can control without folding at the hips.
Pull yourself back upright by driving through the quads.

name: Weighted Reverse Nordic Curl
description: A loaded reverse Nordic curl that increases resistance on the quads through the leaning phase.
instructions: Hold a plate close to your chest while kneeling tall.
Lean back slowly from the knees with your hips extended.
Pause briefly in the deepest controlled position.
Use your quads to return to upright.

name: Assisted Reverse Nordic Curl
description: A supported reverse Nordic curl that makes the movement easier to learn and control.
instructions: Use a band or support to reduce some of your bodyweight while kneeling tall.
Lean back slowly from the knees without hinging at the hips.
Keep the body in one line as far as you can control.
Return upright using the quads and assistance.

name: 45-Degree Leg Press
description: A classic angled leg press machine that lets you load the quads heavily.
instructions: Sit in the machine and place your feet on the platform.
Unlock the sled and lower it until your knees bend deeply.
Keep your lower back in contact with the pad throughout.
Press the sled away until your legs are almost straight.

name: Horizontal Leg Press
description: A horizontal leg press that trains the quads through a stable machine pressing pattern.
instructions: Sit into the machine and set your feet on the platform.
Lower the resistance under control until your knees are bent.
Keep your hips stable against the seat.
Press the platform forward to return to the start.

name: Vertical Leg Press
description: A vertical leg press that loads the quads through a straight up-and-down pressing path.
instructions: Lie into the machine and place your feet on the platform above you.
Unlock the carriage and bend your knees to lower it carefully.
Keep your hips and back supported throughout the rep.
Press the platform upward until your legs are nearly straight.

name: Single-Leg Leg Press
description: A one-leg leg press that builds quad strength and exposes side-to-side differences.
instructions: Sit in the leg press and place one foot at the center of the platform.
Lower the sled until the working knee is deeply bent.
Keep the working foot flat and your pelvis stable.
Press the platform away through the same leg.

name: Wall Sit
description: A simple isometric squat hold that keeps continuous tension on the quads.
instructions: Lean your back against a wall and slide down.
Stop when your knees are bent to a comfortable squat position.
Keep your feet planted and your torso against the wall.
Hold the position for the planned time.

name: Weighted Wall Sit
description: A wall sit holding external load to increase quad demand without movement.
instructions: Set up in a wall sit with your back flat against the wall.
Place a weight on your lap or hold it at your chest.
Keep your knees bent and feet rooted on the floor.
Hold the position without sliding or bouncing.

name: Single-Leg Wall Sit
description: A unilateral wall sit that overloads one quad at a time in an isometric position.
instructions: Slide into a wall sit with your back flat against the wall.
Lift one foot slightly so the other leg supports you.
Keep the stance leg steady and the torso pressed to the wall.
Hold the position before switching sides.

name: Backward Sled Drag
description: A backward drag that strongly loads the quads through repeated knee extension steps.
instructions: Attach straps or handles to the sled and face it while leaning back slightly.
Walk backward with short controlled steps.
Drive through the balls and midfoot to keep the sled moving.
Continue for distance or time while staying steady.

name: Single-Leg Pendulum Squat
description: A one-leg pendulum squat that creates a strong quad-biased resistance curve on the working side.
instructions: Set yourself into the machine with one foot in the main working position.
Lower into the squat slowly while keeping pressure through that foot.
Control the bottom position without twisting or dropping the hip.
Drive the platform up through the working leg to finish the rep.

name: Front Rack Forward Lunge
description: A forward lunge with the load racked in front that keeps the torso upright and quads heavily involved.
instructions: Rack the weight at the front of your shoulders and stand tall.
Step forward into a controlled lunge while keeping your elbows up.
Lower until the front leg is deeply bent and stable.
Push back through the front foot to return to the start.

name: Band Standing External Rotation
description: A standing band drill that strengthens the rotator cuff through external rotation at the side.
instructions: Set the elbow by your side.
Brace the shoulder and wrist.
Rotate the forearm outward under control.
Return slowly without losing position.

name: Cable Standing External Rotation
description: A standing cable drill that loads shoulder external rotation with a smooth resistance curve.
instructions: Set the elbow by your side.
Brace the shoulder and wrist.
Rotate the forearm outward under control.
Return slowly without losing position.

name: Side-Lying Dumbbell External Rotation
description: A side-lying dumbbell exercise that isolates the rotator cuff through external rotation.
instructions: Lie on your side with the elbow bent.
Keep the upper arm pinned to your ribs.
Rotate the forearm up slowly.
Lower the weight with control.

name: Band Seated External Rotation
description: A seated band variation that reduces lower-body movement and focuses on clean cuff mechanics.
instructions: Sit tall with the elbow tucked in.
Grip the band with a neutral wrist.
Rotate the forearm away from your body.
Return under full control.

name: Cable Seated External Rotation
description: A seated cable exercise that trains the cuff with steady tension and strict torso positioning.
instructions: Sit upright beside the cable stack.
Pin the elbow to your side.
Rotate the forearm outward smoothly.
Reverse the motion slowly.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Cuban Rotation
description: A light dumbbell shoulder-health drill that combines upright pulling with controlled external rotation.
instructions: Stand tall holding a light dumbbell at your side.
Lift the elbow up until the upper arm is near shoulder height.
Rotate the forearm upward under control.
Lower slowly back to the start.

name: Single-Arm Cable Cuban Rotation
description: A cable Cuban rotation that loads external rotation through a smooth guided path.
instructions: Set the cable low and stand side-on to the stack.
Lift the elbow until the upper arm is near shoulder level.
Rotate the forearm up without shrugging.
Return slowly along the same path.

name: Single-Arm Band Cuban Rotation
description: A band Cuban rotation that trains the cuff with light progressive resistance.
instructions: Anchor the band low and hold it with one hand.
Lift the elbow up while keeping the shoulder down.
Rotate the forearm upward with control.
Lower slowly back to the start.

name: Single-Arm Cable Scarecrow External Rotation
description: A cable scarecrow drill that strengthens the cuff from an abducted elbow-high position.
instructions: Set the cable around shoulder height.
Raise the upper arm so the elbow stays level with the shoulder.
Rotate the forearm back under control.
Return slowly without arching.

name: Band Towel-Roll External Rotation
description: A band external rotation performed with a towel at the side to improve humeral positioning.
instructions: Place a small towel between your arm and ribs.
Keep gentle pressure on the towel.
Rotate the forearm outward smoothly.
Return without dropping the towel.

name: Cable Towel-Roll External Rotation
description: A cable external rotation with a towel roll that promotes cleaner cuff alignment at the side.
instructions: Pin a towel between the arm and torso.
Stand tall beside the cable.
Rotate the forearm outward with control.
Return slowly and keep the towel in place.

name: Seated Supported Dumbbell External Rotation
description: A seated dumbbell external rotation performed with the elbow supported on the thigh for strict isolation.
instructions: Sit with the elbow braced on your thigh.
Start with the forearm across the body.
Rotate the forearm outward smoothly.
Lower the dumbbell under control.

name: Band 45-Degree External Rotation
description: A standing band exercise that trains the cuff with the arm slightly abducted in the scapular plane.
instructions: Raise the elbow slightly away from your side.
Keep the shoulder down and neck relaxed.
Rotate the forearm outward slowly.
Return to the start with control.

name: Cable 45-Degree External Rotation
description: A cable external rotation with the arm at about 45 degrees of abduction for a different cuff angle.
instructions: Set the upper arm slightly away from your body.
Brace the shoulder without shrugging.
Rotate the forearm outward through the cable line.
Reverse the motion slowly.

name: Single-Arm Band Scarecrow External Rotation
description: A band scarecrow rotation that challenges external rotation in a classic shoulder-health arm slot.
instructions: Anchor the band at about shoulder height.
Set the elbow level with the shoulder and bend it to ninety degrees.
Rotate the forearm backward smoothly.
Return under control to the start.

name: Single-Arm Prone Y Raise Thumb-Up
description: A prone thumb-up Y raise that supports lower-trap and cuff-friendly shoulder mechanics.
instructions: Lie face down with one arm hanging below the shoulder.
Turn the thumb up and brace the shoulder gently.
Raise the arm forward and out into a Y shape.
Lower slowly without swinging.

name: Side-Lying 45-Degree External Rotation
description: A side-lying dumbbell external rotation performed with the arm set slightly away from the body.
instructions: Lie on your side and set the elbow off the ribs.
Keep the upper arm supported and steady.
Rotate the forearm upward slowly.
Lower with control to the start.

name: Incline-Supported 45-Degree External Rotation
description: An incline-supported dumbbell drill that trains cuff external rotation with chest support.
instructions: Lie chest-down on a low incline bench.
Position the upper arm slightly out from the body.
Rotate the forearm upward in a small arc.
Lower slowly without swinging.

name: Wall-Supported Band 45-Degree External Rotation
description: A wall-supported band variation that limits compensation while the arm stays slightly abducted.
instructions: Stand with your upper back lightly against a wall.
Hold the upper arm slightly away from the body.
Rotate the forearm outward slowly.
Return while keeping contact with the wall.

name: Cable Low-to-High External Rotation
description: A cable external rotation that follows a low-to-high line of pull for shoulder control through an angled path.
instructions: Set the cable slightly below elbow height.
Hold the upper arm just off the torso.
Rotate and guide the hand up and out.
Return slowly along the same path.

name: Band Diagonal External Rotation
description: A band diagonal external rotation that combines cuff work with a gentle upward rotational path.
instructions: Anchor the band low and to the side.
Start with the elbow bent and shoulder relaxed.
Rotate the hand up and out diagonally.
Return along the same line slowly.

name: Prone 45-Degree External Rotation
description: A prone dumbbell exercise that loads external rotation while the arm is supported in slight abduction.
instructions: Lie face down with the arm hanging slightly out.
Bend the elbow to ninety degrees.
Rotate the forearm upward in control.
Lower slowly without moving the shoulder blade.

name: Band 90/90 External Rotation
description: A band shoulder external rotation performed with the arm abducted to shoulder height.
instructions: Raise the upper arm to shoulder height.
Keep the elbow bent at ninety degrees.
Rotate the forearm back without arching.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Cable 90/90 External Rotation
description: A cable 90/90 external rotation that challenges cuff strength in a throwing-like position.
instructions: Set the upper arm level with the shoulder.
Keep the elbow bent and wrist neutral.
Rotate the forearm backward under tension.
Return in a slow controlled arc.

name: Single-Arm Incline Y Raise Thumb-Up
description: An incline-supported Y raise that builds shoulder control with a cuff-friendly thumb-up path.
instructions: Lie chest-down on an incline bench.
Set the thumb up and keep the neck relaxed.
Raise the arm into a Y path under control.
Lower slowly back to the start.

name: Single-Arm Cable Y Raise
description: A cable Y raise that trains upward shoulder control through a smooth diagonal path.
instructions: Set the cable low and hold the handle with one hand.
Keep the thumb up and shoulder relaxed.
Raise the arm forward and out into a Y line.
Lower slowly to the start.

name: Single-Arm Band Y Raise
description: A band Y raise that reinforces shoulder-health mechanics with light progressive tension.
instructions: Stand on the band and hold it with one hand.
Keep the thumb up and ribs down.
Raise the arm forward and out in a Y path.
Lower with smooth control.

name: Single-Arm Trap-3 Raise
description: A shoulder-health raise performed in the scapular plane to build lower-trap and cuff support.
instructions: Lie face down with one arm reaching diagonally overhead.
Keep the thumb pointed up and shoulder blade controlled.
Lift the arm a small distance off the bench.
Lower slowly without shrugging.

name: Prone Flat-Bench 90/90 External Rotation
description: A prone dumbbell external rotation on a flat bench that trains the cuff with chest support.
instructions: Lie face down with the upper arm level to the side.
Keep the elbow bent at ninety degrees.
Rotate the forearm upward slowly.
Lower under control to the start.

name: Prone Incline-Bench 90/90 External Rotation
description: An incline-supported prone external rotation that changes the resistance profile at 90/90.
instructions: Lie chest-down on an incline bench.
Set the upper arm out at shoulder height.
Rotate the forearm upward in control.
Lower slowly without bouncing.

name: Seated Supported Cable 90/90 External Rotation
description: A seated cable 90/90 external rotation with the upper arm supported for strict mechanics.
instructions: Sit beside the cable with the upper arm supported.
Keep the elbow bent at ninety degrees.
Rotate the forearm backward smoothly.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Seated Supported Band 90/90 External Rotation
description: A seated band 90/90 variation that uses arm support to reduce compensations.
instructions: Sit with the upper arm supported at shoulder height.
Keep the elbow bent at ninety degrees.
Rotate the forearm backward under control.
Return slowly with the shoulder quiet.

name: Wall-Supported Band 90/90 External Rotation
description: A wall-supported 90/90 band rotation that helps maintain better rib and shoulder position.
instructions: Stand with your back lightly against a wall.
Raise the arm to the 90/90 position.
Rotate the forearm backward under control.
Return slowly while staying tall.

name: Pad-Supported Cable 90/90 External Rotation
description: A cable 90/90 external rotation with the upper arm braced against a pad for strict cuff work.
instructions: Brace the upper arm against a pad at shoulder height.
Keep the elbow bent and neck relaxed.
Rotate the forearm backward against the cable.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Band Quarterback External Rotation
description: A band-based thrower drill that trains cuff external rotation in a sport-specific arm slot.
instructions: Set the arm in a high throwing position.
Keep the elbow bent and shoulder packed.
Rotate the forearm back with control.
Return slowly without twisting.

name: Cable Thrower's External Rotation
description: A cable thrower-style external rotation that strengthens the cuff in an overhead sport position.
instructions: Stand beside the cable in a throwing arm slot.
Keep the elbow bent at ninety degrees.
Rotate the forearm backward smoothly.
Return slowly and stay stacked.

name: Side-Lying Abducted External Rotation
description: A side-lying dumbbell external rotation performed with the shoulder abducted to about ninety degrees.
instructions: Lie on your side with the upper arm supported at shoulder height.
Bend the elbow to ninety degrees.
Rotate the forearm upward slowly.
Lower under control without rolling back.

name: Band Standing Internal Rotation
description: A standing band drill that strengthens the cuff through internal rotation at the side.
instructions: Set the elbow by your side.
Brace the shoulder and keep the wrist neutral.
Rotate the forearm inward under control.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Cable Standing Internal Rotation
description: A standing cable exercise that loads shoulder internal rotation with smooth tension.
instructions: Set the elbow by your side.
Brace the shoulder and keep the wrist neutral.
Rotate the forearm inward under control.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Band Seated Internal Rotation
description: A seated band internal rotation that limits body sway and keeps the movement strict.
instructions: Sit tall with the elbow tucked in.
Brace the shoulder gently.
Rotate the forearm across the body.
Return slowly without shrugging.

name: Cable Seated Internal Rotation
description: A seated cable internal rotation that keeps constant tension on the cuff.
instructions: Sit upright beside the cable.
Keep the elbow pinned to your side.
Rotate the forearm inward across the body.
Return under full control.

name: Single-Arm Incline Trap-3 Raise
description: An incline-supported trap-3 raise that trains overhead shoulder support with strict mechanics.
instructions: Lie chest-down on a low incline bench.
Reach one arm diagonally overhead with the thumb up.
Lift the arm in a short controlled range.
Lower slowly to the start.

name: Single-Arm Cable Trap-3 Raise
description: A cable trap-3 raise that loads the arm in a diagonal overhead path for shoulder support.
instructions: Set the cable low and grip the handle with one hand.
Keep the thumb up and the shoulder packed.
Raise the arm diagonally overhead under control.
Lower slowly along the same line.

name: Single-Arm Band Trap-3 Raise
description: A band trap-3 raise that trains diagonal overhead control with light smooth resistance.
instructions: Anchor the band low and hold it with one hand.
Keep the thumb up and the torso steady.
Raise the arm diagonally overhead with control.
Lower slowly to the start.

name: Single-Arm Serratus Wall Slide
description: A single-arm wall slide that promotes upward rotation and shoulder-friendly scapular control.
instructions: Place one forearm on the wall at shoulder height.
Keep light pressure into the wall and ribs down.
Slide the arm upward smoothly.
Return slowly without shrugging.

name: Band Towel-Roll Internal Rotation
description: A band internal rotation with a towel at the side to encourage clean shoulder positioning.
instructions: Place a towel between the arm and ribs.
Maintain light pressure on the towel.
Rotate the forearm inward under control.
Return slowly without losing the towel.

name: Cable Towel-Roll Internal Rotation
description: A cable internal rotation with a towel roll that promotes strict cuff mechanics at the side.
instructions: Pin a towel between the arm and torso.
Stand tall beside the cable.
Rotate the forearm inward smoothly.
Return slowly and keep the towel in place.

name: Seated Supported Dumbbell Internal Rotation
description: A seated dumbbell internal rotation performed with the elbow supported on the thigh for strict isolation.
instructions: Sit with the elbow braced on your thigh.
Start with the forearm out to the side.
Rotate the forearm inward slowly.
Reverse the motion with control.

name: Side-Lying Dumbbell Internal Rotation
description: A side-lying dumbbell exercise that isolates internal rotation through a short controlled range.
instructions: Lie on your side with the elbow bent.
Keep the upper arm fixed against your torso.
Rotate the forearm inward slowly.
Return under control to the start.

name: Band 45-Degree Internal Rotation
description: A band internal rotation with the arm slightly abducted to train the cuff at a different angle.
instructions: Raise the elbow slightly away from your side.
Keep the shoulder down and wrist neutral.
Rotate the forearm inward slowly.
Return under full control.

name: Cable 45-Degree Internal Rotation
description: A cable internal rotation performed with the arm in slight abduction for a different cuff demand.
instructions: Set the upper arm slightly away from the body.
Brace the shoulder without shrugging.
Rotate the forearm inward smoothly.
Reverse the motion slowly.

name: Band Half-Kneeling 45-Degree Internal Rotation
description: A half-kneeling band drill that loads internal rotation with the arm held off the torso.
instructions: Set up half-kneeling with the elbow slightly out.
Keep the shoulder steady and ribs down.
Rotate the forearm inward under control.
Return slowly without leaning.

name: Cable Half-Kneeling 45-Degree Internal Rotation
description: A half-kneeling cable variation that strengthens internal rotation from a mid-abduction angle.
instructions: Hold the upper arm slightly off the body.
Brace the torso and keep the neck relaxed.
Rotate inward against the cable.
Return under full control.

name: Band 90/90 Internal Rotation
description: A band shoulder internal rotation performed with the arm abducted to shoulder height.
instructions: Raise the upper arm to shoulder height.
Keep the elbow bent at ninety degrees.
Rotate the forearm forward under control.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Cable 90/90 Internal Rotation
description: A cable 90/90 internal rotation that challenges cuff strength in an abducted arm position.
instructions: Set the upper arm level with the shoulder.
Keep the elbow bent and wrist neutral.
Rotate the forearm forward smoothly.
Return in a slow controlled arc.

name: Single-Arm Foam Roller Serratus Wall Slide
description: A foam-roller wall slide that adds smoother upward rotation and serratus-focused shoulder control.
instructions: Place your forearm on a foam roller against the wall.
Keep light pressure into the roller and brace the trunk.
Slide the arm upward in control.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Side-Lying Shoulder Abduction Thumb-Up
description: A side-lying thumb-up raise that trains the shoulder through a cuff-friendly abduction path.
instructions: Lie on your side with the working arm on top.
Turn the thumb upward and keep the shoulder relaxed.
Raise the arm in a short smooth arc.
Lower slowly with control.

name: Single-Arm Bottoms-Up Kettlebell Carry
description: A stability carry that challenges shoulder control by holding a kettlebell upside down at rack height.
instructions: Clean a light kettlebell to a bottoms-up rack position.
Keep the wrist stacked and elbow under the bell.
Walk slowly while staying tall and controlled.
Stop, reset, and switch sides.

name: Single-Arm Overhead Bottoms-Up Kettlebell Carry
description: An advanced overhead carry that trains cuff and scapular stability with the kettlebell upside down.
instructions: Press a light kettlebell overhead in a bottoms-up position.
Lock the elbow softly and keep the ribs down.
Walk slowly while keeping the bell steady.
Lower carefully and switch sides.

name: Seated Supported Band 90/90 Internal Rotation
description: A seated band 90/90 internal rotation with arm support to keep the movement strict.
instructions: Sit with the upper arm supported at shoulder height.
Keep the elbow bent at ninety degrees.
Rotate the forearm forward smoothly.
Return slowly with control.

name: Seated Supported Cable 90/90 Internal Rotation
description: A seated cable 90/90 internal rotation that uses arm support for cleaner mechanics.
instructions: Sit beside the cable with the upper arm supported.
Keep the elbow bent at ninety degrees.
Rotate the forearm forward under tension.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Band Belly Press
description: A band drill that strengthens the subscapularis by pressing the hand toward the abdomen.
instructions: Anchor the band behind you and bend the elbow.
Keep the elbow slightly forward of the torso.
