Press the hand toward your belly under control.
Return slowly without the elbow drifting back.

name: Cable Belly Press
description: A cable belly press that trains internal rotation and subscapularis control with steady tension.
instructions: Stand with the cable pulling the hand away from the belly.
Keep the elbow bent and slightly forward.
Press the hand into the abdomen smoothly.
Return slowly without shrugging.

name: Band Bear Hug Internal Rotation
description: A band bear-hug pattern that strengthens the front-side cuff through internal rotation and protraction.
instructions: Anchor the band behind you at chest height.
Start with the elbow bent and hand away from the chest.
Sweep the arm forward like a one-arm hug.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Cable Bear Hug Internal Rotation
description: A cable bear-hug pattern that loads internal rotation through a forward wrapping path.
instructions: Stand with the cable behind you at chest level.
Keep a soft bend in the elbow.
Sweep the arm across the front of the body.
Return slowly without rotating the torso.

name: Hand-Behind-Back Lift-Off
description: A classic subscapularis drill where the hand lifts away from the lower back under control.
instructions: Place the back of the hand on your low back.
Set the shoulder blade gently down.
Lift the hand away from the back a few inches.
Lower slowly without arching.

name: Band Hand-Behind-Back Lift-Off
description: A band-resisted lift-off that strengthens the subscapularis from the hand-behind-back position.
instructions: Set your hand behind the back with the band adding resistance.
Keep the torso tall and elbow bent.
Lift the hand gently away from the back.
Return slowly with control.

name: Cable Hand-Behind-Back Lift-Off
description: A cable lift-off variation that adds constant tension to the classic subscapularis pattern.
instructions: Stand so the cable resists the hand-behind-back position.
Keep the chest tall and shoulder quiet.
Lift the hand away from the back slowly.
Return carefully to the start.

name: Wall Slide Lift-Off
description: A single-arm wall slide that finishes with a brief lift-off to challenge shoulder control overhead.
instructions: Place one forearm on the wall at shoulder height.
Slide the arm up while keeping light pressure.
Lift the hand slightly off the wall at the top.
Return slowly down the wall.

name: Belly Press Isometric Wall Hold
description: An isometric belly press against a wall that trains subscapularis tension without movement.
instructions: Stand side-on with the elbow bent.
Press the palm gently into the wall toward the belly line.
Hold steady without shrugging.
Relax and reset between efforts.

name: Hand-Behind-Back Lift-Off Isometric
description: An isometric lift-off hold that builds subscapularis control in the hand-behind-back position.
instructions: Place the hand behind your back.
Lift it slightly away from the body.
Hold the position without arching the back.
Lower and reset smoothly.

name: Band Face Pull to External Rotation
description: A band face pull variation that finishes in external rotation for upper cuff and rear-shoulder control.
instructions: Anchor the band at face height.
Pull the elbow back while keeping the shoulder down.
Finish by rotating the forearm back.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Rope Cable Face Pull to External Rotation
description: A rope cable face pull that finishes with external rotation to train the cuff and posterior shoulder.
instructions: Set the rope at face height.
Pull the rope toward the face with the elbow high.
Rotate the hands back to finish the rep.
Return slowly under control.

name: Single-Arm Cable Face Pull to External Rotation
description: A single-arm cable face pull that blends rear-shoulder work with cuff external rotation.
instructions: Set the cable at face height.
Pull the elbow back in line with the shoulder.
Rotate the hand back to finish the motion.
Return slowly without twisting.

name: Single-Arm Band Face Pull to External Rotation
description: A single-arm band face pull that adds external rotation at the end range for shoulder health.
instructions: Anchor the band at eye level.
Pull the elbow back smoothly.
Finish by rotating the forearm backward.
Return to the start with control.

name: Single-Arm Prone W Raise
description: A prone W raise that strengthens the cuff and posterior shoulder with external rotation emphasis.
instructions: Lie face down with one arm hanging under the shoulder.
Bend the elbow and set the thumb up.
Lift into a W shape while rotating out.
Lower slowly to the start.

name: Single-Arm Incline W Raise
description: An incline-supported W raise that targets the cuff with chest support and clean mechanics.
instructions: Lie chest-down on an incline bench.
Start with the arm hanging and elbow bent.
Raise the arm into a W path with external rotation.
Lower under control.

name: Single-Arm Band W Raise
description: A standing band W raise that combines scapular retraction with external rotation on one side.
instructions: Anchor the band in front of you.
Start with the elbow bent near the ribs.
Pull back and rotate into a W position.
Return slowly without shrugging.

name: Single-Arm Cable W Raise
description: A cable W raise that loads external rotation and posterior shoulder control through a smooth path.
instructions: Set the cable just below chest height.
Start with the elbow bent and hand forward.
Pull back and rotate into a W shape.
Return slowly along the same path.

name: Single-Arm Full Can Raise
description: A scaption raise in a thumbs-up position that supports shoulder health with a cuff-friendly line of motion.
instructions: Stand tall with the thumb pointing up.
Raise the arm in the scapular plane.
Stop around shoulder height without shrugging.
Lower slowly to the start.

name: Single-Arm Cable Full Can Raise
description: A cable full-can raise that keeps steady tension through a cuff-friendly scaption path.
instructions: Stand beside the cable with the thumb up.
Raise the arm forward and out in the scapular plane.
Stop at shoulder height with control.
Lower slowly along the same path.

name: Single-Arm Band Full Can Raise
description: A band full-can raise that trains the shoulder in scaption with light progressive resistance.
instructions: Stand on the band with the thumb up.
Raise the arm in the scapular plane.
Stop around shoulder height without shrugging.
Lower slowly to the start.

name: Single-Arm Prone T Raise Thumb-Up
description: A prone T raise with the thumb up that supports posterior cuff and shoulder health.
instructions: Lie face down with one arm hanging straight down.
Turn the thumb up and brace the shoulder.
Raise the arm out to the side to shoulder height.
Lower slowly without swinging.

name: Single-Arm Incline T Raise Thumb-Up
description: An incline-supported T raise that trains posterior shoulder control with a thumb-up position.
instructions: Lie chest-down on an incline bench.
Turn the thumb up and keep the neck relaxed.
Raise the arm out to the side under control.
Lower slowly to the start.

name: Single-Arm Cable T Raise Thumb-Up
description: A cable T raise in a thumbs-up position that supports shoulder health through horizontal abduction.
instructions: Set the cable low and stand side-on.
Turn the thumb up and brace the shoulder.
Raise the arm out to the side to shoulder height.
Return slowly under tension.

name: Single-Arm Band T Raise Thumb-Up
description: A band T raise with the thumb up that builds posterior shoulder and cuff endurance.
instructions: Anchor the band low and stand tall.
Turn the thumb up and keep a soft elbow.
Raise the arm out to the side to shoulder height.
Return slowly without shrugging.

name: Single-Arm Wall Slide With Band
description: A single-arm wall slide with band tension that builds upward rotation and cuff-friendly shoulder control.
instructions: Place one forearm on the wall with light band tension.
Keep the shoulder blade wrapped around the ribcage.
Slide the arm upward smoothly.
Lower slowly without losing pressure.

name: Single-Arm Foam Roller Wall Slide With Band
description: A single-arm foam-roller wall slide that adds reach and cuff-friendly overhead control.
instructions: Place one forearm on a foam roller against the wall.
Keep light outward band tension at the wrist.
Slide the arm up while reaching gently forward.
Return slowly with control.

name: Single-Arm Forearm Wall Slide
description: A single-arm forearm wall slide that improves shoulder motion and scapular control with low load.
instructions: Place one forearm on the wall below shoulder height.
Keep the neck relaxed and ribs down.
Slide the arm upward smoothly.
Lower slowly back to the start.

name: Single-Arm Cable Serratus Punch
description: A cable serratus punch that supports shoulder health by training controlled protraction on one side.
instructions: Set the cable at chest height with a light load.
Start with the elbow slightly bent.
Punch forward by reaching the shoulder blade around the ribs.
Return slowly without shrugging.

name: Single-Arm Band Serratus Punch
description: A band serratus punch that teaches forward reach and shoulder blade control for healthier shoulder motion.
instructions: Anchor the band behind you at chest height.
Start with the elbow soft and hand near the chest.
Reach forward by protracting the shoulder blade.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Supine Single-Arm Serratus Punch
description: A supine dumbbell punch that builds shoulder blade control with minimal joint irritation.
instructions: Lie on your back with the arm straight up.
Keep the elbow locked softly and wrist stacked.
Reach the weight toward the ceiling.
Lower the shoulder blade back down slowly.

name: Quadruped Single-Arm Weight Shift
description: A quadruped stability drill that challenges cuff-supported shoulder control while loading one arm.
instructions: Start on hands and knees with one hand as the working side.
Shift more bodyweight into that arm.
Hold the shoulder steady as you breathe.
Shift back and repeat smoothly.

name: Single-Arm Wall Shoulder Circles With Towel
description: A wall-supported shoulder circle drill that trains cuff-friendly control through small circles.
instructions: Place one hand on a towel against the wall.
Press lightly and keep the elbow soft.
Draw small circles with the hand.
Reverse the direction and stay controlled.

name: Single-Arm Stability Ball Wall Circles
description: A ball-on-wall drill that builds cuff endurance and shoulder stability through controlled circles.
instructions: Place one hand on the ball against the wall.
Keep the shoulder down and elbow soft.
Make small slow circles without losing pressure.
Reverse the direction and maintain control.

name: Single-Arm Medicine Ball Wall Stabilization Circles
description: A firmer ball-on-wall variation that challenges shoulder stability with a denser implement.
instructions: Place one hand on a medicine ball against the wall.
Apply steady pressure and brace the shoulder.
Make small circles with the hand.
Reverse direction without shrugging.

name: Band External Rotation Isometric Hold
description: An isometric band hold that trains cuff endurance in external rotation at the side.
instructions: Set the elbow at your side and rotate outward.
Stop at a strong mid-range position.
Hold without letting the shoulder shrug.
Return slowly and reset.

name: Band Internal Rotation Isometric Hold
description: An isometric band hold that builds cuff endurance in internal rotation at the side.
instructions: Set the elbow at your side and rotate inward.
Stop at a strong mid-range position.
Hold without twisting the torso.
Return slowly and reset.

name: Wall 90/90 External Rotation Isometric
description: An isometric wall press in the 90/90 position that builds overhead cuff stability.
instructions: Raise the arm into the 90/90 position.
Press the back of the hand lightly into the wall.
Hold the shoulder steady without arching.
Relax and reset between holds.

name: Wall 90/90 Internal Rotation Isometric
description: An isometric wall press in the 90/90 position that trains internal rotation stability overhead.
instructions: Raise the arm into the 90/90 position.
Press the palm lightly into the wall.
Hold the shoulder steady without leaning.
Relax and reset between holds.

name: Treadmill Walk (Easy / Zone 2)
description: Low-impact steady walking on a treadmill to build aerobic base and recovery between hard sessions.
instructions: Set a comfortable pace you can sustain while nasal breathing or holding short conversations.
Stand tall with relaxed shoulders and a natural arm swing.
Keep strides smooth; avoid holding the handrails unless you need balance.
Gradually increase duration or incline slightly week to week instead of speed only.

name: Treadmill Incline Walk
description: Moderate incline walking to raise heart rate with lower joint impact than running.
instructions: Set a sustainable incline and speed where you can still breathe through your nose or speak in sentences.
Take short steps and drive through the glutes without leaning heavily on the handles.
Keep chest tall and eyes forward.
If your heart rate spikes too high, lower incline slightly before reducing speed.

name: Treadmill Jog (Steady State)
description: Comfortably-paced jogging to develop aerobic fitness and running economy.
instructions: Warm up with 5–10 minutes of easy walking before picking up to a jog.
Land with moderate cadence; avoid long, heavy heel strikes if they bother your joints.
Stay relaxed in shoulders, jaw, and hands.
Finish with a few minutes of walking to bring heart rate down.

name: Treadmill Run Intervals
description: Alternates harder running efforts with easy recovery for improved speed and VO2 capacity.
instructions: After a thorough warm-up, run hard for the work interval at a controlled, repeatable effort.
Step to the sides or slow the belt for full recovery between reps.
Stop if form breaks down or you feel sharp pain; adjust speed or incline.
Cool down with easy walking until breathing returns to normal.

name: Outdoor Jog (Steady State)
description: Comfortably-paced outdoor jogging to build aerobic fitness with no equipment needed.
instructions: Start with a few minutes of brisk walking before easing into a jog.
Keep the pace conversational; slow to a walk any time you need to.
Pick a flat, familiar route and stay aware of traffic.
Finish with a few minutes of walking to bring heart rate down.

name: Outdoor Run Intervals
description: Alternates brisk outdoor running with easy recovery jogging or walking to build speed and capacity anywhere.
instructions: Warm up with several minutes of easy jogging first.
Run brisk for the work interval at an effort you could repeat, then walk or jog easy to recover.
Choose flat, open ground with sure footing.
Cool down with easy walking until breathing returns to normal.

name: Stationary Bike (Steady / Zone 2)
description: Low-impact cycling at a sustainable effort for aerobic development and active recovery.
instructions: Adjust seat height so knees have a slight bend at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Push and pull smoothly through the full circle; avoid mashing only downward.
Keep upper body relaxed with light grip on handles.
Stay in a conversational effort for base work, or use prescribed power or heart-rate zones.

name: Stationary Bike Intervals
description: High-intensity cycling intervals with recovery periods for conditioning and leg power.
instructions: Warm up 8–15 minutes with gradually increasing effort.
For each work interval, increase resistance and cadence to a strong but repeatable effort.
Spin legs lightly during recovery; don’t stop completely between reps.
Cool down until heart rate and breathing settle.

name: Recumbent Bike (Steady)
description: Seated cycling with back support—common in gyms for low-impact cardio, warm-ups, or long steady sessions with less trunk fatigue than an upright bike.
instructions: Adjust seat so leg is almost straight at full extension without locking the knee.
Push through the full pedal stroke; add light upper-body support from handles without leaning hard.
Keep steady resistance for Zone 2 or use intervals if the bike supports quick changes.
Stop if numb feet or knee pain persists—recheck seat position.

name: Assault / Air Bike
description: Full-body fan bike conditioning using arms and legs for high-output intervals or steady work.
instructions: Brace your core and maintain smooth pulls and pushes on the handles.
Start with shorter intervals; air bikes ramp up resistance as you go faster.
Keep shoulders down and avoid death-gripping the handles.
Scale interval length and rest to match current fitness.

name: Elliptical (Steady State)
description: Low-impact, full-body cardio machine work for sustained aerobic training.
instructions: Stand tall with a slight hip hinge; avoid leaning all your weight on the arms.
Drive through the full stride without bouncing excessively.
Use handles for moderate upper-body contribution, not to lock out your posture.
Hold a steady effort for time or follow heart-rate targets.

name: Elliptical Intervals
description: Alternates harder stride or resistance with easy recovery on the elliptical—common template when you want low-impact interval work.
instructions: Warm up 5–10 minutes at easy resistance before the first hard push.
For work intervals, add resistance and stride rate but stay tall—no collapsing onto the arms.
Recover at low resistance with full foot contact; let breathing settle.
Stop if hips or knees complain; lower range or speed before quitting outright.

name: Rowing Machine (Steady State)
description: Full-body, low-impact rowing at sustainable pace for aerobic capacity.
instructions: Sequence legs–body–arms on the drive; reverse on the recovery.
Keep back neutral; drive with legs first before opening the hips.
Control the return; let the handle pass your knees only after legs flatten.
Pick a stroke rate and split you can hold for the full session.

name: Rowing Machine Intervals
description: Hard rowing efforts with easy paddling recovery for conditioning.
instructions: Warm up with easy rowing and a few progressive strokes.
During work intervals, maintain strong technique; stop if form collapses.
Use light pressure and slow strokes during recovery.
Log splits or watts if tracking progress over weeks.

name: Ski Erg (Steady)
description: Upper-body-dominant ergometer work that still challenges core and hips at sustainable effort.
instructions: Hinge slightly at hips with soft knees; pull handles down and through with lats.
Alternate arms smoothly or use double-pole strokes as programmed.
Keep ribs down and avoid overarching the low back.
Build volume gradually; shoulders should not burn out in the first few minutes.

name: Ski Erg Intervals
description: Short, high-output bursts on the ski erg with controlled recovery.
instructions: Brace trunk before each pull; exhale on the drive.
Maintain a steady rhythm; don’t shorten range just to go faster.
Between intervals, continue light strokes or step off briefly if needed.
Stop if you feel sharp shoulder or elbow irritation.

name: Stair Climber / Step Mill
description: Continuous stepping for strong leg endurance and elevated heart rate with controlled impact.
instructions: Stand fully upright; lightly rest fingertips on rails for balance only.
Place your whole foot on each step when possible.
Start with slower speeds and shorter durations; add time before max speed.
Step off if you feel dizzy or get side stitches that don’t ease with slower pacing.

name: Jacob's Ladder (Ladder Treadmill)
description: Self-paced climbing machine with a moving ladder—demanding full-body cardio found in many strength-and-conditioning gyms.
instructions: Use the safety strap or belt per the manufacturer’s instructions before climbing.
Climb smoothly; let the machine set cadence early until you learn the rhythm.
Keep hips close to the ladder and avoid over-reaching with the arms.
Start with 2–5 minute bouts and build; stop if grip fails or you feel unsafe.

name: VersaClimber
description: Full-body vertical climbing pattern for high heart-rate conditioning.
instructions: Maintain a smooth alternating or parallel stride per machine settings.
Keep hips close to the machine; avoid excessive rocking.
Scale stroke length and tempo to keep movement quality high.
Begin with short bouts and extend as conditioning improves.

name: Arc Trainer (Steady)
description: Gliding stride machine for low-impact cardio with adjustable resistance and incline.
instructions: Let the foot plates move naturally without stomping.
Adjust resistance so effort feels sustainable for the planned duration.
Use arm handles for balance and light upper-body contribution.
Stay tall through the torso.

name: Self-Powered / Curve Treadmill Run
description: Running on a non-motorized curved belt where you set the pace—great for short accelerations and technique.
instructions: Start with light steps at the front curve until the belt moves smoothly.
Stay mid-foot to forefoot biased as appropriate for your mechanics.
Use short sprints or fartlek-style pickups with full walk-down recoveries.
Stop the belt safely before stepping off.

name: Jump Rope — Single Unders
description: Rhythmic rope skipping for coordination and steady cardio; minimal space and equipment.
instructions: Use a rope length that clears your head with a small hop (or hold handles of your jump rope if available).
Spin from the wrists, not huge arm circles.
Land softly on the balls of the feet with slight knee flexion.
Keep jumps low; the rope needs only a small gap.

name: Jump Rope — Double Unders
description: High-turnover rope work where the rope passes twice per jump—intense conditioning in short doses.
instructions: Master consistent single unders and high wrist speed first.
Jump a bit higher while spinning faster; stay tall.
Rest between failed reps to keep quality high.
Scale with intermittent doubles (e.g., 1 double every 5 singles) while learning.

name: Burpee
description: Full-body bodyweight movement combining squat, plank, push-up optional, and jump for conditioning.
instructions: Drop hands to the floor, jump or step back to a plank with a braced torso.
Optional controlled push-up, then jump or step feet forward.
Finish with a small vertical jump or reach overhead if appropriate.
Step back and omit the jump for a lower-impact version.

name: Mountain Climbers (Cardio Pace)
description: Alternating knee drives from a plank for elevated heart rate and core endurance.
instructions: Stack shoulders over wrists; keep hips level with the floor.
Drive knees toward chest without bouncing hips to the sky.
Breathe steadily; slow down before form breaks.
Perform on a bench or elevate hands to reduce intensity.

name: High Knees (In Place)
description: In-place rhythmic knee drives to raise heart rate and hip flexor turnover.
instructions: Pump arms as if sprinting; lift knees toward hip height.
Land softly with quick, light contacts.
Stay tall; avoid folding forward at the waist.
Use timed rounds (e.g., 20–40 seconds) with walk recovery.

name: Jumping Jack
description: Classic full-body warm-up and conditioning movement.
instructions: Start with feet together and arms at sides.
Jump feet out while raising arms overhead or to shoulder height.
Return to start in one smooth motion.
For low impact, tap one foot out at a time without leaving the ground.

name: Lateral Shuffle (Conditioning)
description: Agility-style side-to-side shuffling for lateral conditioning and heart rate.
instructions: Stay low in an athletic stance with chest up.
Push off the outside foot; don’t cross feet.
Cover a set distance or stay between two cones.
Keep head level—avoid excessive bobbing.

name: Box Jump
description: Explosive jump onto a sturdy box or platform for power and conditioning.
instructions: Use a box height you can land on with soft knees and full foot contact.
Swing arms for momentum; jump vertically, not into the box.
Land quietly with hips and knees bent to absorb force.
Step down between reps for joint-friendlier volume; stop before sloppy landings.

name: Jump Squat (Bodyweight)
description: Repeated squat jumps for leg power and high heart rate in short sets.
instructions: Squat to a consistent depth with chest tall.
Explode up; land softly into the next rep or reset between jumps.
Keep knees tracking over toes.
Limit total jumps per session to preserve knee comfort.

name: Kettlebell Swing (Conditioning)
description: Hip-hinge ballistic swings for posterior-chain power and sustained cardio when done for time.
instructions: Hinge hips back; arms are straps, not lifters.
Snap hips to standing; bell floats to chest height (Russian) or overhead if trained for American style.
Breathe rhythmically; stay tall at the top of each rep.
Stop before low-back rounding or shrug-dominated swings.

name: Medicine Ball Slam
description: Explosive overhead slams for full-body power and interval conditioning.
instructions: Use a non-bouncing slam ball on a suitable floor.
Raise ball overhead using hips and core; slam down hard in front of feet.
Pick up fluidly into the next rep.
Stop if elbows or low back gets cranky; reduce volume or weight.

name: Battle Rope — Alternating Waves
description: Rapid alternating arm waves for shoulder endurance and high heart rate.
instructions: Hold one end in each hand, athletic stance, slight hip hinge.
Create continuous waves moving down the rope.
Keep ribs down; breathe in short bursts.
Use 15–30 second work chunks to start; extend as tolerance builds.

name: Battle Rope — Double Slams
description: Lifting both rope ends high and slamming together for power-based conditioning intervals.
instructions: Raise ropes overhead using legs and hips.
Slam aggressively to the floor; reset quickly into the next rep.
Avoid excessive arching through the low back.
Keep sets short and intense with full recovery if power drops.

name: Sled Push
description: Heavy forward pushing for leg drive and brutal conditioning when done for distance or time.
instructions: Set handles at shoulder height; brace core and drive through mid-foot.
Take short, choppy steps; keep spine neutral.
Add load only if you can maintain strong positions.
Walk back or rest fully between pushes as programmed.

name: Sled Drag (Backward)
description: Backward walking against a harness or handles for quad burn and cardio with low collision risk.
instructions: Attach belt or handles; step backward with small, controlled steps.
Keep weight through full feet; avoid leaning too far back.
Choose a load you can move smoothly for the target distance.
Clear space behind you before starting.

name: Farmer's Carry — Brisk Walk (Conditioning)
description: Walking with heavy dumbbells or handles at a brisk pace for grip, trunk, and heart rate.
instructions: Pick weights you can hold with packed shoulders and tall posture.
Walk at a pace that raises breathing but doesn’t ruin form.
Set the weights down before grip failure causes leaning.
Use straps only if grip is intentionally not the limiter.

name: Shadow Boxing (Rounds)
description: Timed rounds of punches, footwork, and head movement without contact for steady cardio.
instructions: Stay light on the feet; keep hands up and chin tucked.
Rotate through hips on crosses and hooks.
Use 2–3 minute rounds with 30–60 seconds rest for conditioning.
Focus on technique at lower fatigue; add speed as skill allows.

name: Swimming — Easy Laps
description: Continuous easy swimming for low-impact full-body cardio (pool required).
instructions: Warm up outside the water or with very easy laps.
Pick a stroke you can sustain with smooth breathing.
Stay in a lane with appropriate speed etiquette.
Exit if you feel cramping, dizziness, or unsafe fatigue.

name: Outdoor Cycling (Steady)
description: Outdoor cycling at sustainable effort for long-duration aerobic development.
instructions: Follow traffic laws and wear appropriate safety gear.
Keep cadence and gearing comfortable for the distance.
Fuel and hydrate on longer rides.
Use heart rate or power zones if you track them.

name: Trail Hiking (Brisk)
description: Outdoor hiking with elevation or brisk pace for low-impact endurance.
instructions: Wear supportive footwear; pack water for longer routes.
Use trekking poles on steep descents if you like, to spare knees.
Keep a pace that allows conversation on flats; power hikes on climbs as desired.
Plan route and weather appropriate to fitness.

name: HIIT — General High-Intensity Intervals
description: Structured work–rest bouts at high effort (roughly RPE 8–10 on work) to train anaerobic power and aerobic recovery; duration, modality, and rest can be tailored. Short “micro” blocks (roughly 4–12 minutes of hard work, plus warm-up and cool-down) use the same rules with a smaller total dose.
instructions: Warm up until you are sweaty and joints feel ready—never start cold on HIIT.
Pick work intervals you can repeat with similar output (avoid going to failure on rep 1).
Use full or active recovery so heart rate drops before the next hard bout.
Short on time: warm up properly, pick 1–2 simple movements, and keep work bouts honest even if total work is only a few minutes.
Cap weekly HIIT volume; most training should still be easy or moderate intensity.
Fill the rest of the week with easy movement (walking, Zone 2, daily steps)—short HIIT is not a substitute for baseline activity.

name: Tabata Intervals (Classic)
description: Named protocol: eight rounds of 20 seconds near-max effort and 10 seconds rest (four minutes per block), often repeated for two to four blocks with longer rests between blocks.
instructions: Choose one simple movement (sprint in place, bike sprint, thrusters, etc.) and stick with it for the full 8 rounds when possible.
20 seconds is short—push pace close to maximal sustainable, not a jog.
Use a timer; 10-second rest passes quickly—stay ready for the next start.
Beginners can reduce total rounds or use a lower-impact move; stop if form collapses.

name: EMOM — Cardio or Mixed Conditioning
aliases: Every Minute on the Minute Cardio
description: At the start of each minute, complete a prescribed workload (reps, calories, or distance), then rest the remainder of the minute; repeats for 10–30 minutes builds pacing under fatigue.
instructions: Set a workload that leaves roughly 15–25 seconds rest early in the session.
If you miss the minute boundary, scale reps or difficulty before the next round.
Keep transitions fast—EMOM rewards efficiency, not wandering between stations.
Log rounds or splits to track progress week to week.

name: AMRAP — Conditioning Circuit
description: Fixed time cap (often 8–20 minutes): complete as many rounds as possible of a small exercise circuit; a staple of HIIT-style classes and functional fitness for work capacity. Often what people call a “MetCon”—mixed strength and cardio under fatigue.
instructions: Pick 3–5 movements you can cycle through safely when breathing hard.
Start slightly conservative; blow up early and the rest of the AMRAP suffers.
Count full rounds plus partial rounds the same way each session for comparable scores.
Order moves to alternate stress (e.g., upper/lower) when possible; scale loads so work stays continuous.
Substitute low-impact options (e.g., step-back burpees) if joints complain.

name: Norwegian 4×4 Intervals
description: Evidence-popular format: four intervals of about four minutes at very high aerobic power (often ~85–95% max heart rate) with three minutes easy recovery between—commonly done running, rowing, cycling, or skiing.
instructions: Build an aerobic base before stacking weekly 4×4 sessions.
During work intervals, hold the fastest steady pace you can repeat for all four bouts—avoid sprinting the first rep only.
Recovery must be truly easy: slow breathing, not just slower working pace.
One session per week is often enough at first; quality beats volume.

name: Sprint Interval Training (Very Short Sprints)
description: Ultra-short near-maximal sprints (e.g., 10–30 seconds) with long full recovery (often 2–4 minutes)—distinct from longer HIIT; trends in research for time-efficient adaptations when recovery is generous.
instructions: Use a true warm-up with gradual build-ups before first maximal sprint.
If hamstrings feel tight or cold, do not hit maximal acceleration.
Rest until breathing and heart rate recover—sprint quality matters more than session sweat.
Limit total sprints per session; stop at technical breakdown.

name: Zone 2 Cardio Session
description: Sustainable easy aerobic work—Session RPE ~5–6 / talk-test or nasal-breath intensity—to build capillary density and fat oxidation; often ~80% of volume in polarized plans. For most people this overlaps with what coaches call LISS (low-intensity steady state).
instructions: Track heart rate, power, pace, or feel—pick one method and stay consistent.
If you drift into heavy breathing, slow down; Zone 2 is not 'sort of hard.'
Typical duration 30–75+ minutes for dedicated sessions; add time before speed or incline.
Walk, bike, swim, or elliptical all count—consistency beats variety.
Frequency beats occasional monster sessions for aerobic development.
Progress by adding 5–10 minutes per week rather than pushing intensity.
Pair with 1–2 harder sessions per week if following a polarized plan.

name: Hybrid Race Prep — Run + Station Circuits
description: Popularized by hybrid fitness races: repeated run segments (often ~1 km) alternated with functional stations (sled, burpees, rowing, etc.) for race-specific conditioning—without using any trademarked race name as the exercise title.
instructions: Start with shorter run segments and fewer total rounds; build distance before speed.
Practice shoes, fueling, and transitions—races are won or lost on pacing and logistics.
Alternate hard race simulations with easy Zone 2 runs through the week.
Scale station work to full range of motion under fatigue.

name: Circuit Training — Cardio Focus
description: Rotate through several stations with minimal rest between (e.g., 30–60 seconds each) for multiple rounds—still common in boutique studios and general-population HIIT.
instructions: Set up equipment before starting so you can flow station to station.
Use a clock or coach cues; equal work at each station keeps rounds comparable.
Modify impact (step vs jump) to survive multiple rounds.
One to three total rounds is plenty for beginners; add rounds gradually.

name: Knee Push-Up
description: A push-up regression performed from the knees that builds pressing strength with a lighter load.
instructions: Start in a plank position with knees resting on the floor and hands under the shoulders.
Keep a straight line from head to knees with the core braced.
Lower the chest toward the floor by bending the elbows.
Press back up to the start position and repeat.

name: Wall Push-Up
description: A standing push-up against a wall that introduces the pressing pattern with minimal load.
instructions: Stand an arm's length from a wall and place both palms on it at shoulder height.
Keep the body in one straight line from head to heels.
Bend the elbows to bring the chest toward the wall.
Press back to the start position and repeat.

name: Dumbbell Squeeze Press
description: A flat dumbbell press with the dumbbells pressed together throughout, keeping constant inner-chest tension.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding two dumbbells pressed together over the chest with neutral grips.
Squeeze the dumbbells into each other as hard as possible.
Lower the dumbbells to the chest while maintaining the inward squeeze.
Press back to lockout without letting the dumbbells separate and repeat.

name: Wide-Grip Bench Press
description: A barbell bench press with a wider-than-standard grip that shortens the range and biases the chest over the triceps.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench and grip the bar well outside shoulder width.
Unrack the bar and hold it over the chest with arms extended.
Lower the bar to the mid chest keeping the forearms vertical.
Press back to lockout and repeat.

name: Dumbbell Floor Fly
description: A dumbbell fly performed lying on the floor, where the limited range keeps the shoulders safe while training the chest.
instructions: Lie on the floor with knees bent, holding dumbbells above the chest with palms facing in.
Keep a slight bend in the elbows throughout.
Open the arms in a wide arc until the upper arms lightly touch the floor.
Squeeze the chest to bring the dumbbells back together and repeat.

name: Weighted Push-Up
description: A push-up loaded with a plate or weight vest to keep building chest strength beyond bodyweight.
instructions: Have a partner place a plate on the upper back, or wear a weight vest.
Set up in a strong plank with hands under the shoulders.
Lower the chest to just above the floor keeping the body rigid.
Press back to the start position and repeat.

name: Band-Resisted Push-Up
description: A push-up with a resistance band across the back that adds accommodating resistance toward lockout.
instructions: Loop a resistance band across the upper back and anchor an end under each hand.
Set up in a plank with the band taut at the bottom position.
Lower the chest to just above the floor under control.
Press up against the band's growing resistance to full lockout and repeat.

name: Deficit Push-Up
description: A push-up with hands elevated on dumbbells or handles so the chest can travel below hand level for a deeper stretch.
instructions: Place two dumbbells or handles on the floor at shoulder width and grip them in a plank.
Keep the body in one rigid line from head to heels.
Lower the chest below hand level until a deep stretch is felt.
Press back to full extension and repeat.

name: Plyo Push-Up
description: An explosive push-up where the hands leave the floor at the top, building pressing power and rate of force.
instructions: Start in a strong plank with hands under the shoulders.
Lower the chest quickly toward the floor under control.
Drive up explosively so the hands briefly leave the ground.
Land with soft elbows, absorb, and flow into the next rep.

name: One-Arm Push-Up
description: An advanced push-up performed on one arm that demands major pressing strength and full-body tension.
instructions: Set a plank with feet wider than shoulder width and one hand centered under the chest.
Place the free hand behind the back or hip.
Lower the chest toward the floor keeping the hips square.
Press back to full extension and complete all reps before switching arms.

name: Dive Bomber Push-Up
description: A flowing push-up that sweeps the chest low from a pike into an upward arc, training the chest and shoulders through a long range.
instructions: Start in a pike position with hips high and hands shoulder-width apart.
Sweep the chest forward and low between the hands in one smooth arc.
Finish with the chest up and hips near the floor.
Reverse the arc back to the pike position and repeat.

name: TRX Chest Press
description: A suspension-trainer press where body angle sets the load, training the chest with a free range of motion.
instructions: Face away from the anchor holding the handles at chest height with arms extended.
Lean forward into a straight-body plank angle; step back to make it harder.
Lower the chest between the handles by bending the elbows.
Press back to full extension keeping the body rigid and repeat.

name: TRX Chest Fly
description: A suspension-trainer fly that adducts the arms against bodyweight for a deep chest stretch and contraction.
instructions: Face away from the anchor with arms extended forward at chest height, body in a forward lean.
Open the arms wide in an arc while the body lowers as one rigid line.
Keep a slight elbow bend and stop at a comfortable chest stretch.
Squeeze the chest to draw the arms back together and repeat.

name: Kettlebell Floor Press
description: A floor press using kettlebells whose offset load challenges the chest and pressing stability through a shoulder-friendly range.
instructions: Lie on the floor with knees bent, holding a kettlebell in each hand at the chest with wrists straight.
Press the kettlebells up to full lockout over the chest.
Lower under control until the upper arms rest lightly on the floor.
Pause briefly, then press again.

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Floor Press
description: A one-arm kettlebell floor press whose offset load builds pressing strength and side-to-side stability.
instructions: Lie on the floor with knees bent, holding one kettlebell at the chest with the wrist straight.
Press the kettlebell to full lockout over the chest.
Lower under control until the upper arm rests lightly on the floor.
Complete all reps before switching sides.

name: Jumping Pull-Up
description: A pull-up regression using leg drive from the floor to jump into the pull and control the descent.
instructions: Stand below a pull-up bar low enough to reach with a small jump.
Grip the bar, then drive through the legs to jump as you pull your chin over the bar.
Use only as much leg drive as needed to complete the pull.
Lower yourself as slowly as possible, then reset and repeat.

name: One-Arm Pull-Up
description: An elite pull-up performed with one arm, demanding exceptional lat, arm, and grip strength.
instructions: Grip the bar with one hand and hang with the arm fully extended.
Brace the core and keep the free arm by your side or behind your back.
Pull until your chin clears the bar without swinging.
Lower under full control and complete all reps before switching arms.

name: Machine High Row
description: A plate-loaded machine row pulling from high to low that trains the lats through a deep overhead stretch.
instructions: Set the seat so the handles sit overhead at a comfortable reach and load the machine.
Grip the handles with the chest against the pad and arms fully extended.
Pull the handles down and back toward your ribs by driving the elbows to your hips.
Return with control to the overhead stretch and repeat.

name: Front Lever
description: An advanced calisthenics hold keeping the body horizontal under a bar with straight arms.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with straight arms and a tight, hollow body.
Depress the shoulder blades and pull the body up until it is horizontal, face up.
Hold the horizontal line with straight arms, tucking the knees to regress if needed.
Hold for the target time, then lower with control.

name: Kettlebell Pullover
description: A pullover performed lying on the floor with a kettlebell, training the lats through a long overhead arc.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent, holding the kettlebell by the horns above your chest.
With arms slightly bent, lower the bell in an arc overhead toward the floor.
Stop at a comfortable lat stretch before the bell touches down.
Pull the bell back over your chest using the lats and repeat.

name: Ring Row
description: A bodyweight row on gymnastic rings whose difficulty scales with body angle, building the mid-back and grip.
instructions: Set rings to about waist height and grip one in each hand.
Walk your feet forward and hang below the rings with a straight body.
Pull your chest to the rings by driving the elbows back.
Lower under control to full arm extension and repeat.

name: Gorilla Row
description: An alternating kettlebell row from a deep hinge with the bells on the floor, combining a heavy row with hip-hinge endurance.
instructions: Set two kettlebells on the floor between your feet and hinge at the hips with a flat back.
Grip both handles, keeping your weight balanced.
Row one bell to your ribs while pushing the other into the floor.
Lower it, then row the opposite side, alternating while holding the hinge.

name: Bodyweight Squat
description: The foundational unloaded squat that builds leg strength, mobility, and control anywhere.
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and toes slightly out.
Sit your hips down and back while keeping your chest tall.
Lower until your thighs are near parallel or as deep as comfortable.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up.

name: Bodyweight Box Squat
description: A squat down to a box or bench that teaches depth control and builds confidence for newer lifters.
instructions: Stand in front of a box or bench with feet shoulder-width apart.
Sit back slowly until you touch the box with control.
Keep your chest up and avoid dropping onto the surface.
Stand back up by driving through your feet.

name: Dumbbell Squat
description: A squat holding dumbbells at your sides for simple, joint-friendly loading at home or in the gym.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Squat down while keeping your chest tall and arms relaxed.
Keep your whole foot planted as your knees bend.
Stand back up without shrugging the weights.

name: Heels-Elevated Goblet Squat
description: A goblet squat with the heels raised on plates or a wedge to bias the quads through deeper knee bend.
instructions: Set your heels on small plates or a wedge and hold one weight at your chest.
Squat straight down while staying as upright as possible.
Let your knees travel forward to load the quads deeply.
Drive back up through the balls and midfoot.

name: Suspension Trainer Squat
description: A squat holding suspension straps for balance support, ideal for learning depth and control.
instructions: Hold the straps with light tension and stand tall.
Squat down while using the straps only for balance.
Keep your feet flat and chest lifted at the bottom.
Stand back up with as little arm help as possible.

name: Resistance Band Squat
description: A squat standing on a band with the other end racked at the shoulders for simple home resistance.
instructions: Stand on the band with both feet and bring the top over your shoulders.
Squat down under control while the band stays secure.
Keep your chest tall as the tension increases on the way up.
Stand fully upright against the band resistance.

name: Dumbbell Thruster
description: A front squat with dumbbells flowing straight into an overhead press for full-body strength and conditioning.
instructions: Hold dumbbells at your shoulders and squat to full depth.
Drive up hard and use the momentum to press the weights overhead.
Lock out overhead, then lower back to your shoulders.
Keep your heels down and trunk braced throughout.

name: Cable Glute Kickback
description: A standing cable hip extension using an ankle strap to isolate the glutes through a controlled kick back.
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable and face the machine.
Hold the frame lightly and soften the standing knee.
Kick the working leg back by squeezing the glute, without arching your lower back.
Return under control and finish the set before switching sides.

name: Machine Glute Kickback
description: A guided hip extension on a kickback or multi-hip machine that loads the glutes through a fixed path.
instructions: Set the pad or platform against the working leg and hold the handles.
Brace your trunk and keep your hips square.
Drive the leg back by extending the hip fully.
Return slowly to the start and repeat on the same side.

name: Kas Glute Bridge
description: A short-range, constant-tension hip thrust variation that keeps the glutes loaded without momentum.
instructions: Set up like a barbell hip thrust with your upper back on a bench.
Start from the locked-out top position with glutes squeezed.
Lower your hips only a few inches, keeping constant tension.
Drive back to lockout slowly without bouncing or losing position.

name: Assisted Nordic Hamstring Curl
description: A band-assisted Nordic curl that makes eccentric hamstring training accessible before the full movement.
instructions: Anchor a band high in front of you and hold it at your chest while kneeling with ankles secured.
Keep your hips extended and your body in one line.
Lower forward slowly while the band takes part of your weight.
Pull back up with your hamstrings, using the band only as needed.

name: Tibialis Raise
description: A wall-supported raise of the toes and forefeet that strengthens the muscles along the front of the shin.
instructions: Lean your back against a wall with your heels about a foot from it.
Keep your legs straight and your hips against the wall.
Raise your toes and forefeet as high as you can toward your shins.
Lower under control and repeat.

name: Heel Walk
description: A bodyweight walk performed on the heels to build endurance in the front of the shins.
instructions: Lift the balls of your feet so you are standing on your heels.
Keep your toes pulled up toward your shins.
Walk forward with short controlled steps.
Stay tall and continue for distance or time.

name: Incline Pike Push-Up
description: A pike push-up with the hands elevated to reduce the load, making the vertical pressing pattern accessible.
instructions: Place your hands on a bench or sturdy surface and walk your feet in.
Lift your hips high into a pike position.
Lower the top of your head toward the surface between your hands.
Press back up under control and repeat.

name: Kettlebell Push Press
description: An explosive kettlebell press that uses leg drive to send the bell overhead, building shoulder power.
instructions: Rack the kettlebell at your shoulder with a braced trunk.
Dip slightly at the knees, keeping your torso upright.
Drive through your legs and press the bell overhead in one motion.
Lower it back to the rack position under control and repeat.

name: Weighted Plank
description: A front plank with a plate on the back that raises the bracing demand without changing the position.
instructions: Set up in a forearm plank and have a partner place a plate on your upper back.
Brace hard and keep your hips level.
Hold the position without sagging or hiking.
Remove the plate carefully before lowering down.

name: Plank Up-Down
description: A plank where you move from forearms to hands one arm at a time, training the trunk to resist rotation.
instructions: Start in a forearm plank with your feet slightly wide.
Press up onto one hand, then the other, reaching a high plank.
Lower back to your forearms one arm at a time.
Keep your hips as still as possible and alternate the leading arm.
